rows.title: Basic characteristics of the Indian economy; features of a developing economy
sub: Group-II M2-A-1: Structure of the Indian economy - basic characteristics and sectoral composition

secs.t: Types of economies → defining feature

x: Exam angle: statements matching a feature (regulation through taxes/credit, coexistence of sectors) to the correct label.
Underdeveloped economies are characterised by low per capita income, low capital formation, agricultural predominance and disguised unemployment, not high and uniformly distributed income.

Mixed economy matches public-private coexistence; developing economy matches the infrastructure precondition; underdeveloped economy matches its structural deficiencies; dual economy matches the coexistence of modern and traditional sectors.

secs.t: Economists → contributions

x: Lewis's dual-sector model describes surplus labour moving from
the subsistence sector to the modern sector

secs.t: Terms → meaning

x: India's middle path retained State control over the commanding heights, particularly
heavy industry, infrastructure and finance
, while permitting a regulated private sector in consumer goods.
Disguised unemployment
exists when surplus workers are employed and the marginal productivity of labour is zero.
The public sector comprises general government and public corporations owned or run by the government.

secs.t: India at Independence → features and causes of underdevelopment

x: Colonial deindustrialisation converted the textile exporter into a raw-material supplier and captive market.
All four statements correctly describe recorded causes of underdevelopment: inadequate savings, population pressure, disguised unemployment and weak human capital indicators.
Ragnar Nurkse's vicious circle is low income leading to low saving, low investment and low productivity, which in turn leads back to low income.

secs.t: Sectors by activity → classification

x: Exam angle: match codes asked in G1 2022 and 2023 - Trade = Service, Water supply = Industrial, Fisheries = Primary, GDP = CSO; "tertiary sector is also called service sector"; transport is tertiary, not mining/fishing/cement.
Mining and quarrying are primary activities in the activity-based classification but may be counted within the broad Industry sector in the three-sector presentation.

secs.t: Data → sectoral shares, dual economy and demography — Sectoral composition: GDP share vs employment share

x: Exam angle: Assertion-Reason on "structural change in the composition of national income" - both true, R explains A.
tertiary sector
accounted for 52.9 per cent, compared with 21.4 per cent for the primary sector and 25.8 per cent for the secondary sector.
Changes in sectoral output shares, alongside the continuing concentration of employment in agriculture, demonstrate structural change in the economy.

secs.t: Data → sectoral shares, dual economy and demography — Private investment
Data → sectoral shares, dual economy and demography — Dual economy: organised vs unorganised, rural vs urban

x: Rural work was dominated by agriculture at 57.7% and self-employment at 62.8%.
Higher work participation in these States is associated with subsistence work and the need for manual labour, especially in rural activities.
Per capita income differences, poverty ratios and variations in sectoral composition are all indicators of regional imbalance.

secs.t: Data → sectoral shares, dual economy and demography — Demography

x: A TFR of 1.9 is
below the replacement level of 2.1
, indicating that fertility has fallen below the level required for long-term population replacement.
Median age rose from 24 in 2011 to about 29 and is projected to reach 36 by 2036.
Census 2011 recorded India's population at
121.09 crore
, with females at 48.46% and a sex ratio of 940.

secs.t: India's world standing → GDP rank and income class

x: Exam angle: nominal vs PPP rank; which method and which variable (GNI, not GDP) the World Bank uses.
India's 2026 per capita GDP ranking was stated as 149th in nominal terms, at USD 2,813, and 119th in PPP terms, at USD 12,964.
India is projected to become an upper-middle-income country by 2030; India is currently classed as lower-middle income (per capita income USD 2,760, July 2026), so it is not high income.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh economy profile → data vs India

x: Services contributed 43% of Andhra Pradesh's current-price GVA in 2025-26, followed by agriculture and allied activities at 33% and industry at 24%.
Per capita GSDP is a gross measure, whereas per capita income is calculated as NSDP divided by population.
All three figures are reported Andhra Pradesh indicators: 11.3 per cent GSDP growth over 2024-26, per capita income of Rs 2,94,507 in 2025-26, and projected per capita GSDP of Rs 2,98,058.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The cited criticism highlights the coexistence of a large GDP with an HDI rank of 130, indicating that economic size does not automatically ensure equivalent human development.
The inter-State Gini coefficient rose from 0.230 in 1994-95 to
in 2025-26, indicating increased inequality between States.
The term “
premature leapfrogging
” describes the expansion of services without a sufficiently strong intervening industrial phase.

rows.title: Structural change - sectoral composition of output and employment; the missing manufacturing transition
sub: Group-II M2-A-6: Sectoral distribution of income in India - shares of agriculture, industry and services

secs.t: Sector classification → other name, activities and compiling bodies

x: GDP and sectoral GVA are compiled by the NSO; State GSDP and sectoral GVA by the State DES; and ASI and ASUSE manufacturing components by the NSO.
Mining and quarrying are grouped under the primary sector, water supply under the secondary or industrial sector, and transport and storage under the tertiary sector.

secs.t: Economists and models → prediction

x: The Clark-Fisher model predicts a transition from the primary sector to the secondary sector and then to the tertiary sector as income rises.
The Lewis turning point is when the surplus farm labour is exhausted, after which wages start rising.
The Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister stated that services-led growth cannot be sustained without a manufacturing base.

secs.t: Data → sectoral share of GVA over time (old series)

x: Agriculture
was the largest contributor to India's GDP at Independence, accounting for approximately 50 percent.
The 2017-18 PYQ key puts agriculture at about 17% (later revised to 18.3%) and services at 54.4%, with industry at 29.2%.
In 1950-51 industry contributed only about
of GDP (GS 2023), while agriculture was the largest contributor at over half.

secs.t: Data → GVA by sub-sector and the new GDP series (base 2022-23)

x: Exam angle: the 2024-25 "primary" share (21.4%) includes mining, so it is not directly comparable with the old "agriculture, forestry & fishing" share.
Allied sectors such as livestock and fisheries grow at about
5-6 per cent
a year, which is why their GVA share rises while that of crops falls.
Manufacturing GVA was estimated at Rs 38.6 lakh crore, equivalent to
14.7 percent
of GDP in 2023-24 under the new NAS.

secs.t: Data → share of employment vs share of output

x: In 2021-22, the Primary sector accounted for 21.82% of GDP and 43.96% of the workforce.
A structural change in the composition of national income has occurred, reflected in the changing relative importance of the primary, secondary and tertiary sectors.
Manufacturing employed approximately 11.4% of workers in 2023-24, comprising 1.9 crore organised and 3.3 crore unorganised workers.

secs.t: Data → sectoral growth rates

x: Agricultural growth was 2.5 percent in the 9th Plan, 2.4 percent in the 10th Plan and 3.6 percent in the
11th Plan
The services sector recorded 8.3% growth in 2024-25, 8.9% in 2025-26, and 10% in Q1 2026-27.
The chronological sequence is 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 and Q1 2026-27, giving
B, D, A, C

secs.t: Terms and debates → the missing manufacturing stage

x: The Economic Survey explains that the decline in manufacturing's nominal share reflects
a relative-price effect
; in real terms, it remains stable at 17-18 percent.
Agriculture recorded real growth of
in 2025-26 according to the sectoral growth table. ⚠ Sources differ: SAE: agriculture 2.5% in 2025-26 (FY25 4.3%); MoSPI Provisional Estimates (Jun 2026): 4.2% (FY25) to 3.0% (FY26).

secs.t: AP sectoral composition of GSVA vs India

x: Public administration grew slowest (0.05%); communications grew fastest within services (15.13%).
Andhra Pradesh is moving from farming towards services without passing through a strong manufacturing stage, a pattern described as a missing manufacturing transition.
The cited Group-II 2017 key used the split of
31.77% agriculture, 22.23% industry and 46.0% services

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Agricultural growth slowed from 4.2% to approximately 3.0% in 2025-26. ⚠ Sources differ: SAE: agriculture 2.5% in 2025-26 (FY25 4.3%); MoSPI Provisional Estimates (Jun 2026): 4.2% (FY25) to 3.0% (FY26).
MSMEs are the second-largest employer after
agriculture
The principal drivers identified were real estate, IT, and trade-hotels.

rows.title: Services sector - growth, composition and contribution to GDP and employment
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I C-2

secs.t: Services → definition, types and constitutional lists

x: Trade, hotels and restaurants, public administration and defence are tertiary activities, while manufacturing, construction and utilities are secondary.
Mining and quarrying
is not one of the eight service sub-sectors.
All three statements correctly represent the stated constitutional distribution of selected service-related subjects.
International bodies such as the WTO use
the United Nations Central Product Classification
, or UNCPC, for services.

secs.t: Data → services share in GVA, growth and employment

x: Exam angle: services' contribution to GDP is "more than 50%"; to employment "about a third".
Services produce
more than 50%
of India's GVA according to the Economic Survey 2025-26.
The First Advance Estimates placed services-sector growth at
The tertiary sector accounted for 53.89% of GDP, while the primary sector employed 43.96% of the workforce.

secs.t: Issues and debates → mismatch and service-led growth

x: Manufacturing employed about 72 million persons, while services are characterised as a high-growth, low-volatility anchor growing at roughly 7–8% annually.

Both statements are true, and the manufacturing sector's linkages with logistics, IT and finance, together with its stabilising effect on GDP cycles, explain why it is considered necessary for sustainable service-led growth.

secs.t: Terms and indices → meaning

x: The ISP is a fixed-weight Laspeyres volume index with weights based on GVA.
The ISP draws data from
GST returns and administrative records
A GCC is an offshore unit set up by a multinational to undertake its own core work, unlike a third-party vendor.
Mode 2 is consumption abroad, illustrated by a person travelling overseas for medical treatment.

secs.t: Data → services trade and GCCs

x: NASSCOM reported 1,760 GCCs employing about 19 lakh persons in FY2025.
The number of GCCs has risen to over 1,800, and their foreign-exchange-generating activities help cushion the merchandise trade deficit.
India is described as the world's
7th-largest
services exporter with a 4.3% share; WTO data (April 2025) rank it 8th with the same share, so quote the source.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Banking
led the services sector in Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25 with a contribution of 14.25%.
All three statements are correct for 2025-26: services GVA was Rs 3,59,931 crore, growth was 10.67%, and communications grew fastest at 15.13%.
Karnataka, along with Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Telangana, produces about 40% of India's services output; 58.7% is the figure associated with Bihar's GSVA share from services.

rows.title: Role of the IT and ITES industry in India's development - exports, employment and challenges
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I C-2

secs.t: Policies and institutions → year and role

x: The Software Export Scheme of 1972 permitted computers to be imported against an export obligation.
The Computer Policy was introduced in 1984 and the Software Export Policy in 1986; the two policies liberalised imports and data links.
The six goals were e-Government, e-Industry, e-Innovation/R&D, e-Learning, e-Security and e-Inclusion.
e-Agriculture pricing
was not among them.

secs.t: Data → IT-BPM revenue, exports and jobs

x: Software exports grew by about
50 percent
annually after 1995–96, aided by low costs and international quality standards.
Software and computer services are India's largest services export and services forex earner, helping offset the merchandise trade deficit in the balance of payments.
NASSCOM estimated about
58 lakh
, or 5.8 million, direct jobs in the IT-BPM industry in FY2025.

secs.t: Firms, hubs and destinations → place

x: India's IT-BPM exports mainly go to the
USA and Europe
, making the sector sensitive to their visa regimes and client spending cycles.
Coimbatore, Indore, Jaipur and Bhubaneswar
are identified as emerging Tier-2/Tier-3 centres.
The IT Park at Madhurawada (Rushikonda), Visakhapatnam, is an Andhra Pradesh example under the
AP IT & GCC Policy 4.0

secs.t: Challenges → factor and effect

x: High-end services can record rapid GVA growth but limited employment generation because they are skill-intensive and automated.
Visa rules, protectionism and client spending cycles are all external factors affecting the IT-BPM industry.
Routine ITES/BPM work
is identified as the segment most exposed to automation and generative AI.
GERD is reported at approximately
0.64–0.7 percent of GDP
in the context of shortages of frontier-AI and chip-design talent.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The industry contributes to foreign-exchange earnings, formal employment and services-led growth.
The recent demand for AI-related roles has been led by the banking, financial services and insurance sector and the telecom sector.
The
Department of Electronics
was the first to spot the opportunity for software exports in India.
STPI, established in 1991, represented
India’s first export-park model for software

rows.title: Other services - tourism, banking, insurance, health and education services
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I C-2

secs.t: Acts, committees and regulators → year and provision

x: Banks may undertake insurance business
as a corporate agent or through a joint venture
, subject to the applicable regulatory approval.
Equipment leasing, factoring and mutual-fund business are all among the para-banking activities that banks may undertake with RBI approval.
The
Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025
, passed by Parliament on 17 December 2025, raised the FDI cap from 74% to 100%.

secs.t: Insurance terms and products → meaning

x: Insurance premium income was Rs 11.9 lakh crore in FY25, and health insurance overtook motor insurance as the leading non-life business.
The sovereign-backed P&I cover was launched under the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool, designed by New India Assurance, issued first to SCI and provided indemnity up to USD 1.5 billion.

secs.t: Health and education services → data and schemes

x: PM-JAY and State schemes together cover about 80 per cent of citizens, but only about 35 per cent of those insured used the benefit.
PM-JAY was launched in 2018 with coverage of Rs 5 lakh per family, and insurance coverage has roughly tripled since its launch.
Rajiv Aarogyasri was launched as a cashless health insurance scheme for families below the poverty line and operated through a State trust.

secs.t: Transport, postal and telecom → FIRSTs and dates

x: UDAN means Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik, was launched in 2016, and its first flight was the Shimla-Delhi service in April 2017.
The correct order is
A, C, B, D
: BSNL was corporatised on 1 October 2000, the first UDAN flight (Shimla-Delhi) flew in April 2017, India Post Payments Bank was launched in 2018, and 5G services began on 1 October 2022.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: More than 40 crore Indians were reported to be in a healthcare gap, while public health spending was reported at 1.43% of GDP.
The bank credit-deposit ratio reached
in the first quarter of FY27, described as a 62-year high.
Andhra Pradesh services were reported to be growing at 10.67%, with banking and insurance growing at 13.59%.

rows.title: Occupational structure of India - trends and inter-state variation
sub: Group-II M2-A-5: Occupational pattern in India - trends, structural retardation and informality

secs.t: Occupational structure — definitions, terms and FIRSTs — Definitions and theory

x: Occupational structure is the distribution of the workforce across primary, secondary and tertiary activities.
The occupational structure changed much more slowly than the output structure, so statement 3 reverses the relationship.

secs.t: Occupational structure — definitions, terms and FIRSTs — Terms → meaning

x: The unorganised sector consists largely of small and scattered units outside effective government control, taxation and monitoring.
NCEUS defined the unorganised sector as unincorporated private enterprises owned by individuals or households, on a proprietary or partnership basis, with fewer than 10 workers.
The Code on Social Security, 2020 includes home-based, self-employed and wage workers in the unorganised sector within the category of unorganised workers.

secs.t: Occupational structure — definitions, terms and FIRSTs — FIRSTs

x: Census 2011 was the 15th Census conducted since 1872 and the 7th Census conducted after Independence.
The 2027 Census is described as the first
app-based digital Census

secs.t: Data — sector shares of the workforce since 1951

x: Agriculture
has remained the sector with the highest employment share, although its share has declined over time.
The 2021-22 workforce shares were primary 43.96%, secondary 22.24% and tertiary 33.80%.
The NSSO 70th round reported that
of rural households were agricultural households.

secs.t: Data — cultivators, labourers, rural and women workers — Cultivators vs agricultural labourers (Census 2001 → 2011)

x: Exam angle: direction of change of cultivators vs labourers.
Cultivators declined from 127.3 million to 118.8 million, while agricultural labourers increased from 106.8 million to 144.3 million.
Fragmentation reduced the average holding size and increased the relative importance of small and marginal farmers, contributing to the decline in cultivators.
Average holding size fell from 2.28 ha (1971) to 1.08 ha (2015-16).

secs.t: Data — cultivators, labourers, rural and women workers — Women in the workforce

x: The low share of operational holdings held by women, alongside their agricultural work, is associated with the
feminisation of agriculture
The regular wage or salaried share rose from 22% to 24%, whereas self-employment declined from 58% to 56%.
Women's earnings were 76% of men's wages in salaried work, 69% in casual work and 36% in self-employment.

secs.t: Committees, codes and surveys on informal employment

x: PLFS 2022-23 placed the informal share of non-farm jobs at about
78 per cent
Arjun Sengupta
was the chairman of the NCEUS.
The NSS 73rd Round estimated employment of about
11 crore people
in unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises.
The continuing survey series is the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises, or ASUSE, under the NSS framework.

secs.t: Unemployment types → sector where predominant

x: Disguised unemployment is predominant in
agriculture
, where surplus workers may have marginal productivity close to zero.
Seasonal unemployment is characteristic of agriculture because work is available mainly during sowing and harvesting seasons.
Structural unemployment
results from a mismatch between available skills and job requirements caused by technology or broader structural change.

secs.t: Changes and issues — slow shift out of agriculture and jobless growth

x: Population pressure on land
helped keep a large workforce dependent on agriculture, so its employment share declined only marginally during the Plan era.
Jobless growth denotes GDP or output growth that is not matched by adequate employment growth, especially growth in formal and quality jobs.
In
the late 1990s
, employment growth fell to early-plan levels even while GDP continued to grow.

secs.t: Places — inter-state variation and Andhra Pradesh — Inter-state variation

x: Urbanised Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry
have high shares of other workers, including service-sector workers.

AP had a lower cultivator share, 14.5 per cent against 24.7 per cent; a higher all-agriculture share, 62.4 per cent against 54.6 per cent; and a lower other-worker share, 34.8 per cent against 41.6 per cent.

secs.t: Places — inter-state variation and Andhra Pradesh — AP today (PLFS 2023-24; AP SES 2025-26)

x: For AP in 2023–24, LFPR was 47.5 per cent, WPR was 45.6 per cent and unemployment was 4.1 per cent.
Andhra Pradesh recorded an LFPR of 47.5%, comprising 59.5% for males and 35.8% for females.
In Andhra Pradesh, agriculture accounted for 45.6%, services 31.6%, and manufacturing and industry 22.8% of employment.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The United Nations declared 2026 the International Year of the
Woman Farmer
A fall in unemployment may also reflect distress entry into low-productivity work.

rows.title: Economic development since independence - phases and growth rates; the Hindu rate of growth

secs.t: Persons → statements on India's growth

x: Dani Rodrik and Arvind Subramanian
argued in 2004 that the growth transition began around 1980 with a pro-business attitudinal shift.
J. Bradford DeLong argued in 2003 that India’s economic take-off occurred in the 1980s, before the 1991 reforms.
Job-poor growth and youth unemployment of approximately 10 per cent are identified as important criticisms.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: Hindu rate of growth and ICOR

x: A lower ICOR means that less additional capital is required to generate one additional unit of output, indicating greater investment efficiency.
Although investment increased from 7% to 11%, capital-intensive industries with long gestation periods resulted in a high ICOR and relatively low growth.
Since g = s/k, a higher capital-output ratio reduces growth when the savings rate remains unchanged.

secs.t: Policies, plans and the licence regime, 1944-1991

x: The major policy orientation was import substitution supported by state planning and public investment, rather than export promotion or deregulation.
The Bombay Plan of 1944 was prepared by industrialists who themselves sought state protection, making the Licence Raj partly a capitalist demand.
The 1980s saw a pro-business, not pro-market orientation, including broad-banding of licences, tax cuts, NRI deposits and a higher MRTP limit.

secs.t: Chronology of economic milestones and crises, 1962-2021

x: Exam angle: arrange these events chronologically.
Rupee devaluation occurred in June 1966, the Green Revolution began in the mid-1960s, bank nationalisation took place in July 1969, and ‘Garibi Hatao’ was launched in 1971.
The wars of 1962 and 1965, along with severe droughts in 1965–66, contributed to the failure of the Third Plan and the Plan Holiday of 1966–69.

secs.t: Data — phases of development and average growth

x: The average growth rate during 1980–81 to 1989–90 was in the range of 5.13 to 5.18 per cent.
Post-reform growth averaged approximately 6.5 per cent, was 6.8 per cent from 1993–94, and peaked at 8.5 per cent during 2003–08.
The figures are 7.2 per cent for 2023–24, 7.1 per cent for 2024–25 and 7.7 per cent as the 2025–26 projection.

secs.t: Debates — 1980s acceleration vs 1991 as turning point

x: The 1980s growth phase is viewed as debt-fuelled and unstable, and it ended in
the 1991 economic crisis

rows.title: Economic planning in India - origins, Planning Commission, National Development Council

secs.t: Pre-independence plans → year and person

x: The Congress National Planning Committee was initiated by Subhas Chandra Bose, chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru, and its final report appeared in 1949.
The Bombay Plan was prepared by eight industrialists, including J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla and Kasturbhai Lalbhai, and sought state-led industrialisation and protection.
The
Gandhian Plan
, prepared by Shriman Narayan Agarwal in 1944, emphasised decentralised and self-contained villages.

secs.t: Persons → roles in planning bodies

x: Gulzarilal Nanda was the first and M.S. Ahluwalia the last Deputy Chairman.

secs.t: Constitution, Articles and committees on planning

x: The
Balwantrai Mehta Committee
recommended in 1957 that planning and development should be entrusted to Panchayati Raj Institutions.
The Thungon Sub-Committee identified the
Zila Parishad
as the planning pivot at the district level.
The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments provide the institutional framework for rural and urban local self-government, including decentralised planning mechanisms.

x: The Council approved draft Five-Year Plans, linked the Planning Commission with the States and was intended to meet at least twice a year.
The National Planning Council constituted in 1965 was
an expert advisory body attached to the Planning Commission
A formal resolution abolishing the National Development Council remains pending; replacement of the Planning Commission did not itself complete that formal abolition.

x: The Planning Commission assessed resources and prepared the draft plan; the Finance Ministry handled budgetary allocation, while the National Development Council approved the draft as the apex approving body.
The
National Development Council
prescribed guidelines for formulation of the national plan, including assessment of the resources required, and approved the draft plan.

The common-plan idea encouraged centralisation and became a continuing source of
Centre-State tension

Swarna Andhra @2047 monitoring covers 651 key performance indicators across 30 Secretariat departments.
Andhra Pradesh introduced district-level decentralised planning during the Sixth Plan (1980–85), allocating Rs 1 crore to each of its 23 districts and setting up District Planning Councils.

x: NITI Aayog is described as a think tank that promotes bottom-up planning and cooperative federalism; it is not primarily a fund allocator.
The training supports
decentralised Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans under the new rural employment law
Zonal Councils
are statutory bodies.

rows.title: Objectives of Indian planning; types of planning (imperative, indicative, perspective, rolling)
sub: Group-II M2-A-9: Strategy of planning in India - objectives, models and the plan approach

secs.t: Planning Commission and NDC — set-up, composition, functions — Planning Commission vs NDC

x: Gulzarilal Nanda
was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission; M.S. Ahluwalia was its last Deputy Chairman.
The Planning Commission was modelled on the
Soviet Gosplan
planning organisation.
The Planning Commission was created by
an executive resolution
and was neither a constitutional nor a statutory body.
The Planning Commission was set up on 15 March 1950, but the NDC came in 1952.

secs.t: Planning Commission and NDC — set-up, composition, functions — Planning Commission - resolution year, composition, functions

x: Exam angle: "body set up after Independence for a common plan" = Planning Commission.
The Deputy Chairman was the de facto head of the Planning Commission, held Cabinet-minister rank and attended Cabinet meetings without a vote.
All four were functions of the Planning Commission: resource assessment, plan formulation, priority-setting, resource allocation, progress appraisal and planning grants to States.
NITI Aayog emphasises bottom-up planning and cooperative federalism and functions primarily as a think tank, not as a fund allocator.

secs.t: Objectives of planning — chief vs subsidiary

x: The socialistic pattern of society was adopted at the Avadi Congress in 1955 and was subsequently reflected in the Second Plan and the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956.
The declared aim combined a rapid rise in living standards with efficient resource use and increased production and employment opportunities for all.

secs.t: Plans → thrust, strategy and programmes

x: The First Plan focused on agriculture, irrigation and power; the Second on rapid industrialisation; the Third on self-reliance and food self-sufficiency; and the Fifth on poverty removal and self-reliance.
The First to Third Plans followed the
trickle-down approach
, assuming that the benefits of growth would reach poorer sections.
The Sixth Plan, covering 1980–85, placed removal of poverty foremost and included IRDP, NREP and RLEGP among its programmes.

secs.t: Plan financing — domestic savings, deficit financing, foreign aid

x: Foreign aid was one of the three sources, along with domestic savings and deficit financing (the Fourth Plan aimed to reduce dependence on it).
The Harrod-Domar framework links growth to
the savings rate and the capital-output ratio

secs.t: Types of planning — terms → meaning — Imperative vs indicative

x: Imperative planning uses binding quotas and allocation, whereas indicative planning guides the private sector.
The USSR under Stalin, beginning with the 1928 planning experience, and China are examples associated with imperative planning.
India shifted to indicative planning from the Eighth Plan, covering 1992–97, following the economic reforms of 1991.

secs.t: Types of planning — terms → meaning — Other planning dichotomies

x: Article 243ZD deals with the District Planning Committee and Article 243ZE with the Metropolitan Planning Committee.
Planning by inducement works through prices, taxes and subsidies (planning by direction uses commands and controls).

India displayed imperative features in the early public sector, moved towards indicative planning and inducement after 1991, and Kerala's People's Plan Campaign is an example of decentralised planning.

secs.t: Types of planning — terms → meaning — Perspective planning

x: Perspective planning covers a long period of 15–20 years or more.
Perspective planning was a function of the
Planning Commission
in India.
A long-term perspective plan for 1985–2000 accompanied
the Seventh Plan
Lack of a sufficiently developed perspective has been cited as a standard criticism of Indian planning.

secs.t: Rolling plan — Myrdal, Janata government, 1978-80

x: Under a rolling plan, the plan is revised annually and extended forward by one year.
The rolling plan stressed
employment
in contrast to the emphasis associated with the Nehru model.
Frequent yearly revision was criticised because it weakened commitment to the originally stated targets.
Gunnar Myrdal suggested the rolling plan for developing countries.

secs.t: Multi-level planning — levels, committees and AP economic regions

x: Multi-level planning operates through NITI Aayog at the Centre, Planning Boards in the States, DPCs at the district level, and block or mandal bodies with Gram Panchayats through GPDPs.

The Small Farmers Development Agency (SFDA), Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP), Integrated Tribal Development Programme (ITDP) and Intensive Agricultural District Programme (IADP) operated outside the panchayat framework.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Indian planning was criticised for lacking a sufficiently long-term perspective and for becoming centralised.
NITI Aayog lacks financial powers and represents a shift towards cooperative and competitive federalism rather than centralised plan-grant allocation.
The new rural employment law is stated to operate on the basis of the
Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan
Kerala’s People’s Plan Campaign devolved
35–40 per cent
of the plan outlay to local bodies.

rows.title: Plan models - Harrod-Domar, Mahalanobis, wage-goods (Vakil-Brahmananda), Gandhian and Bombay plans

secs.t: Persons → plans, models and ideas

x: The Harrod-Domar model was developed independently by
Roy Harrod and Evsey Domar
The First Plan was based on the
Harrod-Domar model
, in which growth depends on the savings rate and the capital-output ratio (g = s/k) and the bottleneck is limited aggregate savings.
Vakil and Brahmananda put forward the wage-goods model in their 1956 work,
Planning for an Expanding Economy

secs.t: Non-official plans and books → authors

x: The Bombay Plan favoured a significant State role, public sector development and protection of infant industries; it did not advocate
a completely non-interventionist State
The Gandhian Plan emphasised agriculture, cottage and village industries, decentralisation, Swadeshi, Sarvodaya and Trusteeship.
The Sarvodaya Plan of 1950 was associated with Jayaprakash Narayan and drew upon Vinoba’s Sarvodaya concept.

secs.t: Harrod-Domar model — terms and equation

x: The answer is
Harrod-Domar
The model states that growth depends positively on the savings rate and negatively on the capital-output ratio.
The model links increased investment with higher output and employment through the
multiplier effect

secs.t: Mahalanobis model — strategy, sectors, omissions, outcome

x: Consumer goods were largely left to the
small and cottage sector
, while the public sector concentrated on basic and heavy industries.
The model assumed that building machines domestically would eventually enable India to become self-sufficient in producing consumer goods.
The strategy’s neglect of agriculture contributed to food shortages, shortages of essential goods and high inflation by the late 1950s.

secs.t: P.C. Mahalanobis → institutions, honours and FIRSTs

x: Mahalanobis chaired the National Income Committee, whose recommendation led to the National Sample Survey; its first round was held in 1950–51.
Mahalanobis helped create the NSSO and CSO, founded the journal Sankhya and devised the Mahalanobis distance.
National Statistics Day is observed on 29 June, the birth anniversary of
P.C. Mahalanobis
, since 2007.

secs.t: Alternatives to Mahalanobis — wage-goods model and the Janata strategy

x: A larger supply of wage goods makes it possible to support and employ disguised unemployed labour in productive activities.
The Janata Government ended the Fifth Plan in 1978, adopted a Rolling Plan for 1978–80, and followed a concept advocated by Gunnar Myrdal.
The Janata strategy emphasised agriculture, rural development, employment, small and cottage industries, and minimum needs rather than heavy industry.

secs.t: Plan → model it was based on, with distractor models

x: The Allen S. Manne and Ashok Rudra model was associated with the Fourth Five-Year Plan, 1969–74.
The Third Five Year Plan, also known as the Gadgil Yojana, was associated with the John Sandy and S. Chakravarthy growth model and followed an import substitution strategy.
The Feldman-Mahalanobis model focused on the scarcity of capital goods, while the Harrod-Domar model stressed limited aggregate savings.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Harrod–Domar model focused on savings, the Mahalanobis model on capital goods, and the wage-goods model on food.
The Bill proposes to make the Institute a statutory body corporate, provide for an 11-member Board of Governors, and designate the President as Visitor.
The Soviet Union under Stalin began five-year plans in 1928 and followed imperative planning, whereas India follows indicative planning.

secs.t: Plans I to XII → period, model, main objective — Plan → period, model, tagline

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2024 asked the prime objectives of the Third ("make the economy independent"), Sixth ("poverty eradication and technological self-reliance") and Ninth ("growth with justice and equity") Plans.
Exam angle: "prime objective of the Nth plan" and "rolling plan period" are asked almost every year.
Human resource development was the principal objective of the Eighth Plan, whereas the Tenth Plan targeted 8 per cent GDP growth and doubling of per capita income in ten years.

The Third Plan (1961-66) aimed at a self-reliant and self-generating economy ('make the economy independent'); the Fourth (1969-74) at growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance; the Sixth (1980-85) at poverty eradication and technological self-reliance; and the Eighth (1992-97) at human resource development.

secs.t: Plans I to XII → period, model, main objective — Plans cut short or terminated early
Plan → focus sector, FIRSTs and programmes introduced

x: The
Sixth Plan
was the first plan to focus on gender issues and inter-State and intra-State inequalities.
The
Eighth Plan
placed human development at the core and shifted emphasis from heavy industry to infrastructure.
The Eighth Plan’s public outlay was financed mainly by deficit financing, while its developmental emphasis moved towards human development and infrastructure.
The Eleventh Plan placed the
social sector
first, with education at the top of its priorities.

secs.t: Second Plan — outlay data and criticism of the Nehru-Mahalanobis strategy

x: The outlay was pruned because of food and capital shortages, inflation, unrealistic closed-economy assumptions and the 1957–58 foreign-exchange crisis.
The strategy was criticised for neglecting agriculture, generating food shortages and inflation, and relying on capital-intensive heavy industry that created few jobs.

secs.t: Eleventh and Twelfth Plans — strategy and monitorable targets

x: The Eleventh Plan envisaged continued reform and a competitive private sector; it did not propose its complete withdrawal.
The Eleventh Plan set 27 national monitorable targets, including 13 targets at the State level.
The Eleventh Plan targeted 9 per cent GDP growth, 4 per cent agricultural growth, an IMR of 28 and a TFR of 2.1.
The Eleventh Plan was titled “Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth”, while the Twelfth Plan emphasised “Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth”.

secs.t: Data — plan-wise growth, target vs achieved

x: The
Eleventh Five Year Plan
recorded the highest GDP growth, with actual growth of about 8 per cent.
The
First, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh and Eighth
Plans achieved growth above their respective targets.
The Twelfth Plan had a 9 per cent target in the Approach Paper, but the final target was fixed at
8 per cent

secs.t: Data — GDP growth record, highest and lowest years

x: Growth in 1990–91 was 1.1%; it fell below 1% during the crisis year 1991–92.
GDP grew about 3.6% in 1950-51.
1979 recorded the lowest growth since 1961, about -5.2%, owing to drought and the second oil shock.
Of these periods,
had the highest average growth.

secs.t: Achievements vs failures of planning

x: Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela steel plants, along with Chittaranjan, Perambur and the IITs, formed part of the industrial and scientific base created during planning.
The
Atomic Energy Commission
contributed to scientific and technological capacity, not directly to food self-sufficiency.
The expression was used to describe persistent poverty and inequality under the Eighth Plan despite the existence of a safety net.

x: The Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana was launched by the Centre in 2007, with ₹1,862 crore allotted.
Jalayagnam was an irrigation mission launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2004 for completing major and medium irrigation projects.
Population received 60 percent, per capita income 25 percent, and fiscal performance and special problems received 7.5 percent each.
Special Category States received assistance in the ratio of 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Five Year Plan system ended in 2017, but plan-style credit planning and regional planning continue through other institutions and frameworks.
The NABARD Andhra Pradesh State Focus Paper 2026–27 proposed a credit plan of
₹5.11 lakh crore
, up from ₹4.24 lakh crore.
Kerala continues to prepare Annual Plans, and its Gender Budget accounts for more than one-fifth of plan outlay.

secs.t: Third and Fourth Plans — targets, failures and the Plan Holiday

x: The Third Plan grew only 2.2% against a 5.6% target; it was derailed by the 1962 and 1965 wars and the 1965-66 droughts; and three Annual Plans (Plan Holiday, 1966-69) followed before the Fourth Plan.
The Fourth Plan followed the Gadgil strategy, which emphasised growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance.

secs.t: Changes — directed to indicative planning and end of the plan era

x: After 1991, planning became indicative: it signalled priority sectors while private investment played a larger role.
Indicative planning
uses guidelines, goals and signals to influence private-sector decisions instead of imposing binding quotas.
The Planning Commission was established in 1950, the National Development Council in 1952, the Planning Commission was dissolved in 2014, and NITI Aayog was established in 2015.

secs.t: Overall assessment — achievements vs failures

x: The chief drawback was
implementation failure
, even though planning produced several measurable achievements.
Regional disparities persisted and therefore were a failure rather than an achievement.
Rising unemployment
was identified as a failure and as a root cause of poverty.
Average growth over Plans I to XI was about
4.5 per cent
, compared with roughly 1 per cent before Independence.

Padma Desai earned her Harvard Economics PhD in 1960 and co-authored the 1970 work with Jagdish Bhagwati.

abolition of the Planning Commission
ended the system of discretionary plan grants.

Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati

The mandate of NITI Aayog covers knowledge and innovation, NITI for States, driving transformational change, and monitoring and evaluation.
NITI Aayog was set up by
a Union Cabinet resolution of 1 January 2015
, replacing the Planning Commission (dissolved 2014).

secs.t: Objectives and guiding approach — Cabinet resolution

x: One Cabinet-resolution objective is to formulate credible plans at the village level and aggregate them progressively at higher levels.
All three statements reflect the objectives of NITI Aayog in promoting shared national priorities and cooperative federalism.
Antyodaya, inclusive and participatory development, and attention to small enterprises are guiding priorities.
A is true: NITI Aayog was created by an executive Cabinet resolution and is advisory.

secs.t: Composition — posts and how they are filled

x: The Prime Minister is the Chairperson, appoints the Vice-Chairperson, and may nominate up to two part-time members from universities and research bodies.
The key gives
five full-time and two part-time members

. 'Three full-time' is the 2015 set-up found in older sources; up to eight full-time and no part-time members described the Planning Commission; and four is the ceiling for ex-officio Union Ministers, not part-time members (maximum 2).

x: NITI Aayog follows a bottom-up approach and promotes cooperative federalism, unlike the Planning Commission’s top-down, one-size-fits-all planning.

The Planning Commission limited the role of States largely to the National Development Council and annual plan discussions, whereas NITI Aayog gives every Chief Minister a direct role through its Governing Council.
Like NITI Aayog later (1 January 2015), the Planning Commission was created by a Cabinet resolution on 15 March 1950, with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru as its first chairman.

NITI Aayog’s State rankings encourage
competitive federalism
by comparing performance across States and promoting improvement.

National multidimensional poverty fell from 55.3% in 2005-06 to 14.96% in 2019-21 and was estimated at 11.28% in 2022-23.
Both statements are true, and the measurable comparison of State performance and district-level outcomes explains how these indices strengthen competitive federalism.

rows.title: Economic growth vs economic development; measures of development
sub: Group-II M2-A-7: Economic growth and economic development - concepts, measures and indicators

secs.t: Growth vs development — definitions and indicators — Growth vs development

x: Development has a broader, not narrower, scope than growth.
Real GDP or real GNP
measures changes in output and is therefore a conventional measure of economic growth.
Development cannot occur without some growth, although growth alone may not produce development.
Growth is regarded as a means, whereas development is the broader end involving improved well-being, capabilities and distribution.

secs.t: Growth vs development — definitions and indicators — Models of development

x: Exam angle: "which is NOT emphasised by the new view" - answer is the simple growth rate only.
The Directive Principles envisage adequate livelihood and reduced inequality, rather than merely a higher national income.
An increase in per-capita GNP may indicate economic growth, but it does not signify development if poverty and unemployment are increasing.

secs.t: Growth vs development — definitions and indicators — Indicators of development

x: A larger share of GDP from the primary sector is not treated as an indicator of economic development.
Human resource development is an important sign and component of economic development.
Structural transformation involves movement from an agrarian economy towards industrial and service sectors.

secs.t: Economists → approaches and theories of development

x: The capability approach is associated with Amartya Sen; the basic needs approach with the ILO and Paul Streeten; the income approach with the conventional or classical approach; and the welfare approach with Pigou.
The Basic Needs Approach (ILO, 1976; Paul Streeten) aims at
food, shelter, health and education
for all, rather than mere growth of income or output.
Ragnar Nurkse
is associated with the vicious circle of poverty, expressed through the idea that a country is poor because it remains poor.

secs.t: Books → authors

x: Gunnar Myrdal wrote Economic Theory and Underdeveloped Regions; A.O. Hirschman wrote The Strategy of Economic Development; Charles P. Kindleberger wrote Strategic Factors in Economic Development.

secs.t: Measures of development → developer, year, components

x: PQLI is based on literacy, infant mortality and life expectancy at age one.
The PQLI is calculated as a simple average of its three components and is expressed on a 0–100 scale.
Paul Samuelson is associated with NEW, Nordhaus and Tobin with MEW, and Corrado Gini with the Gini coefficient.
Gross National Happiness was introduced as an idea by
Bhutan's fourth King, Jigme Singye Wangchuck
, during the 1970s.

secs.t: Curves and inequality measures → economist

x: The Kuznets curve presents an inverted-U relationship: inequality initially rises and subsequently falls with increasing income.
The Environmental Kuznets Curve suggests that pollution initially rises and later falls as per capita income increases.
The Laffer curve shows that tax revenue may decline when tax rates are increased beyond a certain point.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: growth terms and sustainable development

x: Exam angle: "Who used the term Hindu rate of growth and why" - Raj Krishna, stagnant growth.
Trickle-down is the belief that the benefits of growth will percolate automatically to poorer sections of society.
The term
sustainable growth
is used for a policy aim directed towards the economic and social well-being of people.
The definition balances present needs with the ability of future generations to meet their own needs; it neither rejects development nor prohibits resource use.

secs.t: Determinants of growth — factors and effects

x: Natural resources and technical progress are economic factors, while effective institutions, rule of law, population quality and social structure are non-economic factors.

A higher ICOR means more capital is needed per unit of extra output, i.e. capital is less efficient, so a given saving and investment rate yields lower growth (growth = saving rate / capital-output ratio).

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The combination of high growth with inadequate well-being, declining real wages and unemployment reflects the
high growth–low well-being paradox
Swarna Andhra @2047 targets GSDP of ₹308 lakh crore, per capita income of ₹55 lakh and growth above 15%, with progress tracked through 651 KPIs.
The distinction highlighted is that welfare often refers to immediate redistribution, while development is a broader process involving sustained improvement in economic and social conditions.

rows.title: Distributive justice and inclusive growth - concept, indicators, policy instruments

secs.t: Inclusive growth — definitions and three pillars

x: Exam angle: a direct "three pillars" recall question; do not confuse with the 11th Plan's components of inclusive growth (below).
Inclusive growth is broad-based, shared and pro-poor growth that raises people's participation in the growth process.
Inclusive growth considers both the pace and pattern of growth, including who receives the benefits, gender balance and regional balance.

secs.t: Articles and amendments on distributive justice

x: Article 38 seeks a social order based on social, economic and political justice and directs the State to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities.
Article 38(2) was added by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.
Art. 39(c) targets concentration of wealth and means of production.

secs.t: Persons → growth-first vs redistribution (Bhagwati-Sen debate)

x: The debate contrasts the growth-first approach with prioritising investment in social infrastructure such as health and education.
Why Growth Matters
, published in 2013, is associated with Jagdish Bhagwati and Arvind Panagariya.
Sen emphasised
primary education and health
as the highest priorities for backward countries.
Development as Freedom is associated with Sen's capability approach, while the Kerala Model illustrates high health and education outcomes at modest income.

secs.t: Approaches to poverty — trickle-down vs direct attack

x: The trickle-down approach assumes that growth generated through tax cuts and business incentives will spread to all sections of society.
VB-G RAM G and DAY-NRLM
are identified as examples of direct poverty-attack measures.
Trickle-down corresponds to the early Plans’ growth-first strategy; direct attack to ‘Garibi Hatao’; welfare to Nordic states; and bottom-up to the SHG movement.

secs.t: Plans and schemes for inclusive growth — Inclusive growth in the Plans - FIRST/LAST

x: The 12th Plan's theme was '
Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth

'. 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth' was the 11th Plan (2007-12), the first to make inclusive growth the objective; 'Garibi Hatao' is linked to the 5th Plan's direct attack on poverty; and 'Sabka Saath...' is the present government's framing, not a Plan theme.

secs.t: Plans and schemes for inclusive growth — Instruments → latest position

x: DAY-NRLM covers 10.05 crore women in 90.09 lakh SHGs.
VB-G RAM G replaced MGNREGA and increased the employment guarantee from 100 days to 125 days.
PM Vishwakarma relates to 18 artisan trades, not agricultural commodity exchanges.
Aspirational Districts began in January 2018 with 49 key performance indicators across five themes.

secs.t: Plans and schemes for inclusive growth — Statement traps

x: Inclusive growth is not expected from a high national-income growth rate alone; rural development, agriculture and farm credit are important supporting instruments.
The identified target segments include
marginal farmers, landless labourers and SC/ST communities
; the focus is not limited to persons in semi-urban areas.
Education reform and vocational training
support inclusive growth.

secs.t: Data — measuring inclusion

x: GDP, industrial output and employment are measures of growth, whereas HDI, poverty rates, literacy, access to basic services and gender equality indicate inclusive development.
The two poverty-line comparisons cover 2011–12 to 2022–23 and report the stated declines.
The WEF’s IDI measures development
beyond GDP
by incorporating growth, inclusion and sustainability-related dimensions.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Welfare delivery in Andhra Pradesh is stated to occur through
Direct Benefit Transfer
(DBT).
The World Bank indicates falling poverty, whereas the World Inequality Database indicates rising income inequality.
The 12th Five-Year Plan was the last Five-Year Plan.

rows.title: Human Development Index - components, methodology, India's rank and trend
sub: Group-II M2-A-8: Human development and inclusive growth - HDI, MPI and India's performance

secs.t: Human development — concept, persons and origin

x: The HDI was conceived by
Mahbub ul Haq
with Amartya Sen; Inge Kaul was also part of the team.
The capability approach treats
people and their capabilities
, rather than economic growth alone, as the ultimate criteria of development.
Malaysia has higher GNI per capita, but Chile has a much higher HDI because of better life expectancy and schooling outcomes.

secs.t: HDI methodology — components, goalposts, formula

x: The goalposts are 20–85 years for life expectancy, 0–18 for expected schooling, 0–15 for mean schooling and 100–75,000 PPP dollars for GNI per capita.
Purchasing Power Parity dollars allow income to be compared fairly across countries with
different price levels
Long and healthy life is measured by life expectancy; knowledge by mean and expected years of schooling; and standard of living by GNI per capita in PPP dollars.

secs.t: Related indices → year introduced and what they measure

x: IHDI adjusts potential human development for inequality and the gap from HDI indicates the loss due to inequality.
PHDI, introduced in 2020, adjusts HDI for planetary pressures represented by carbon dioxide emissions and material footprint.
GDI was introduced in 1995, CPM in 1996, HPI in 1997 and IHDI in 2010.
HDI is criticised for ignoring or inadequately reflecting inequality, sustainability and gender.

secs.t: Data — HDI categories and India's rank

x: Sri Lanka and Maldives ranked above India, and Brazil, Russia, China and South Africa all ranked above India among the original BRICS members.
An HDI value from 0.550 to 0.699 falls in the
medium human development
category.
India was ranked 134th among 193 countries in the HDR 2023–24, based on HDI values for 2022.

secs.t: Places — state HDI and National Human Development Reports

x: Kerala consistently tops Indian States in human development and is commonly associated with the Kerala Model.
Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh
are identified among the lowest-ranking States in human development.
District-level estimates reveal sharper intra-State gaps that may be concealed by State-level averages.
The first NHDR was published in 2001 and the second, titled India Human Development Report, was published in 2011.

secs.t: Data — Andhra Pradesh HDI gap and multidimensional poverty

x: The MPI score fell by approximately half, from 0.053 to 0.025, over the cited period.
Andhra Pradesh ranked ninth among States in the cited multidimensional poverty comparison.
Andhra Pradesh's MPI was reported at 0.025 and its headcount ratio at 6.06%, which was under half the national headcount ratio of 14.96%.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: inclusive growth and human capital

x: The three pillars (APPSC 2025 key) are Market Economics, Empowerment and Pragmatism - not 'Antyodaya, Empowerment, Poverty and Unemployment'.
Human capital formation raises productivity and earnings, promotes faster growth and helps reduce poverty; it does not cause a
permanent decline in labour productivity
Human capital formation includes investment in education, health, skills acquired through on-the-job training, migration and information, all of which enhance people's productive capacity.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The policy discussion indicates that the Government now leans on the Multidimensional Poverty Index rather than relying only on income poverty lines.
India ranked 149th by nominal GDP per capita (about $2,813) and 119th by PPP (about $12,964) in 2026, close to its HDI rank.
Kerala
is moving to extreme-poverty-free status, a current development in poverty debates.

rows.title: Related UNDP indices - IHDI, Gender Inequality Index, Gender Development Index, Multidimensional Poverty Index

secs.t: UNDP indices → year introduced and FIRSTs

x: The HPI measured deprivation in
longevity, knowledge and a decent standard of living
The Gender-related Development Index and Gender Empowerment Measure were both introduced in the HDR 1995 as earlier companion indices.
The GII came in HDR 2010 and a higher value means more inequality.
GDI/GEM dates to 1995, HPI to 1997, and MPI, GII and IHDI to 2010.

secs.t: Indices → dimensions and indicators

x: The Human Poverty Index indicated
the standard of living
by measuring selected forms of deprivation.
The labour-market dimension uses female and male labour-force participation among persons aged
15 years and above

The Global MPI covers nutrition and child mortality under health; years of schooling and school attendance under education; and cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing and assets under living standards.

secs.t: Terms → meaning (IHDI loss, parity, headcount x intensity)

x: Exam angle: 0.069 vs 0.690 vs 0.096 style options; the value is small because MPI = headcount x intensity.
A GDI value of 1 represents
gender parity
in the measured dimensions of health, education and earned income.
The MPI proposed by Alkire and Santos uses household-survey micro-data to identify multiple deprivations at the individual level.

secs.t: Bodies and persons → MPI (publishers, method, global vs national)

x: Exam angle: "Which organisation estimates the National MPI?" - NITI Aayog.
The MPI was proposed by
Sabina Alkire and Maria Emma Santos
The National MPI retains the three equally weighted dimensions, uses the Alkire–Foster method and expands the indicator count to 12.
The National MPI is monitored under the
Global Indices for Reforms and Growth
initiative.

secs.t: Data — Global MPI, India by edition

x: The headcount ratio fell from 55.1% in 2005–06 to 16.4% in 2019–21, representing about 234 million people in poverty in the latter period.
The Global MPI 2022 reported that
414 million
people moved out of multidimensional poverty in India between 2005–06 and 2019–21.
The 2018 Global MPI reported 271 million moving out between 2005-06 and 2015-16, with Bihar the poorest State.

secs.t: Data — National MPI trend between NFHS rounds

x: All three statements correctly describe the Progress Review 2023: about 13.5 crore people escaped poverty, MPI declined from 0.117 to 0.066, and intensity fell from 47% to 44%.
For 2019–21, the National MPI reported a headcount ratio of 14.96%, intensity of 44.39% and MPI value of 0.066.
The World Bank figures show a decline from 57.7% to 23.9% at the $4.20-a-day line and from 27.1% to 5.3% at the $3-a-day extreme-poverty line.

secs.t: Places — state-wise MPI, India and Andhra Pradesh

x: Andhra Pradesh had a headcount ratio of 6.06% and intensity of 41.12%, both lower than India’s 14.96% and 44.39%.
Kerala has an MPI value of 0.002, Goa 0.003, Tamil Nadu 0.009 and Bihar 0.16.
The values were Bihar 0.160, Meghalaya 0.133, Jharkhand 0.131 and Uttar Pradesh 0.103, giving the stated descending order.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Rural poverty was lowest in
Himachal Pradesh
at 0.4% under the updated assessment.
The steepest falls in poverty were reported in
Odisha and Bihar
The two estimates are different because they use different poverty lines and count poverty differently.

rows.title: Other global indices - Global Hunger Index, Environmental Performance Index, Ease of Doing Business, Global Innovation Index, World Happiness Report

secs.t: Global indices → publisher

x: The Global Hunger Index is published by Concern Worldwide of Ireland and Welthungerhilfe of Germany.
WIPO co-publishes the Global Innovation Index with Cornell University and INSEAD; this association dates from 2007.
The Agriculture Orientation Index is published by FAO, not IFPRI.
WIPO was established in 1967, is a UN agency headquartered in Geneva and has 193 members.

secs.t: Indices → indicators and components

x: The GHI uses undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality;
maternal mortality
is not one of its four indicators.
B. The GII has five input pillars and two output pillars, and knowledge and technology outputs is an output pillar, so statements 1-3 are correct.
The six variables include GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity and perceptions of corruption.

secs.t: Ease of Doing Business — India's rank, indicators and successor

x: The report functioned as a ready reckoner for
foreign investors
by comparing business regulations across economies.
The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (
DPIIT
) is the nodal agency for India's participation in B-READY.
Enforcing contracts
and registering property remained among India’s worst indicators in Doing Business 2020.
A
Single Window System
for business clearances counts towards Ease of Doing Business.

secs.t: Issues — India's objections to GHI and EPI

x: India objected to the preference for absolute emissions, the neglect of the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities, and the use of contested indicators.
The counter-evidence includes India's 23rd position in CCPI 2026, 50 percent non-fossil installed power capacity in 2025 and achievement five years before the 2030 NDC target.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India ranked 176th of 177 overall, 175th in Air Quality and 130th in Climate Mitigation in the EPI 2026.
India occupied the
54th
position in StartupBlink's Innovators Business Environment Index 2026.
Perception surveys and absolute-emission metrics may disadvantage populous developing countries, particularly because absolute emissions can be high due to population size.

rows.title: Environmental degradation as a development challenge; green accounting and green GDP

secs.t: Functions of the environment and FIRSTs

x: The environment supplies renewable and non-renewable resources, assimilates wastes, sustains genetic and biological diversity, and provides scenery and amenity.
An environmental crisis arises when resource extraction exceeds regeneration and waste generation exceeds the environment’s absorptive capacity.
EIA was first used in 1978 for river valley projects; the notification dates are 1994 and 2006, and clearance is compulsory for 39 project categories.

secs.t: Terms → meaning

x: Absorptive capacity is the ability of the environment to absorb degradation, or the maximum pollutant load an ecosystem can process and neutralise without harm.
A green economy fosters green industries and green jobs that preserve or restore environmental quality while decoupling development from resource use and pollution (APPSC-GS 2025 key).

secs.t: Causes of degradation → effects; resource → cause matching

x: Green urea uses
green hydrogen and captured carbon dioxide
and is regarded as a low-carbon alternative.
Urban particulate pollution and coal-based power
are identified as the main reasons for India’s low Environmental Performance Index score.
Deep bore tubewells are associated with groundwater depletion, brick production with topsoil loss, and agricultural expansion with habitat loss.

secs.t: Persons, reports and frameworks → green accounting

x: The
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
compiles environment accounts based on SEEA and has released ecosystem and natural-asset accounts since 2018.
EnviStats India is an annual MoSPI publication based on the United Nations Statistics Division’s FDES 2013.
The six components are conditions and quality; resources and use; residuals; extreme events; human settlements and health; and protection and management.

secs.t: Acts, rules and policy tools

x: The Green Credit Rules, 2023 were framed under the
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986

secs.t: Data — land degradation, restoration and cost

x: The Atlas estimated 97.85 million hectares, equivalent to 29.77% of India's area, as degraded during 2018–19.
B. The World Bank's 2013 assessment put India's annual cost of environmental degradation at about
of GDP (Rs 3.75 lakh crore, for 2009), through higher healthcare spending and lower labour productivity.
Environmental degradation raises healthcare expenditure and reduces labour productivity, creating a combined economic cost.

secs.t: Debates — growth vs environment trade-off

x: The trade-off view argues that environmental rules can slow growth and reflects the ‘grow first, clean up later’ approach associated with Environmental Kuznets Curve logic.
The poor, particularly
people living in slums and flood-prone areas
, bear most of the costs of environmental degradation.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The AP Common Zoning Regulations 2026 provide for
nine
land-use categories.
Forests, hills, water bodies, eco-sensitive areas and Coastal Regulation Zone areas are development-restricted under the regulations.
Conventional GDP does not account for the depletion of natural resources; consequently, recorded growth can coexist with a loss of natural capital.

rows.title: Sustainable development - definition, Brundtland Report, SDGs and India's progress

secs.t: Sustainable development — milestones and FIRSTs

x: The 2012 Rio+20 Conference, formally the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development, took the decision to develop the SDGs.
The World Conservation Strategy was issued in 1980, followed by the Brundtland Report in 1987, the Rio Earth Summit in 1992 and Agenda 2030/SDGs in 2015.
The 1980 World Conservation Strategy was associated with
IUCN, UNEP and WWF
and represented an early use of the term sustainable development.

secs.t: Books, reports and persons → sustainable development

x: The World Commission on Environment and Development was chaired by
Gro Harlem Brundtland
, who was the Prime Minister of Norway.
The
World Commission on Environment and Development
, popularly called the Brundtland Commission, is credited with first defining sustainable development in Our Common Future.

secs.t: Terms → meaning

x: The core goal is to meet present needs without reducing the options available to future generations, within the Earth’s carrying capacity.
The finite carrying capacity of the Earth is a concern reflected in Limits to Growth, Our Common Future and the 1992 UNCED process.
The precautionary principle, polluter pays principle and common but differentiated responsibilities were endorsed at Rio 1992.

secs.t: Agenda 2030 and the SDGs — roots, principles, number game

x: Exam angle: 169 targets vs distractors 99, 129, 150.
India’s National Indicator Framework 2026 contains 277 indicators and is associated with the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
Universality means that Agenda 2030 applies to all countries, irrespective of their level of development.
A specific focus of Agenda 2030 is ending all discrimination and violence against
women and girls

secs.t: Data — India's SDG progress

x: India ranked 94th, behind the four mentioned South Asian countries, lagged on 13 goals, and had SDG 2 as its principal concern.
In the 2025 SDSN report, India ranked 99th out of 167, scored approximately 67, and entered the top 100 for the first time.
Kerala and Uttarakhand jointly occupy the top position with a score of 79, whereas Bihar is at the bottom with 57.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs is aligned with
SDG 11
, which concerns sustainable cities and communities.

rows.title: India's environmental policy framework - National Environment Policy, EIA, polluter pays and precautionary principles

secs.t: Acts, bodies and schemes → year and purpose

x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 protects wildlife and habitats and regulates hunting.
Environmental Impact Assessment is mandatory under the
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
SPCB compensation powers rest on
Sec. 33A of the Water Act and Sec. 31A of the Air Act
The Eco-Mark scheme was launched in 1991 to label environment-friendly consumer products.

secs.t: Cases → year and doctrine

x: Ratlam Municipality (1980) recognised the municipal duty to deal with public nuisance and protect public health and sanitation.
The Bichhri case of Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action concerned chemical units in Rajasthan and clean-up costs.
The
Taj Trapezium
case (1997) mandated the use of CNG as an environmental protection measure.

secs.t: Principles → meaning

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2024 and 2025 both asked what the precautionary principle means: "act/stop even without full scientific certainty".
Under the precautionary principle, the burden of proof shifts to the actor undertaking the potentially harmful activity to demonstrate that it is benign.
The precautionary principle requires preventive action despite the absence of complete scientific certainty, and the burden of proof lies on the developer.

secs.t: Policies and schemes → features (NEP 2006, NAPCC 2008, Eco-Mark)

x: The Eco-Mark logo is
an earthen pot
, used for labelling environment-friendly consumer products.

The eight missions include Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture and Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change.
NAPCC came in 2008 with eight missions (Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, Strategic Knowledge).

secs.t: AP environmental institutions — APPCB, EPTRI

x: The APPCB functions under the Water and Air Acts, issues consents and classifies industries, including White and Green categories.
White-category industries are practically non-polluting, while Green-category industries have low pollution potential.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Coastal Regulation Zone provisions fall under the
Environment (Protection) Act
The Vanashakti ruling is associated with 31 July 2026.
The criticism concerned thin baseline data and the adequacy of the initial environmental information.
SAEIA/SCEIA (July 2026) and the EP Fund Rules 2026 are current developments.
The Common Zoning Regulations 2026 of Andhra Pradesh provide for 9 land-use categories.

rows.title: National income concepts - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, factor cost vs market price, GVA, deflator
sub: Group-II M2-A-2: National income of India - concepts: GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, GVA, factor cost and market price

secs.t: Terms → meaning (GDP, GNP, national income, SDP) — GDP

x: GDP
measures the market value of final goods and services produced within a country's geographical boundaries during a year, including production by residents and non-residents.
GDP is the market value of final output, represented as quantity of output (Q) multiplied by its price (P).
National income is the sum of wages, rent, interest and profits earned by factors belonging to the country, including the adjustment for NFIA.

secs.t: Terms → meaning (GDP, GNP, national income, SDP) — State Domestic Product

x: That is the APSES definition of
State Domestic Product
(asked in APPSC 2025).
Production taxes are levied irrespective of the quantity of output;
stamp duty
and property tax are examples.
Transfer earnings
are not payments for factor services and are therefore excluded from national income.

secs.t: Aggregates → formula

x: NDP = GDP – depreciation, NNP = GNP – depreciation, and NNP at factor cost is National Income.
Depreciation, or consumption of fixed capital, is deducted because production used only to replace worn-out capital adds nothing new to the productive stock.
NFIA is
factor income received from abroad minus factor income paid abroad

secs.t: Aggregates → formula — Market price vs factor cost

x: Indirect taxes and subsidies, not direct taxes, form the relevant bridge.

secs.t: Aggregates → formula — Personal, disposable and per capita income

x: Per capita income
is calculated as national income divided by population.
Undistributed corporate profits, social security contributions and corporate tax are deducted.
Personal disposable income equals personal income minus
personal direct taxes and non-tax payments such as fines and fees
National savings equals national disposable income minus consumption: ₹800 crore − ₹650 crore =
₹150 crore

secs.t: GNP vs GDP — rule and worked examples

x: Exam angle: numerical questions give GDP, NFIA, depreciation and net indirect taxes and ask for NI.
GNPMP = 500 – 10 = ₹490 crore; NNPMP = 490 – 50 = ₹440 crore; NNPFC = 440 – 40 =
₹400 crore
India's net factor income from abroad is usually negative, making GNP lower than GDP.

secs.t: Included vs excluded in national income

x: Commission on resale is payment for a productive service and is included.
Value added at each stage is included, while intermediate goods are excluded separately to avoid double counting.

secs.t: Nominal vs real GDP and the GDP deflator

x: The 2022–23 series uses
double deflation
, which separately deflates output prices and input prices.
The increase in nominal GDP is exactly matched by the increase in the price index from 100 to 120, so output measured at constant prices remains unchanged.
A rising GNP or GDP deflator indicates a higher general price level.
The
GDP deflator
covers all goods and services in GDP (consumption, investment, government, exports), whereas WPI, CPI and CPI-IW price fixed baskets (APPSC-G2 2025 key).

secs.t: Data — GVA headline, PPP and India's rank

x: The difference between GDP and GVA at the relevant price level is attributable to
net product taxes
PPP estimates are made under the International Comparison Program of the UNSD, with the World Bank as global implementing agency and the NSO as India's nodal agency.
Lower prices in India make its output larger when valued using purchasing power parity than when converted at market exchange rates.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The new GDP series introduced
double deflation and Supply-Use Tables
as important methodological features.
GDP measures production within the domestic territory, while GNP is based on the income or production associated with the country’s nationals or residents.
Andhra Pradesh per capita income is computed on the basis of
Net State Domestic Product (NSDP)

rows.title: Methods of measuring national income - product, income and expenditure methods; difficulties
sub: Group-II M2-A-3: Measurement of national income - product, income and expenditure methods; difficulties

secs.t: Economists → definitions of national income

x: Marshall defined the national dividend in terms of the net aggregate of commodities and services produced by labour and capital acting on natural resources.
Pigou's definition includes income from abroad and restricts national income to the portion measurable in money.
Fisher's definition is consumption-based.

secs.t: Terms → meaning (circular flow, value added, double counting)

x: Factor payments constitute the money flow from
firms to households
in return for factor services.
Leakages are saving, taxes and imports; injections are investment, government spending and exports.
Gross Value Added includes depreciation, while Net Value Added is calculated as GVA minus depreciation.
Under double deflation, real GVA is real output minus real intermediate consumption, with output and input prices deflated separately.

secs.t: Methods → what is summed (product, income, expenditure)

x: Exam angle:
"Cost and Accounting method" is NOT a method
of measuring national income.
The production or product method measures national income by summing the value added by each producing unit, which is equal to the value of the final product after avoiding double counting.
The income method sums compensation of employees, operating surplus (rent, interest, profit) and mixed income.

secs.t: Methods → sectors in India

x: The expenditure method is used partly for construction, and expenditure data including PFCE acts as a check on and cross-check of demand-side estimates.
India applies the production method to agriculture, mining and manufacturing, the income method to services, and the expenditure method partly to construction and as a cross-check.
The income method is used for service activities such as trade, transport, banking, real estate, public administration and other services.

secs.t: Inclusion and exclusion test — what enters national income

x: Interest on productive loans is a return to a factor of production and is included.
The second-hand good itself was counted when originally produced.
Transactions in shares and bonds merely transfer ownership of financial assets and do not represent current production.
Changes in inventories are included, while tax revenue as such, interest on public debt and unpaid services of housewives are excluded.

secs.t: Difficulties in measuring national income in India

x: The informal sector is difficult to measure because it often lacks proper accounts; a well-documented and fully accounted sector would not constitute the stated difficulty.
When individuals perform several occupations, classification of their output and income becomes difficult because occupational specialisation is absent.
Supply and Use Tables are used to reconcile supply and expenditure data and thereby reduce the discrepancy between the two sides of GDP estimation.

secs.t: State income — AP terms, formulae and compilation

x: GST data is now available in addition to the earlier practice of allocating manufacturing GVA according to States' shares in the Annual Survey of Industries.
The guideline seeks to integrate administrative records, sector databases and surveys, while improving coverage of services and the unincorporated segment and consistency with national accounts.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 2022-23 series uses ASUSE, PLFS, GST, PFMS and e-Vahan data.
The new series improves real GVA estimation through double deflation and volume extrapolation.
The 2022-23 PFCE benchmark is based on the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2022-23.
AP's real growth was 9.88% against India's 7.4%.
