rows.title: India's national accounts - NSO/MoSPI, base year revisions, quarterly estimates, informal sector estimation
sub: Group-II M2-A-4: India's national accounts - NSO, base-year revisions and data issues

secs.t: Persons and bodies → early estimates and FIRSTs

x: Exam angle: "first Indian to calculate national income by scientific method" = V.K.R.V. Rao.
Dadabhai Naoroji
made the first recorded attempt in 1868 and estimated per capita income at Rs 20.
The committee was constituted in August 1949, chaired by P.C. Mahalanobis, included Gadgil and Rao, and submitted its first report in 1951.

secs.t: Statistical bodies → year and role (CSO, NSO, NSC, ISI) — CSO and divisions

x: The National Accounts Division handles GDP, consumption and capital formation; ESD compiles IIP; the Kolkata wing conducts ASI; and NSO compiles the National Industrial Classification.
A. The statistical office set up on 2 May 1951 began as the
Central Statistical Institute
and was merged into the CSO in 1954; the CSO has prepared national income estimates since 1955.

secs.t: Statistical bodies → year and role (CSO, NSO, NSC, ISI) — Statistical bodies

x: The NSO is the umbrella body for national accounts, IIP, CPI and surveys.
MoSPI/NSO prepares estimates of consumption, capital formation and saving with institutional-sector detail.
The sectors identified for these estimates are
household, private corporate and public sectors
The private corporate share of GFCF was 33 per cent, described as a decadal low.

secs.t: Base year → meaning and sequence of revisions

x: Exam angle: CPI's old base is the calendar year 2012, not 2011-12.
Periodic revision makes the estimates more representative of changing production patterns and relative prices.
The IIP was rebased to 2022-23 and is released
monthly with a 28-day lag

secs.t: 2011-12 series (2015) — method, criticism and persons

x: The 2011-12 series adopted
GVA at basic prices
as the headline measure.
The MCA-21 company database represented an
enterprise approach
and partly replaced the earlier reliance on ASI for the relevant estimation.
The series was criticised for unusually high manufacturing growth that was inconsistent with physical indicators and for overestimating the private corporate sector.

secs.t: 2022-23 series — release, method changes and revisions — Release and choice of year

x: 2022-23 was treated as a relatively normal year; 2017-18 involved the GST transition, 2019-21 was affected by COVID, and 2021-22 carried base effects.
MCA-21
continues to be used for organised manufacturing but is not included in this particular list of new data sources.
The new series cut GDP by 3-4%, so nominal 2022-23 GDP fell from about Rs 269 to Rs 261 lakh crore.

secs.t: 2022-23 series — release, method changes and revisions — Revisions under the new series

x: The 2023-24 growth estimate was cut from 9.2% to 7.2%, whereas the 2024-25 estimate was raised from 6.5% to 7.1%.
HCES 2022-23 was the first full Household Consumption Expenditure Survey since 2011-12; the 2017-18 results were withheld.

secs.t: Estimates → timing (release calendar and quarterly GDP)

x: Advance estimates use the
benchmark-indicator method
, which projects the relevant aggregates using available indicators.
Quarterly GDP estimates are released about two months after the relevant quarter ends, although older material had indicated about one month.
The IMF flagged the
absence of a seasonally adjusted series and a lag in disaggregating capital formation

secs.t: Surveys → what they measure; informal sector estimation

x: The household or unincorporated sector is benchmarked on ASUSE and subsequently extrapolated with suitable indicators.
PLFS
measures employment, unemployment, LFPR and WPR through monthly, quarterly and annual estimates.
HCES covers household consumption, ASI covers registered factories, ASUSE covers unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises and TUS covers time use.
All four statements correctly describe the recent expansion of PLFS and ASUSE estimation arrangements.

secs.t: AP — GSDP estimation by DES

x: The 2025-26 First Advance Estimate placed Andhra Pradesh GSDP at
Rs 17.62 lakh crore
at current prices.
The
Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Andhra Pradesh
, estimates GSDP for the State.
Under the consistency mandate, States integrate administrative, sectoral and survey data and keep their accounts consistent with the national accounts.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Current criticism and debate concern the coverage of the informal sector and the use of MCA-based manufacturing GVA.
The NSO follows IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard norms and acts as India's nodal agency for the International Comparison Programme.
DES-AP moved towards the
base under the MoSPI GSVA guideline.
AP DES compiles GSDP and a State CPI-IW series.

rows.title: Trends in India's national income, per capita income and sectoral shares; inter-state GSDP comparison
sub: Group-II M2-A-18: Current state of the Indian economy - growth trends, key challenges and outlook

secs.t: Terms and FIRSTs — Hindu rate of growth, largest sector, income class

x: The expression refers to economies achieving growth of 7% or more for a decade or longer.
Services is the largest source by sector, while the household sector, largely unorganised, is the largest institutional source.
India remained a lower-middle-income economy according to the World Bank's GNI per capita classification using the Atlas method.

secs.t: Data — growth record and real GDP growth by year — Historical record

x: Growth did not rise steadily; the economy contracted in 2020-21, followed by subsequent recovery.
India's nominal GDP at market prices grew almost
twelve times
since 1991.
Real GDP growth for 2024-25 was
7.1 percent
under the new series; the old-series figure was 6.5 percent.
The 2025-26 FAE was 7.4 percent, SAE was 7.6 percent and Q3 growth was 7.8 percent.

secs.t: Data — growth record and real GDP growth by year — Latest quarter and size

x: The 2025-26 estimate placed the economy at about ₹345 lakh crore, equivalent to approximately USD 3.9 trillion.

secs.t: Data — sectoral and institutional shares

x: Industry contributed about
13 percent
of GDP in 1950-51.
Agriculture's share was about 17 percent by 2017-18, services exceeded 50 percent, and the order was services greater than industry greater than agriculture.
The 2022-23 series raised agriculture's GVA by 3.8-5.9 percent and cut trade GVA by 36 percent.
Agriculture
was the largest contributor at Independence (APPSC 2023).

secs.t: India's GDP rank — nominal, PPP and projections

x: India ranked fourth by nominal GDP after overtaking Japan in 2025, when its nominal GDP was stated as USD 4.18 trillion.
India is the 3rd largest economy by PPP GDP, after the United States and China (ICP 2021; APPSC 2025).
The
World Bank
implements the ICP, while UNSD is associated with the programme and the NSO is the nodal agency in India.

secs.t: Inter-state comparison — per capita income, divergence and AP

x: India as a whole had a per capita income of approximately
in the cited comparison.
The new contribution criterion uses the square root of GSDP; the per capita GSDP income-distance criterion remains, and devolution remains at 41 percent.
A rising Gini means greater inequality, so State incomes have diverged.

secs.t: Macro stability and infrastructure — indicators and schemes

x: The Union fiscal deficit figures are 4.8% for FY25, 4.4% for FY26 and 4.3% as the FY27 budget estimate.
All three statements correctly describe S&P's August 2025 upgrade and the affirmed BBB/A-2 stable assessment.
The NIP covered projects estimated at approximately
₹111 lakh crore
The seven engines are roads, railways, airports, ports, mass transport, waterways and logistics infrastructure.

secs.t: Growth forecasts → agency

x: The IMF's World Economic Outlook projected global growth of
for 2026 in the reference scenario.
The Global Economic Prospects is published by the World Bank, monetary policy projections are associated with the RBI, and advance or quarterly estimates are issued by NSO (MoSPI).
The RBI projected Q1 FY27 growth at 7.0%, whereas actual growth was 7.8%.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The new GDP series reduced nominal GDP and per capita income estimates, while raising the FY26 growth estimate to 7.6%.
Dollar GDP rankings move with exchange rates and base revisions.
The stated concern is that Indian manufacturing lacks sufficient depth and that productivity must increase to support the Viksit Bharat objective.

rows.title: Demography of India - Census 2011 findings, population growth, density, sex ratio, literacy

secs.t: Population growth — phases and FIRSTs

x: The sequence is 1901–21 stagnant, 1921–51 steady growth, 1951–81 rapid growth, and 1981–2011 high but slowing growth.
Census 2011 counted 121.09 crore people with decadal growth of 17.7% in 2001-11.
1921 is the great divide: before it population stagnated (it even fell in 1911-21), after it population grew continuously.
Agricultural labourers
outnumbered cultivators for the first time in Census 2011.

secs.t: Data — sex ratio, literacy, religion and STs (India)

x: India's overall literacy rate rose from 18.33% in 1951 to 72.98% in 2011.
The final 2011 sex ratio is 943.
The Census definition covers persons aged 7+ who can both read and write with understanding.
In 2011, Hindus constituted 79.8% and Muslims 14.2% of India's population.
Christians numbered about 2.78 crore and constituted 2.3% of the population.

secs.t: Places — Census 2011 State and UT rankings

x: Rajasthan
recorded the largest gender gap in literacy, at 28 percentage points, compared with the national gap of 16 points.
Kerala has the highest sex ratio (1,084), Goa is the most urbanised State (~62%), Arunachal Pradesh has the lowest density (17) and Bihar the lowest literacy (~62%).
Haryana
had the lowest sex ratio among States at 879 (UT lowest: Daman and Diu 618).

secs.t: Data — workers and SC/ST household amenities

x: Census 2011 recorded about 14.4 crore agricultural labourers and 11.9 crore cultivators.
All four statements correctly describe the Census 2011 ST household amenity data.
Marginal ST landholdings accounted for 56.26% in India and 64.83% in Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh in the Census — 1901 to 2011

x: In 2011, Andhra Pradesh had a population of 495.77 lakh and a sex ratio of 997.
The urban population share of Andhra Pradesh was
in 2011, compared with 24.13% in 2001.
Statement 3 is the trap: 495.77 lakh is for the present 13-district AP; undivided AP had 8.46 crore people in 2011.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes is surveying States as part of the current demographic discussion.
The Census Town definition has been criticised on the ground that it may undercount the extent of urbanisation.
Andhra Pradesh's sex ratio of 997 is higher than India's 943, whereas its literacy rate of 67.35 per cent is lower than India's 72.98 per cent.

rows.title: Demographic transition theory and India's position; demographic dividend and its window

secs.t: Demographic transition — stages and India's position

x: India's phases were stagnant during 1901–21, steady growth during 1921–51, population explosion during 1951–81 and declining growth after 1981.
SRS 2024 shows TFR below replacement for the fifth consecutive year, consistent with India moving from late Stage 3 into Stage 4.

secs.t: Terms → meaning (CBR, CDR, MMR, dependency ratio, youth)

x: MMR = maternal deaths per
1,00,000 live births
(some sources wrongly say per 1,000).
A lower dependency ratio means fewer dependants relative to the working-age population and is a favourable condition for a demographic dividend.
The Economic Survey describes the failure to create the required conditions as potentially producing a '
demographic nightmare

secs.t: Data — vital rates and State extremes

x: The cited figures are U5MR 28, sex ratio at birth 918 during 2022–24, and MMR 80.5 in 2023.
The dependency ratio is falling primarily because fertility has declined, reducing the proportion of children.
The elderly share is projected to rise from 8.6 percent to 16 percent by 2041 and to 20.5 percent, or 325.3 million, by 2051.

secs.t: Demographic dividend — preconditions and determinants

x: Better health, education, skills and adequate jobs are necessary to realise the dividend.
Female labour-force participation rose from 23.3 percent to
41.7 percent
between 2017–18 and 2023–24.
Female education, child survival, urbanisation, the cost of raising children and contraception access are determinants of birth rate.

secs.t: States — youthful, intermediate, ageing; AP

x: Kerala's 60+ population is projected to reach 22.8% by 2036, marking the end of its demographic-dividend phase.
Andhra Pradesh's decadal growth rate declined from a peak of 21.13% during 1981–91 to 9.21% during 2001–11.
Both statements are true, and the ageing of Kerala and Tamil Nadu together with their falling working-age share explains the greater pension-related expenditure pressure.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh is in Stage 4, reflecting a low-fertility demographic setting.
The Gram Sabhas held in Andhra Pradesh in May 2026 gathered feedback on incentives proposed to reverse the trend of falling fertility.

rows.title: Population policy of India - NPP 2000, family welfare programme, ageing and migration issues

secs.t: Population policy — milestones and FIRSTs

x: The 1952 programme was clinic-based; the 1960s saw extension and target approaches with camps; 1976 brought the first National Population Policy; and 1996 introduced the target-free approach.

The 42nd Amendment (1976) put population control in the Concurrent List, the first National Population Policy came in 1976, and the programme was renamed Family Welfare in 1977 after the Emergency's forced sterilisations.

secs.t: NPP 2000 — objectives, targets, bodies and shortcomings

x: The policy adopted a target-free, voluntary and informed-choice approach and envisaged delivery through government, industry and NGOs.
The policy is criticised as family-planning-centred with a narrow focus on sterilisation, and the 1976-77 coercion left distrust.
The immediate objective concerned unmet needs for contraception and health services; the medium-term objective was TFR 2.1 by 2010; the long-term objective was population stabilisation by 2045.

secs.t: Family welfare schemes → objective and target group

x: The current focus includes Healthy Timing and Spacing of Pregnancies, Nayi Pahel kits, Saas Bahu Sammelans and FP-LMIS.
PM Matru Vandana Yojana 2.0
is a maternity-benefit scheme for pregnant and lactating women.
JSY (2005, NRHM) gives a cash incentive for institutional delivery to cut maternal and neonatal mortality (APPSC 2018 key).

secs.t: Terms and barriers — Couple Protection Rate, rural factors

x: Social orthodoxy and psychological factors
were identified as important causes of the low rural impact of family planning programmes.
Sterilisation reluctance, especially among men, is linked partly to distrust after the coercive sterilisation experience of 1976-77.
The Couple Protection Rate is the percentage of eligible couples
effectively protected against childbirth by an approved contraceptive method

secs.t: Amendments and Articles → seat freeze and delimitation

x: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 froze the allocation of seats based on the 1971 Census until 2000.
The delimitation concern is that southern States could lose approximately 8-10 Lok Sabha seats.
Articles 82 and 170
relate to the allocation and readjustment of seats on the basis of population.
The
87th Amendment (2003)
allowed boundary readjustment on the 2001 Census.

secs.t: Migration — streams, reasons and theorists

x: For inter-State female migration, Urban-Urban was the largest stream; across all streams, Rural-Rural was the largest, with marriage a major driver.
Marriage is the major stated reason for women’s migration, work for men’s migration, and Gulf migration represents the international migration context.
Everett Lee is associated with push-pull theory and intervening obstacles, Michael Todaro with the expected-income rural-urban model, and E.G. Ravenstein with the Laws of Migration.

secs.t: Ageing — data, policy and Acts

x: The IMF estimates that ageing could reduce GDP growth by about
70 basis points
a year over 2025–2050.
The National Policy on Older Persons, 1999 was associated with the Ministry of Social Justice, covered 14 areas of intervention, and included health care and nutrition.
The Act makes the maintenance of parents and senior citizens
a legal duty of children and relatives

secs.t: AP — Population Management Policy 2026

x: The Andhra Pradesh draft policy proposed removing the two-child norm for local body elections.
The draft policy shifts the emphasis from
population control to population management
The draft policy proposes an incentive of
for a second or third child.
Matrutva refers to maternal health, Shakti to women's work participation, Kshema to elderly care and Naipunyam to skills.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The cited NFHS-6 figures are a Total Fertility Rate of 2.0 and a Contraceptive Prevalence Rate of 69.1%.
The coercion-versus-choice debate is framed through the contrast between the 1976–77 approach and the National Population Policy, 2000.
The pro-natalist turn is discussed in relation to delimitation and Finance Commission population weights.
Population weights constitute approximately
of the devolution criteria referred to in the debate.

rows.title: Inequality - Lorenz curve, Gini coefficient, Kuznets hypothesis; income vs wealth inequality in India

secs.t: Persons → curves and measures

x: The Lorenz curve was developed by
Max Lorenz
in 1906 to represent the distribution of income or wealth.
The Lorenz, Phillips, Laffer and Marshall curves respectively represent distribution, inflation–unemployment, tax rate–revenue and demand relationships.
Corrado Gini
proposed the coefficient in 1912 in “Variability and Mutability”.

secs.t: Terms → meaning (Lorenz curve, Gini, Kuznets and EKC)

x: The Environmental Kuznets Curve places per-capita income on the X-axis and environmental degradation or pollution on the Y-axis.
The Kuznets hypothesis describes an inverted-U relationship: inequality rises during the initial phase of development and falls at higher income levels.
The Environmental Kuznets Curve links pollution or environmental degradation with per capita income in an inverted-U pattern and conveys the stated growth-related message.

secs.t: Data — measuring inequality in India (consumption, income, wealth, land)

x: Consumption inequality rests on NSS/HCES (MoSPI); income inequality, with no official income survey, is estimated from PLFS wages, tax data and the WID; wealth inequality uses the All India Debt and Investment Survey plus WID/Oxfam.

Disguised

Seasonal

Seasonal unemployment is associated with agriculture, tourism and agro-industries; technological unemployment with manufacturing and routine services; cyclical unemployment with recession-hit industry and services; and structural unemployment with the whole economy over the long run.

secs.t: Disguised, frictional, structural and cyclical → features

x: Exam angle: "unemployment caused by depression in an economy" =
Cyclical
Disguised unemployment is hidden unemployment, is common on family farms, and involves zero or negative marginal productivity for surplus workers.

Frictional unemployment results from the temporary time lag involved in changing or searching for jobs, while structural unemployment is long-term and arises from a mismatch between skills and available jobs.

secs.t: Other classifications → meaning

x: Invisible underemployment
exists when a person works full-time but earns very little or works below their ability, as in the example of an MBA working as a driver.
Full employment means that everyone willing to work at the prevailing wage finds work, but frictional and structural unemployment may still exist.

secs.t: Economists → laws and statements on unemployment

x: Keynes explained unemployment in developed economies mainly through
deficiency in effective demand
, which is associated with demand-deficient or cyclical unemployment.
Stagflation combines high inflation with high unemployment and therefore breaks down the traditional Phillips-curve trade-off.
Okun's law states that a one percentage point increase in unemployment above the natural rate is associated with roughly a 2% reduction in output below potential GDP.

secs.t: Data — educated unemployment

Rapid population growth, labour immobility and the shift towards capital-intensive production contribute to a long-run shortfall of labour demand relative to supply.
India has substantial seasonal, disguised and underemployment, while its basic unemployment problem is structural rather than solely Keynesian demand deficiency.

25 crore
people.

The Grameen Bank model originated in Bangladesh, not Andhra Pradesh.

, Ministry of Finance.

of foodgrains per month to eligible needy elderly persons.

secs.t: Food security — definitions, dimensions and FIRSTs

x: The World Food Summit definition emphasizes physical and economic access to
sufficient, safe and nutritious food for an active and healthy life
Availability, accessibility, affordability or access, utilisation/absorption and stability are associated with food security.
Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and landless or poor OBC sections are identified as among the most food-insecure groups.
Buffer stocks were formally introduced during the
Fourth Five-Year Plan
, covering 1969–74.

secs.t: Economists and indices → views on hunger

x: Both statements are true, and unequal distribution explains why aggregate surplus does not automatically ensure household food security.
Amartya Sen
developed the entitlement approach, especially in his work Poverty and Famines (1981).
Sen argued that famine results from a collapse of people's entitlements or command over food, not merely from a decline in overall food availability.

secs.t: Buffer stocks and OMSS — mechanism, norms and stock data

x: The minimum buffer stock levels are fixed by the
Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs
and specified for each quarter.
Quarterly buffer norms are fixed as on 1 April, 1 July, 1 October and 1 January (set by the CCEA); option A lists exactly these four dates in calendar order.
The estimate placed stocks at about 602 lakh metric tonnes, roughly three times the prescribed buffer norms.

secs.t: Acts and Articles → purpose

x: Exam angle: "what % of rural population" - answer
; urban

NFSA provides the legal right to subsidised grain; the Essential Commodities Act regulates essential goods; the Food Corporations Act created FCI; and Article 47 concerns nutrition and living standards.
The TPDS (Control) Order, 2015 provides operational rules for ration cards and Fair Price Shops under the NFSA framework.

secs.t: NFSA entitlements → quantity and price, and the 2026 amendment — Entitlements

x: An AAY household is entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains per household per month under the NFSA framework.
PHH entitlement is 5 kg per person per month.

secs.t: NFSA entitlements → quantity and price, and the 2026 amendment — Nutrition entitlements of special groups

x: The draft Bill proposes 7 kg per person for AAY households, while retaining an overall cap of 35 kg per household.
The stated aim is to remove the inequity under which smaller AAY households receive a greater quantity per person when the entitlement is fixed per household.
NFSA provides pregnant women and lactating mothers a free meal along with a maternity benefit of at least ₹6,000.

secs.t: NFSA grievance redress → Section and body

x: The NFSA provides an internal mechanism and District Grievance Redressal Officers, while State Food Commissions monitor implementation and hear appeals.
Each State has a State Food Commission, an existing body may be designated to avoid new costs, and non-compliance with DGRO recommendations can attract penalties.
Social audits, mandatory disclosure of PDS records and vigilance committees are all accountability mechanisms under the NFSA framework.

secs.t: Food schemes → year and support (PDS to PMGKAY, Bharat brand) — PMGKAY

x: The sequence is initial PDS in the 1940s, RPDS in June 1992, TPDS in June 1997 and NFSA in 2013.
PDS provides grain through Fair Price Shops; ICDS gives supplementary nutrition at anganwadis; PM POSHAN gives hot cooked meals; Food-for-Work gives grain as wages.
ICDS provides supplementary nutrition through anganwadis to
children aged 0–6 years and pregnant and lactating women

secs.t: Food schemes → year and support (PDS to PMGKAY, Bharat brand) — Price interventions

x: Bharat-brand atta, rice and dal are sold at subsidised retail prices through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets, as well as mobile vans.

NCCF procures essential goods and undertakes price-stabilisation operations.

x: PHH entitlement is 5 kg per unit, AAY entitlement is 35 kg per card, and wheat is supplied at 1 kg per card at Rs 16 per kg.
Ragi for all areas and jowar in Rayalaseema may be supplied up to 3 kg per card free of cost in lieu of rice.
All four statements correctly describe the Mee Mart initiative: its partners, first location, proposed scale and price advantage.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh is exploring a wider PDS basket including pulses, oil and fortified foods, along with convergence with Anganwadi and the Mid-Day Meal programme.
Climate-related food-security concerns now include an affordable, nutritious supply for about 1.4 billion people, rather than only the availability of sufficient grain.
The debate supports adding eggs, milk and dietary diversity while retaining cereal support rather than cutting it.

and targets villages on the northern border.

of water of the required quality.

Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
, elaborated in Target 3 Billion (co-authored with Srijan Pal Singh) to bridge the rural-urban divide.

MGNREGA provides up to 100 days of wage employment per household, with one-third participation intended for women, while NRLM promotes SHG-based self-employment and livelihoods.

73 per cent
, had FHTCs as on 31 March 2024.

Rs 4,000 crore
to the Jal Jeevan Mission.

The Community Development Programme of 1952 is identified as the first rural development programme.

4,041 statutory towns and 3,892 Census towns

x: Andhra Pradesh

recorded the highest decadal growth of urban population during 2001–2011.

secs.t: Data — urbanisation trends, Census 2011 extremes, projections — Hidden urbanisation

x: Cities occupy about 3% of land, generate around 60% of GDP, and the urban population is projected to reach about 60 crore by 2031.

urban, much higher than the Census figure.

x: The missing middle consists of more than 40 crore Indians who are outside full subsidy coverage but cannot afford private healthcare.
NHP 2017 envisaged higher public health spending, a shift toward preventive and primary care, and universal health coverage.
The NHA 2019-20 estimates were released in April 2023 by Dr V.K. Paul of NITI Aayog (PYQ).

secs.t: Health programmes and missions → launch and target

x: PMSMA was launched in 2016 for pregnant women in the second and third trimesters and provides free antenatal care on the ninth day of every month.
PMSMA concerns antenatal care, JSY institutional delivery assistance, U-WIN vaccination records, and RKSK adolescent health.
U-WIN, launched in 2024, is a digital vaccination registry for pregnant women and children in the 0–16 age group.

secs.t: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and Ayushman Arogya Mandir — features and data

x: Childhood cancer is covered, pre-existing diseases are covered from day one, and women hold approximately 49% of cards and account for about 48% of admissions.
By 28 October 2025, more than 42 crore cards had been issued, with 10.3 crore admissions worth ₹1.49 lakh crore across more than 33,000 hospitals.

secs.t: NEP 2020 — committee, structure, targets and linked schemes

x: ULLAS concerns adult literacy; DIKSHA is the digital infrastructure and e-content platform; Samagra Shiksha integrates school education; NIPUN Bharat focuses on foundational literacy and numeracy.
Both the NCF for Foundational Stage (2022) and the NCF for School Education (2023) were developed by
NCERT
NEP 2020 targets 100% GER
from pre-school to secondary

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — health budget, Family Physician, ABHA, Sanjeevani

x: AP's 2026-27 health budget is ₹19,306 crore (up 9.5%), equal to 5.81% of the State budget, and ranks 4th after Education, BC Welfare and PR&RD.
Under the Family Physician concept, PHC doctors visit villages on fixed days through 104 mobile units.
The village health clinics are located at the
village secretariat level
, complementing the Family Physician system.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — education schemes → year

x: Amma Vodi (Jan 2020) gave annual aid to mothers of school children.
Mana Badi Nadu-Nedu was launched in 2019, Amma Vodi in January 2020, Jagananna Gorumudda in 2020, and Thalliki Vandanam in 2025.
Nadu-Nedu was designed for school infrastructure and its model was also used for upgrading PHCs and CHCs.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All four are identified concerns: declining health-budget share, weak learning outcomes despite enrolment, the missing middle and high out-of-pocket expenditure.
The term ‘missing middle’ refers to approximately 40 crore people who remain inadequately covered by existing health-financing arrangements.
Kerala is presented as a classic example of health- and education-led human capital, reflected in its low infant mortality rate.

rows.title: Indian agriculture - importance, land use classification, cropping seasons and cropping pattern
sub: Group-II M2-A-43: Indian agriculture - importance, land use and cropping pattern

secs.t: Data — importance of agriculture (GVA, employment, growth, exports)

x: Agriculture contributes nearly one-fifth of national income at current prices and employs 46.1% of the workforce according to the cited recent estimates.
Agriculture recorded an average growth of
during FY16-FY25, described as its highest decadal growth rate.
Agriculture supports agro-industries, underpins food security, and the NFSA covers approximately 67% of the population.
Agri exports hit a record $51.91 billion, about 11.86% of merchandise exports.

secs.t: Land use — terms and India statistics (NSA, GCA, cropping intensity)

x: All four are correct for 2021-22: geographical area 328.7 Mha, net sown area 141 Mha (42.8%), gross cropped area 219.16 Mha, and cropping intensity 155.4% (GCA ÷ NSA × 100).
Tubewells accounted for 47.3 per cent, canals 24.7 per cent, other wells 13.2 per cent, other sources 12 per cent and tanks 2.8 per cent of net irrigated area.

secs.t: Nine-fold land use classification — Andhra Pradesh data

x: Net area sown accounted for 36.29 per cent, forests 22.63 per cent, current fallows 8.96 per cent and barren and unculturable land 8.19 per cent.
The earlier APSES 2024-25 reported figure for
was 49.55 lakh hectares, or 30.4 per cent of the geographical area.
Andhra Pradesh's geographical area is
162.97 lakh hectares
, the base for its nine-fold land-use shares.

secs.t: Operational holdings — definition, size classes, Agriculture Census data — Definition and size classes

x: All three are correct for the Tenth Agriculture Census 2015-16: about 146 million holdings, average size 1.08 ha (down from 2.28 ha in 1971), and small + marginal holdings at 86.2% of holdings but only 47.3% of the area.
An operational holding comprises land used for agricultural production and operated as one technical unit, regardless of title, size or location.

secs.t: Operational holdings — definition, size classes, Agriculture Census data — Census 2010-11 (PYQ-tested) and women's share

x: Exam angle: number-vs-area contrast (85-86% of holdings, 44-47% of area) and the census year attached to each figure.
The references correspond respectively to 1971, 2010–11, 2015–16 and 2021–22 provisional Andhra Pradesh results.
In 2010-11, small and marginal holdings were about 85% of holdings but only about 44% of the area, and women operated 12.8% of holdings (PYQ key).

secs.t: Operational holdings — definition, size classes, Agriculture Census data — AP - 11th Agriculture Census 2021-22

x: Operational holdings in AP rose to 96.90 lakh from 85.24 lakh, even as the average holding size fell from 0.94 ha to 0.86 ha.

secs.t: Cropping seasons — kharif, rabi, zaid: months and crops

x: Kharif crops are generally sown in June–July with the onset of the south-west monsoon and harvested around September–October or October–November.
Rabi crops are sown after the monsoon withdrawal and depend substantially on
western disturbances and irrigation
Zaid Kharif is associated with sowing in August–September and includes
rapeseed and oilseeds
, harvested around December–January.

secs.t: Crop classification — food vs cash crops, both-season crops

x: Food crops comprise
cereals, millets and pulses
Groundnut is an oilseed, tea is a plantation crop and fruits belong to horticulture.
Paddy, maize, jowar, bajra and pulses
are reported as grown in both Kharif and Rabi in Andhra Pradesh.
Moong and urad can be grown in more than one season.

secs.t: Cropping pattern trends — India

x: Pulses and oilseeds have stagnant yields, while rice and wheat acreage increased in the three States in association with assured MSP procurement.
Horticulture at 367.72 MT overtook foodgrains at 357.73 MT in 2024-25.
The proposed shift of about 20 per cent of rice area towards pulses and legumes aims to reduce urea use and save groundwater.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh cropping pattern — paddy, foodgrains, expanding and shrinking crops — Paddy and foodgrain area

x: Paddy
is AP's largest foodgrain crop: 20.97 of 37.51 lakh ha of foodgrain area in 2024-25 (2nd AE).
The foodgrain area in Andhra Pradesh in 2021–22 was approximately
41.3 lakh hectares
; an earlier examination key gave the figure as nearly 41.44 lakh hectares.
Andhra Pradesh recorded 37.51 lakh hectares under foodgrains and production of 161.86 lakh tonnes in 2024–25.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh cropping pattern — paddy, foodgrains, expanding and shrinking crops — Expanding vs shrinking crops

x: Cotton
is popularly known as “white gold” and is among the expanding crops in Andhra Pradesh.
Maize cultivation is expanding in the Godavari–Krishna belt because of demand for poultry feed and starch.
Oil palm is an expanding crop in
East Godavari, Eluru and West Godavari
districts.

secs.t: Agro-climatic zones — number, zone → districts, all-India regions — Number of agro-climatic zones - pre- and post-bifurcation

x: Exam angle: answer "six" and name the Survey; count questions have changed their key over the years.
The zones are defined by climate, soil, topography and other factors that determine the best cropping system for each region.
The AP Socio-Economic Survey 2023-24 and 2024-25 gives six agro-climatic zones for Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Agro-climatic zones — number, zone → districts, all-India regions — Agro-climatic zones of AP - names, districts, headquarters

x: Exam angle: matching zones to districts, e.g. Southern zone = Nellore, Scarce Rainfall zone = Kurnool/Anantapuramu.
The North Coastal Zone comprised Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam.
The Scarce Rainfall Zone comprises Kurnool and Anantapuramu, with its zonal headquarters at Nandyal.

secs.t: Agro-climatic zones — number, zone → districts, all-India regions — All-India classification

x: Western Himalayan, Trans-Gangetic Plains and Southern Plateau and Hills are examples of Planning Commission regions.
The coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh fall in the East Coast Plains and Hills region, while Rayalaseema falls in the Southern Plateau and Hills region.
The Planning Commission identified 15 agro-climatic regions with 72 sub-zones, whereas NARP divided the country into 127 agro-climatic zones.

secs.t: Agriculture since 1991 — policies, WTO, GM crops, reforms

x: Bt cotton in 2002 remains the only major GM breakthrough, no new GM approvals have followed it with mustard and brinjal pending, and genome-edited rice varieties such as Kamala have been released.
The Agricultural Renewal Action Plan covered soil health, irrigation and water augmentation, demand management, and credit and insurance.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 51% deficit applied to Andhra Pradesh; India's deficit was 13%, not 51%.
The planned response included shifting towards
pulses and drought-resilient crops
in view of the deficient rainfall conditions.
Strong institutional credit access is the opposite of the stated constraint.
Andhra Pradesh holdings are smaller than the national average.

rows.title: Irrigation - sources, major/medium/minor projects, groundwater depletion, micro-irrigation, PMKSY and watershed development

secs.t: Irrigation — sources and project classes (types)

x: Tubewells
accounted for the largest share, 47.3% of India's net irrigated area in 2021–22.
Uttar Pradesh
has the largest tubewell-irrigated area in India.
Tanks are important in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu because these regions have
undulating hard-rock terrain
Major = CCA above 10,000 ha; medium = 2,000-10,000 ha (minor = up to 2,000 ha).

secs.t: Canals and projects → state and source (places)

x: The Indira Gandhi Canal originates at
Harike barrage on the Sutlej–Beas system
and runs in Rajasthan.
The Nagarjuna Sagar canals serve Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, draw from the Krishna, and are known as the Jawahar Right Canal and Lal Bahadur Shastri Left Canal.
Veligonda Phase-I was inaugurated at
Gantavanipalli in Markapuram district
on 31 August 2026.

secs.t: Schemes and Acts → year and provisions (AIBP, Atal Bhujal, APWALTA, PM-KUSUM, APMIP) — AIBP

x: 99 projects received funding through NABARD’s LTIF, 26.71 lakh hectares of potential was created against 34.63 lakh hectares targeted, and eight of the projects are in Andhra Pradesh.
APWALTA is the
Andhra Pradesh Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002
, which addresses issues including indiscriminate borewell digging.
Atal Bhujal Yojana was launched in December 2019 as a World Bank-aided
Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti

secs.t: Schemes and Acts → year and provisions (AIBP, Atal Bhujal, APWALTA, PM-KUSUM, APMIP) — PM-KUSUM

x: Component A = 10,000 MW decentralised grid-connected plants (0.5-2 MW) near substations; Component C = solarisation of 35 lakh grid-connected pumps incl. feeder-level solarisation.
The current reported coverage is 42.25 lakh acres benefiting 15.09 lakh farmers, with 64% in Rayalaseema; an earlier figure was 37.90 lakh acres.
The White Paper proposed completing 36 projects by December 2028 at a cost of ₹35,555 crore under an Irrigation Action Calendar.

secs.t: Data — groundwater extraction (CGWB) and AP irrigation

x: Groundwater contributes 41% of GIA, is drawn through about 19 lakh borewells, and the State has 38,862 tanks with a registered ayacut of 25.60 lakh acres.
The stage rose from 60.47% in 2024 to 60.63% in 2025.
AP's stage of development is 31.5%, which is Safe; only 12 of its 679 mandals are over-exploited.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The
2026 El Niño drought
has made the Irrigation Action Calendar a priority in Andhra Pradesh.
Solar pumps may reduce diesel dependence but can also encourage groundwater over-draw.
Rayalaseema depends on lifted Krishna and Godavari water and drip irrigation, while Andhra Pradesh ranks first in micro-irrigation.

rows.title: Water resources and river-linking; water use efficiency and command area development

secs.t: Water stress — thresholds, trend and FIRSTs

x: The chronological sequence is 1,816 m³ in 2001, 1,545 m³ in 2011, 1,341 m³ projected for 2025 and 1,140 m³ projected for 2050.
Tamil Nadu
was the first State to make rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory for all buildings.
APWALTA 2002 requires rainwater harvesting on plots of
200 square metres and above

secs.t: Persons → contributions on water and river-linking

x: K.L. Rao proposed the Ganga-Cauvery link (some sources call it a Godavari-Cauvery link).
The Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister requested that the
Godavari–Cauvery link
be taken up as a national project.

secs.t: Water policies, missions and bodies → year and provision — Councils, policies and ministry

x: The National Water Resources Council is chaired by the
Prime Minister
; Chief Ministers are its members.
The National Water Policy was issued in 1987 and revised in 2002 and 2012.
The policy focuses on recycling and reuse, micro-irrigation incentives and community participation, among other measures.

secs.t: Water policies, missions and bodies → year and provision — Missions and campaigns

x: In May 2019, the Ministry of Jal Shakti was formed by merging the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation with the
Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation
The sixth edition launched on 22 March 2025 carried the theme “
Jal Sanchay, Jan Bhagidari: Jan Jagrukta Ki Or
M-CADWM commenced from 2025-26 with an allocation of ₹1,600 crore and uses underground piped irrigation along with SCADA/IoT water accounting.

secs.t: Terms → meaning in water-use efficiency

x: Drip irrigation is approximately 90% efficient, sprinkler irrigation 70–80%, and flood, basin or canal-based surface irrigation 30–50%.
Micro-irrigation delivers water directly to the roots and reduces losses through evaporation and runoff.
Conservation or zero tillage, contour ploughing, mulching and crop rotation are soil-moisture practices.
Zero Budget Natural Farming promotes
mulching and contour farming
as important soil and moisture conservation practices.

secs.t: River links → route, states and features

x: The
Ken–Betwa
Link Project is the first National Perspective Plan link to be implemented.
The Daudhan Dam is located inside the
Panna Tiger Reserve
The three links are Godavari (Inchampalli)–Krishna (Nagarjunasagar), Krishna (Nagarjunasagar)–Pennar (Somasila), and Pennar (Somasila)–Cauvery (Grand Anicut).
Pattiseema is the Polavaram-Prakasam barrage link carrying Godavari water to the Krishna delta, built by the TDP government in 2014-2019.

secs.t: Data — CWMI, CAD and river-linking progress

x: Gujarat
held the top position in the Composite Water Management Index referred to for 2026.
CADWM runs under PMKSY-HKKP; new approvals stopped after 2021-22, while ongoing works continue.
Pre-feasibility reports have been prepared for all 30 links, feasibility reports for 26, and detailed project reports for 14, including one intra-State link.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: On 31 August 2026, Veligonda Phase-I brought Krishna water to Nallamala Sagar.
Polavaram diverts
80 TMC
of Godavari water to the Krishna basin.
The diverted Krishna basin water feeds the
HNSS and GNSS
projects for Rayalaseema.
The principal criticisms mentioned are ecological concerns, displacement and disputes over the concept of a surplus basin.

rows.title: Agricultural inputs - seeds, fertilisers and the subsidy regime, pesticides, mechanisation, extension services
sub: Group-II M2-A-45: Agricultural inputs and technology - seeds, fertilisers, irrigation and mechanisation

secs.t: Green Revolution technology — origins, timeline and phases

x: Although the package included HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, assured irrigation, pesticides and mechanisation, the scientific core was the use of HYV seeds.
Kalyan Sona and Sonalika
were associated with HYV wheat derived from Norman Borlaug’s Mexican dwarf wheats.
The programme became full-fledged from 1966 after the 1965-66 and 1966-67 droughts, foodgrain production fell to 72.3 and 74.2 MT, and India depended on PL-480 supplies.

secs.t: Persons → contributions on farm inputs

x: C.
Subramaniam
, as Union Agriculture Minister, drove the policy shift towards the Green Revolution.
The call for a Second Green Revolution was made by PM
Manmohan Singh
(APPSC 2025).

secs.t: Terms → meaning in seeds, fertilisers and organic inputs

x: The Evergreen Revolution means productivity improvement in perpetuity without ecological harm.
In vermicomposting, earthworms convert organic waste into nutrient-rich manure.
Neem-based pesticides are plant-derived
bio-pesticides
, the safer alternative to chemical pesticides that the draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 and IPM seek to promote.
IPM combines biological control, cultural control and need-based chemical control in order to reduce pesticide use.
The principle “seeing is believing” is implemented through
demonstrations
, along with learning by doing.

secs.t: Acts and regulators — seeds, GM crops and pesticides

x: DRR Dhan 100 Kamala comes from Samba Mahsuri; it is Pusa DST Rice 1 that comes from MTU1010.
Pusa DST Rice 1 was developed from MTU1010 and was due for commercial launch.
The Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules, 1971 set up the Central Insecticides Board and the Registration Committee.
At least 66 pesticides used in India are banned elsewhere, Aldrin killed mugger crocodiles in Kota, and the Supreme Court banned Endosulfan in 2011.

secs.t: Fertiliser subsidy regime — urea, NBS, DBT, neem coating, nano and Soil Health Card — Urea and subsidy size

x: Urea
receives the heaviest fertiliser subsidy.
Budget 2026–27 allocated
₹1.71 lakh crore
for fertiliser subsidy.
India is the second-largest fertiliser consumer and third-largest producer.

secs.t: Fertiliser subsidy regime — urea, NBS, DBT, neem coating, nano and Soil Health Card — Reforms → year and provision

x: NBS provides a fixed per-kilogram subsidy on nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur, announced annually.
Neem coating slows nitrogen release and stops diversion of farm urea to industry.
PM-PRANAM allows States to retain 50% of the subsidy saved through reduced chemical fertiliser consumption.
Fertiliser DBT began as a pilot in
October 2016
(PYQ key), with subsidy paid to companies after sale at PoS devices.

secs.t: Fertiliser subsidy regime — urea, NBS, DBT, neem coating, nano and Soil Health Card — Nano fertilisers

x: The 2023–24 N:P:K ratio was 10.9:4.1:1, against the ideal ratio of 4:2:1.
A 500 ml bottle of IFFCO Nano Urea is stated to replace
one 45 kg bag of conventional urea
Nano DAP launched in April 2023 contains
8% nitrogen and 16% phosphorus
The reported number of Soil Health Cards generated was
25.79 crore

secs.t: Organic and natural farming schemes → year and features

x: Zero Budget Natural Farming was developed by
Subhash Palekar
The National Mission on Natural Farming was approved as a stand-alone mission in
November 2024
PKVY promotes cluster-based organic farming with 50 farmers and 50 acres per cluster, certified through PGS-India or NPOP.

secs.t: Irrigation and mechanisation schemes → components and features

x: The Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana is an
umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2015–16
PDMC was part of PMKSY during 2015–2021 but is now under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY), not presently under PMKSY.
M-CADWM provides
pressurised piped irrigation from the source to the farm gate
Har Khet Ko Pani includes CAD&WM, surface minor irrigation, repair, renovation and restoration of water bodies, and groundwater-related measures.

secs.t: Research and extension institutes → location and role

x: NATP began in 1998 with World Bank aid, while NAIP ran from 2006 to 2014 and was also World Bank-funded.
NAIP components included ICAR as a catalyst for change, production-to-consumption research, sustainable rural livelihood security, and basic and strategic research.
CRRI is located at Cuttack, IARI at New Delhi (Pusa), CTRI at Rajahmundry and ICRISAT at Patancheru, Hyderabad.
ANGRAU
runs weather-linked SMS alerts and diagnostic apps for agromet advisories.
The Meghdoot app for IMD–ICAR agromet advisories was launched in 2019.

secs.t: Data — varieties, mechanisation and irrigation

x: 3,236 HYVs were notified since 2014 against 3,969 in 1969-2014, so fewer, not more.
Tubewells accounted for
47.3 percent
of the net irrigated area in 2021-22.
SMAM subsidised
20.93 lakh
machines during 2014-15 to 2025-26.
SMAM (2014-15 to 2025-26) set up 27,563 custom hiring centres nationally, and Andhra Pradesh had 239 CHCs in 2025-26 (75 of them with Kisan Drones).

secs.t: AP inputs — APCNF, RSKs, fertiliser, pesticides and SMAM — Natural farming and green manure

x: Sunn hemp, dhaincha and green gram are mentioned in connection with green manure seed.
APCNF is run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS) and uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham.
APCNF won the
Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity
Pesticide use declined from 2,650 MT in 2014–15 to 1,716 MT in 2024–25, measured as active ingredient.

secs.t: AP inputs — APCNF, RSKs, fertiliser, pesticides and SMAM — Rythu Seva Kendras

x: Rythu Seva Kendras are village one-stop centres providing a range of agricultural inputs and services.
RSKs handle inputs, soil testing, e-Panta, CCRCs, insurance and procurement.
Soil sampling initially ran through 10,778 RSKs; these were rationalised to 8,489 functional centres.
Permanent buildings for RSKs are coming up under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (
MGNREGS

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Although subsidies helped small farmers adopt high-yielding varieties, they are criticised for disproportionately benefiting prosperous regions and the fertiliser industry.
A urea-centred subsidy regime is criticised for distorting the balance among nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, expressed as the NPK ratio.
APCNF is recognised as a global natural-farming model, and RSKs deliver agricultural inputs at the village level in Andhra Pradesh.

rows.title: Green Revolution - components, achievements and criticism; White, Yellow, Blue and Rainbow revolutions

secs.t: Green Revolution — package components and FIRSTs

x: The package included HYV seeds, assured irrigation, fertilisers, pesticides, mechanisation, institutional credit and MSP or assured procurement.
HYVs are short-statured, respond to fertiliser and water, mature faster and can therefore support double cropping.
Wheat was the first crop transformed by the Green Revolution and Punjab was the pioneer state.

secs.t: Persons → revolutions and contributions

x: M.S. Swaminathan is associated with the Green Revolution in India, while Norman Borlaug is associated with it at the global level.

secs.t: HYV varieties → crop and origin

x: IR-8 was a dwarf rice variety from the International Rice Research Institute in the Philippines and is associated with 1966.
Lerma Rojo 64-A and Sonora 64
were Mexican dwarf wheat varieties associated with Borlaug.
BPT 5204 is the parent of DRR Dhan 100 Kamala; MTU 1010 is the parent of Pusa DST Rice 1; and MTU 7029 is the popular mega-variety Swarna.

secs.t: Programmes → year and coverage — IADP, IAAP, BGREI, Operation Flood — Green Revolution programmes

x: BGREI aims to raise rice-based productivity in eastern India through high-yielding varieties, irrigation, balanced nutrient use and integrated pest management.
Purvodaya follows the logic of improving rice-based productivity and shifting the rice bowl towards eastern India, as envisaged by BGREI.
The Godavari and Krishna delta canals, associated with Sir Arthur Cotton's Dowleswaram barrage, helped make coastal Andhra Pradesh a rice-surplus belt.

secs.t: Programmes → year and coverage — IADP, IAAP, BGREI, Operation Flood — Operation Flood

x: Verghese Kurien worked with
Tribhuvandas Patel at Anand
in the development of the dairy cooperative movement.
Milk output was 239.3 million metric tonnes in 2023-24, and India is the world’s largest milk producer.
Operation Flood was run by the NDDB from 1970 and built a national milk grid on the Anand or Amul cooperative model.

secs.t: Colour revolutions → product and person

x: The Blue Revolution (fisheries) is linked with Hiralal Chaudhuri and Arun Krishnan, Pink (meat processing, prawn, onion) with Durgesh Patel, Red (meat and tomato) with Vishal Tewari, and Golden (horticulture and honey) with Nirpakh Tutej.

Pink Revolution is meat processing, prawn, onion and pharmaceuticals (the 'poultry' in item iv is not part of the Pink Revolution; eggs and poultry belong to the Silver Revolution, but iv is still the only fit for Pink).

secs.t: Green Revolution outcomes — gains, disparities and ecological costs

x: Exam angle: assertion-reason questions linking HYV + fertiliser + irrigation to both higher output and ecological damage.
Groundwater extraction in Punjab and Haryana is 35–57 per cent above recharge, and salinity and biodiversity loss are recognised costs.
The intensive use of HYV seeds, fertilisers and assured irrigation explains both higher output and ecological pressures such as groundwater depletion and soil-related problems.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India's first genome-edited rice, Pusa Rice DST1, is derived from Andhra Pradesh's MTU 1010 and is due for commercial launch.
The Johl Committee proposed shifting
20 per cent
of the paddy area to address the problems associated with water-intensive rice-wheat monoculture.
The rice-wheat monoculture is criticised for being water-intensive and for limiting crop diversification.

sub: Group-II M2-A-44: Agricultural production and productivity - trends, determinants and regional variation

secs.t: Data — Plan-wise agricultural growth and bad years

x: Negative agricultural growth occurred in 2002-03, when drought was a major factor, and also in 2014-15.
The Third Plan recorded 0.73%, while the Eighth Plan achieved 4.68% against a 4.1% target and was the best-performing Plan.
The drought-related collapse during the Third Plan helped set off the
Green Revolution
Agriculture's share in national income declined from 56.5% in 1950-51 to about 18% in the current reference period.

secs.t: Data — growth FY16 to FY27 and its drivers

x: FY24 growth was 2.7%, not 4.6%; 4.6% was the initial FY25 estimate.
Crops grew only 3.5%; fishing (8.8%) and livestock (7.1%) led growth.
FY25 growth was initially reported as 4.6% but was later revised to
Agriculture and allied sector growth was 3.1% in the FY26 advance estimate.

secs.t: Data — foodgrain production records

x: Total foodgrain production reached
376.56 million tonnes
Foodgrain production was 265.05 million tonnes in 2013-14 and the 2018-19 3rd Advance Estimate was about
283 million tonnes
Foodgrain production in 2024–25 was a record
357.73 million tonnes
, equivalent to 3,577.3 lakh tonnes.
Horticulture production was 367.72 million tonnes, exceeding foodgrain production of 357.73 million tonnes in 2024–25.

secs.t: Rank — India's global position in crops, milk and fish

x: India's reported rice production was 150.18 million tonnes, while China's was
145.28 million tonnes
India is both the largest producer and the largest consumer of pulses, with production of 25.68 million metric tonnes as the cited latest figure.
India ranks
second
in the world in silk, along with wheat, sugarcane, fruits, vegetables, eggs and cotton.

secs.t: Places — leading producer state → crop

x: Gujarat is the leading state for cotton, followed by Telangana and Maharashtra.
Chhattisgarh
is described as the 'Rice Bowl of central India'.
Madhya Pradesh leads in pulses, followed by Rajasthan and Maharashtra.
The increase in Telangana's cultivated area was associated with the Kaleshwaram project and Mission Kakatiya.

secs.t: Data — area trends of stagnant or declining crops

x: Cotton
area fell by 18 lakh hectares, and its output declined to 290.91 lakh bales in 2025–26 from approximately 350 lakh bales.
India became a net importer of raw cotton after declines in cotton area and output.

secs.t: Data — yield per hectare by crop and state

x: The cited explanation links lower yields in major rice states with climatic stresses, while Punjab benefits from canal and tubewell irrigation despite low rainfall.
Bt cotton was associated with an increase in yield from 190 kg/ha in 2002 to
480 kg/ha
Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat
have the highest pulse yields, helped by black or semi-arid soils and high seed replacement rates.

secs.t: Terms → meaning — cereal yield, yield gap and TFP

x: Cereal yield is measured in kilograms per hectare of
harvested land under cereals
India's yields of cereals, maize, soybean and pulses trail global averages, whereas
groundnut
is identified as an exception because of semi-arid concentration and improved varieties.
Total factor productivity is the part of output growth that cannot be explained by increased use of inputs such as land, labour, capital and fertiliser.

secs.t: Causes of yield gaps and pathways

x: All three statements reflect the reported effects of heat on agricultural productivity: around 8% yield loss per 1°C, wheat losses of 6–10%, and the loss of about four years of rice and wheat productivity gains.
Balanced nutrition comes through the Soil Health Card; DSR is a water-saving pathway.
In El Niño years, pulse acreage declines by about 2–9%, while output declines by about 6–30%.

secs.t: Missions, policies and committees → year and target crops

x: The mission targets 350 lakh tonnes from 310 lakh hectares, provides 100% MSP procurement for tur, urad and masoor, and runs from 2025–26 to 2030–31.
The Technology Mission on Oilseeds was launched in 1986, NFSM in 2007-08, INSIMP in 2011-12 and NMOOP in 2014.
NMOOP dates from 2014, NMEO-Oil Palm from 2021, and NMEO-Oilseeds from 2024 with a target of about 70 MT by 2030-31.
'Tilhan' means oilseeds, so the Tilhan Mission (Feb 2020, PYQ) relates to
oilseed production
, in the line of the Technology Mission on Oilseeds and NMEO.

secs.t: AP — foodgrain production and yields

x: The kharif paddy yield was 5,612 kg/ha, while the rabi yield was higher at 6,979 kg/ha.
Andhra Pradesh produced 157.59 lakh tonnes of foodgrains in
The foodgrain production of Andhra Pradesh in 2018–19 was about
151 lakh tonnes
2023–24 was the only year of contraction in the Survey series, with agriculture and allied growth of −1.58%.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh has a paddy yield of about 6 tonnes per hectare, among the best, but its foodgrain output fluctuates with monsoon conditions.
India’s rice yield is described as
less than half
of China’s rice yield, highlighting a major yield gap.
ICAR released 184 new climate-resilient or high-yield varieties covering 25 crops.

rows.title: Agricultural strategy and policy - National Agriculture Policy, doubling farmers' income, National Missions

secs.t: Agricultural strategy — phases, definitions and goals

x: The pre-Green Revolution phase (1951-68) saw land reforms, irrigation, Community Development, PL-480 imports and droughts in 1965-67.
The Early Green Revolution phase was 1968–81 and was marked by HYV seeds, initially in wheat, along with fertiliser, irrigation and the New Agricultural Strategy.
Sustainable agriculture maintains the quality of land while meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.

secs.t: Persons → contributions to farm policy

x: Sharad Joshi backed globalisation, whereas Tikait of the Bharatiya Kisan Union and Nanjundaswamy of the Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha opposed the Dunkel Draft.

secs.t: Commissions, committees and policies → year and recommendations — Commissions

x: The National Commission on Agriculture functioned during 1970–76 and submitted its report in 1976 under the chairmanship of
Nathu Ram Mirdha
The National Commission on Farmers recommended MSP at C2 plus 50 per cent, while the Government MSP policy uses 1.5 times A2+FL.
The policy emphasised private participation, price protection, agricultural insurance and a broad-based Rainbow Revolution across farm sub-sectors.

secs.t: Commissions, committees and policies → year and recommendations — Doubling Farmers' Income

x: The seven sources include crop productivity, livestock productivity, resource-use efficiency, cropping intensity, diversification to high-value crops, better price realisation and movement to non-farm jobs.
The approach shifts from “production” to “income” through value addition, clusters, e-NAM and APMC reform, post-harvest infrastructure, livestock-fisheries integration and land-leasing laws.
NRAA provides expert knowledge and coordinates the upgrading of dryland and rainfed areas through a watershed approach.

secs.t: Liberalisation and WTO — changes and effects since 1991

x: Amber Box support is subject to reduction commitments, with de minimis limits of 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries.
Input costs for fertiliser, seed and pesticide rose by over
300 per cent
since the early 2000s, while real farm incomes stagnated.
Bt cotton
, approved in 2002, is the only genetically modified crop identified as approved for commercial cultivation in India.

secs.t: National Missions → launch, crops and features — Missions

x: NMSA is one of the 8 NAPCC missions, focuses on climate-resilient rainfed farming, became a sub-mission of Krishonnati from 2018-19, and has been under PM-RKVY since 2022-23.
NMEO-Oilseeds was announced on 3 October 2024 with ₹10,103 crore and aims to raise oilseed production from 39 MT to 69.7 MT by 2030-31.

secs.t: National Missions → launch, crops and features — NMSA components

x: Exam angle: mission → crops matching; NMSA → NAPCC link; which mission was renamed NFSNM.
NFSM was renamed the
National Food Security and Nutrition Mission
(NFSNM) in FY 2024-25.
RAD, Soil Health Management and Per Drop More Crop are NMSA components.
MIDH follows a 60:40 sharing ratio generally and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan regions.

secs.t: Schemes for better price realisation → objective

x: The
Price Support Scheme
(PSS) under PM-AASHA involves procurement through agencies such as NAFED and NCCF.
Operation Greens was included in Budget 2018–19 and, from 2021–22, was widened from the original TOP commodities to 22 perishables.
Krishi UDAN uses air transport for perishables with the objective of improving value realisation.

secs.t: AP agriculture support — budget, PM-KISAN and Annadata Sukhibhava

x: The 2026–27 Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Budget had an approximate outlay of ₹53,753 crore, included ₹12,153 crore for the Agriculture Department, and represented 33.20 per cent of GSDP.
PM-KISAN is a Central Sector scheme, operative from 1 December 2018, that provides ₹6,000 per year in three instalments of ₹2,000 to eligible landholding farmer families.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Union Budget 2026–27 allocated
₹1.3 lakh crore
to agriculture, representing a 2.6 per cent increase.
Farm unions criticised the absence of
statutory MSP and debt relief
in the Union Budget 2026–27.
AP leads India in
oil palm
: 2.49 lakh ha (48% of India's area; earlier 2.27 lakh ha) and 22.81 lakh MT of fresh fruit bunches in 2024-25 (SES 2025-26).

Group-II M2-A-53: Agrarian distress - causes, farmer suicides and policy response

secs.t: Causes of agrarian crisis → latest data point

x: The stated cycle begins with high input costs, leads to borrowing, crop failure or low prices, non-repayment, fresh borrowing and asset sales, ultimately producing a debt trap.
Rain-fed farming covers about half of the net sown area, groundwater supplies about 64% of irrigation, and 17% of groundwater blocks are over-exploited.

secs.t: Data — small and marginal holdings and their viability

x: India had about 146 million holdings averaging 1.08 hectares in 2015-16, while only provisional State results of the 2021-22 Census were available as stated.
The provisional Andhra Pradesh figures are an average holding size of 0.86 hectares and 96.90 lakh holdings, compared with 0.94 hectares and 85.24 lakh holdings in 2015-16.
Custom Hiring Centres, cluster farming and cooperative or joint farming
are identified as remedies for the viability constraints of small holdings.

secs.t: Data — farm household income, debt and informal credit (NSS surveys, Guntur study) — NSS 77th Round SAS (2019)

x: The NSSO 77th Round Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households was conducted for 2019.
Approximately
50 percent
of agricultural households were indebted according to the NSSO 77th Round.
Approximately
50 percent
of Andhra Pradesh farmers relied on non-institutional credit, compared with about 31 percent nationally.
The next Situation Assessment Survey, to be conducted with AIDIS, is scheduled for

secs.t: Data — farm household income, debt and informal credit (NSS surveys, Guntur study) — Guntur study

x: Tenant farmers had an average debt of ₹2,07,444, whereas owner farmers had an average debt of ₹76,306.
The guard-rails prescribe a maximum of three lenders per borrower and a household borrowing cap of ₹2 lakh.
The comparison is between 7.72 crore operative KCCs and
146 million
agricultural holdings recorded in the 2015–16 Agricultural Census.

secs.t: Data — farmer suicides (NCRB ADSI)

x: The National Crime Records Bureau publishes the report titled “
Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India
” (ADSI), which is the cited source for these suicide data.
10,546 farm-sector suicides comprised 4,633 farmers and 5,913 agricultural labourers, representing 6.2 per cent of the total.
ADSI 2015 named
bankruptcy or indebtedness
as the biggest cause of farmer suicides (APPSC Group 1 2017 key).

secs.t: Commissions and committees → chair and recommendations

x: C2 includes A2, family labour and imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital; hence all three statements are correct.
The National Policy for Farmers, 2007 drew upon the reports of the
National Commission on Farmers
chaired by M. S. Swaminathan.
The special committee on the 2011 Konaseema crop holiday was chaired by
Mohan Kanda
(asked in APPSC Group 1 2012).

secs.t: Loan waivers → year and provisions

x: The AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme was implemented through
Rythu Sadhikara Samstha
Loan waivers provide immediate relief but do not permanently eliminate structural causes of agrarian distress.
Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the expectation of future waivers explains why repeated waivers can weaken repayment discipline and credit culture.

secs.t: Crop insurance — PMFBY, RWBCIS and AP — PMFBY

x: PMFBY became voluntary in 2020, covers pre-sowing to post-harvest losses and localised calamities, and is a Central Sector Scheme with the Centre’s premium subsidy transferred directly to insurers.
From Kharif 2026, PMFBY also covers losses from
wild-animal attack and paddy inundation
, in addition to localised calamities from pre-sowing to post-harvest.

secs.t: Crop insurance — PMFBY, RWBCIS and AP — RWBCIS

x: Under Dr YSR Free Crop Insurance during 2019-24, the State paid the entire premium and CCRC holders were covered.
Both figures are correct: coverage was 34.93 lakh farmers over 28.67 lakh hectares in 2024, followed by 10.63 lakh farmers over 11.81 lakh hectares in the 2025–26 data.
In July 2026 the CM ordered that every cultivated crop be insured for Kharif 2026, making District Collectors accountable for coverage.

secs.t: Income support schemes → State and features

x: Annadata Sukhibhava tops up PM-KISAN, and its Kharif 2026 first instalment was ₹7,000 per farmer, involving ₹3,125 crore for 46.85 lakh farmers.

ADWDRS provided full waiver to eligible overdue loans of small and marginal farmers; the AP scheme covered specified loans up to 31 December 2013; Telangana waived crop loans for more than 25 lakh families; horticulture relief was ₹10,000 per acre subject to a family ceiling.

secs.t: Farm protests — Dunkel Draft (1990s) to 2026

x: Sharad Joshi of Shetkari Sangathan supported globalisation, while Nanjundaswamy of KRRS and Mahendra Singh Tikait of BKU opposed it.
Replacement with a new crop insurance law was not among the stated demands.
The three farm laws were repealed in 2021
Andhra Pradesh farm bodies held statewide protests demanding
MSP procurement

secs.t: AP agrarian distress — tenant farmers, crop holiday and CCRCs — AP-specific drivers

x: The 2011 crop holiday was observed by paddy farmers of
Konaseema in East Godavari
district.
AP-specific distress is associated with higher tenant debt, non-institutional borrowing, risky cash crops and delayed procurement.

secs.t: AP agrarian distress — tenant farmers, crop holiday and CCRCs — Tenancy laws and CCRCs

x: CCR cards provide access to bank credit, insurance, input subsidy and benefits such as Annadata Sukhibhava without affecting the owner's rights.
The
requirement of the landowner's signature
is a major obstacle for tenant cultivators seeking formal credit and other benefits.
Tenant farmers pay rent and bear the production risk, while often lacking land passbooks, Kisan Credit Cards and insurance coverage.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The groups demanded free crop insurance and public insurers only, opposing the premium share under the 2026-27 guidelines.
The reported AP figures were 93.2 percent indebted agricultural households and ₹20,000 annual Annadata Sukhibhava support including ₹6,000 from PM-KISAN, with tenants included.
All three statements reflect the stated debate: waivers versus structural credit reform, tenant invisibility, and the distinction between immediate debt pressure and deeper agrarian risks.

secs.t: Land reforms — goals, types and FIRSTs

x: The principal goals were regulation of rent, security of tenure and ownership rights for tenants.
Compulsory membership is not a feature of joint cooperative farming; participation is voluntary.

secs.t: Persons → contributions to land reform

x: The Kumarappa Committee recommended
cooperative farming
Bhoodan was initiated by Acharya Vinoba Bhave at
Pochampally in Nalgonda, Telangana
The Land Tribunal was headed by the
Revenue Divisional Officer
(RDO).

secs.t: Programmes → region and outcome — Operation Barga, consolidation, Bhoodan, cooperative farming

x: Tenancy reform sought to regulate rent by limiting it to approximately
one-fourth to one-sixth of the produce
Consolidation succeeded in
Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
, while it made little progress in southern and eastern States.
Bhoodan began at Pochampally in 1951, involved pledges exceeding 40 lakh acres, much of it barren, and subsequently led to Gramdan.

secs.t: Land ceiling laws — unit, limits and outcome

x: Pre-1972 ceiling laws generally used the individual as the unit and encouraged benami transfers to relatives; the 1972 guidelines shifted to the family unit.
The 1972 guidelines prescribed a ceiling range of
10–18 acres
for two-crop irrigated land.
Exemptions for plantations, orchards and mechanised farms
reduced the amount of land available for redistribution.

secs.t: Constitutional amendments, Articles and cases on land reform

x: The insertion of Articles 31A and 31B and the Ninth Schedule followed the constitutional issues highlighted in
Kameshwar Singh v. Bihar
The Thirty-fourth Amendment of 1974 and the Sixty-sixth Amendment of 1990 placed additional land laws in the Ninth Schedule, including 55 State Acts, among them Acts of Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Recent reform initiatives and committees

x: Exam angle: "which was not a focus area" - eliminate corporate farming.
The committee was titled “
State Agrarian Relations and Unfinished Task in Land Reforms
The Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016 was prepared by
NITI Aayog
, with inputs associated with the T. Haque Committee.
The Model Act sought to legalise leasing, facilitate credit and insurance for tenants, and protect owners’ titles.

secs.t: AP land laws → year and provisions — Abolition of intermediaries and tenancy, 1948-1956

x: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act was recommended by the
Prakasam Committee
The Act abolished
zamindari and inamdari
systems in the Andhra area and facilitated conversion to ryotwari.
Following the Hyderabad Jagir Abolition Regulation, 1949, jagirs and Sarf-e-khas lands became Diwani, or ryotwari, lands after Police Action.

secs.t: AP land laws → year and provisions — Ceiling and land protection

x: The Bill was introduced under Chief Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, the Act was placed in the Ninth Schedule, and it came into force on 1 January 1975.
The standard ceiling range was 10–27 acres for wet land and 35–54 acres for dry land; some references cite 30–54 acres for dry land.
Plantations, orchards, religious and charitable trusts, cooperatives and Bhoodan lands were among the exemptions.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The stated criticism is that about 28.9 percent of land is with farmers holding 0–1 hectare.
Leasing reform and digitisation of land records have been urged to address continuing problems in land distribution and land administration.
The Srikakulam Naxalite unrest and the droughts of 1966–69 pushed Phase II of land reforms in Andhra Pradesh.

rows.title: Land records and titling - Digital India Land Records Modernisation, SVAMITVA

secs.t: Terms → meaning in land records and titling

x: The National Generic Document Registration System is the ‘One Nation One Registration Software’ under DILRMP, serving sub-registrars and citizens through a common configurable application.
In the presumptive system, registration records a transaction and title may be challenged through earlier deeds, mutation or possession.
The conclusive system provides for a single authoritative title register, unlike the separate records maintained under the presumptive system.

secs.t: Schemes → origin, funding and components — DILRMP and SVAMITVA — DILRMP origin and funding

x: Modern record rooms, survey or resurvey, data entry, cadastral-map digitisation, State data centres, computerised registration and core GIS are DILRMP components.
DILRMP provides for a mandatory gender column in the Record of Rights.
The programme began as NLRMP in 2008, became a Central Sector Scheme in 2016, and Phase 2 covering 2016–26 brought ULPIN.
NLRMP (2008) merged CLR and SRA&ULR.

secs.t: Schemes → origin, funding and components — DILRMP and SVAMITVA — DILRMP phases

x: Phase 1 (2008-16) focused on digitisation, resurvey, maps and registration-mutation linkage; Phase 2 (2016-26) added ULPIN, NGDRS and related integration; Phase 3 (2026-31) focuses on the GIS-based Land Stack.
SVAMITVA expands to
Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas
SVAMITVA uses Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS) for geo-referencing.

secs.t: Data — DILRMP and SVAMITVA progress

x: ULPIN had been rolled out in 29 States/UTs and covered 36.67 crore parcels.
The Department of Land Resources awarded the Bhoomi Samman Platinum grade to
168 districts in 16 States
The target is 6.62 lakh villages at Rs 566.23 crore, the scheme is extended to 2025-26, and over 2.76 crore property cards have been prepared (up from 2.42 crore in May 2025).

secs.t: Acts and rulings on conclusive titling

x: The Act is a model framework and its objectives include fewer disputes, easier credit and lower transaction costs.
The Supreme Court held that registration of a transfer deed is distinct from title and did not uphold the Bihar requirement of mandatory proof of mutation.
The Act was criticised for limiting disputes to the High Court and for issues relating to 22-A listings.

secs.t: AP land records — Bhu Bharathi to Mee Bhoomi and resurvey

x: Bhu Bharathi was initiated in 1992 as a computerisation initiative for land records in the erstwhile united Andhra Pradesh.
The pilot implementation of Bhu Bharathi was undertaken in
Nizamabad
district.
From January 2026, AP issues QR-coded pattadar passbooks with the State emblem: 36 lakh issued, 56 lakh more by March 2027 covering 8,232 villages.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Clear titles improve the ability to use land as collateral and can reduce litigation.
Karnataka's Bhoomi project was launched in 2000 and is recognised as a pioneer in computerised Records of Rights, Tenancy and Crops (RTCs).
The National Digital Land Initiative or Land Stack is described as a cloud GIS system with Bhu-Aadhaar assigned to every parcel.
