rows.title: Non-performing assets - causes, twin balance sheet problem, recognition and provisioning

secs.t: NPA — definitions, classification and types

x: An asset becomes an NPA when interest or principal remains overdue for more than
90 days
The sequence proceeds from SMA-0 to SMA-1 and SMA-2, followed by NPA classification as sub-standard, doubtful and loss.
Agricultural loans become NPAs after two crop seasons for short-duration crops or one crop season for long-duration crops.
SMA-0, SMA-1 and SMA-2 cover 1–30, 31–60 and 61–90 overdue days respectively.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: NPA and stress measures

x: Net NPA is calculated as Gross NPA minus
provisions
Stressed assets include
NPAs, restructured loans and written-off assets
A wilful defaulter has the capacity to repay but refuses to do so or diverts the borrowed funds.
Evergreening involves extending fresh loans to repay old loans, thereby keeping the underlying default hidden.
IRACP means
Income Recognition, Asset Classification, Provisioning

secs.t: Twin balance sheet problem — Economic Survey 2016-17

x: The twin balance sheet problem describes over-leveraged firms alongside capital-starved banks burdened with NPAs.
The Economic Survey
, under Chief Economic Adviser Arvind Subramanian, discussed the festering twin balance sheet problem.
Over-leveraged firms face difficulty investing.

secs.t: Causes of NPAs — factor → effect

x: 2010-15 lending to infrastructure, steel and power led to stalled projects.
Aggressive lending and shocks lead to NPAs, which require provisioning and cause capital erosion, resulting in weak credit growth.

secs.t: Asset Quality Review (2015) and the 4R response

x: The AQR was designed to uncover hidden NPAs and ensure that banks recognised the underlying asset quality problems.
The AQR was intended to end, not perpetuate, the concealment of defaults as standard assets.
The four Rs were
Recognise, Resolve, Recapitalise and Reform
The response included the IBC, recapitalisation and NARCL.

secs.t: Rules → new NPA Master Directions (from 1 April 2027) and ECL

x: Stage 1 involves 12-month expected loss, Stage 2 lifetime loss, Stage 3 full lifetime provision, and loss allowances use the effective interest rate method.
A loan or advance becomes an NPA when interest or principal is overdue for more than
90 days
The RBI is shifting from the incurred-loss model to a forward-looking 3-stage Expected Credit Loss (ECL) model; the 90-day overdue test stays.

secs.t: Data — GNPA, NNPA and PCR trend

x: SCB GNPA peaked at approximately 11.2 per cent in
March 2018
, after the Asset Quality Review.
In March 2026, GNPA was 1.93 per cent and NNPA was 0.39 per cent, described as a decadal low.
PSB GNPA declined from 4.97 per cent in March 2015 to 2.58 per cent in March 2025.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The new NPA and ECL rules are scheduled to be implemented from
1 April 2027
A key criticism of the ECL approach is that
it raises the capital needs of banks
Only
about 13%
of written-off loans were recovered, indicating that low NPAs are partly explained by write-offs rather than complete recovery.

rows.title: NPA resolution - SARFAESI, DRTs, IBC 2016, NARCL/bad bank, Prompt Corrective Action framework
sub: Group-II M2-A-26: Non-performing assets - causes, resolution mechanisms (SARFAESI, IBC, NARCL) and PCA

secs.t: Terms → meaning: stress indicators and causes of NPAs

x: Evergreening occurs when fresh loans are used to repay old loans, thereby concealing the underlying NPA.
The Asset Quality Review exposed evergreening and other hidden stressed loans that had not been properly recognised.
Loan frauds, diversion of funds, weak credit appraisal, slow recovery and corporate over-leverage are causes of stress.

secs.t: Data — GNPA, NNPA, PCR and share of recoveries

x: The March 2026 Gross NPA ratio of 1.93 per cent was described as a
decadal low
The decline in NPAs has been attributed to the 4R strategy, higher provisioning, the IBC and NARCL.
The indicated changes are a move to Expected Credit Loss provisioning and higher risk weights for unsecured consumer credit and NBFC exposures.

secs.t: Recovery forums — Lok Adalats and Debt Recovery Tribunals

x: DRTs were established under the
Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993
, and are also used under SARFAESI.
The DRTs and DRATs handle debts above
₹20 lakh
under the stated framework.
The FY 2024 shares were IBC 48%, SARFAESI 32%, DRTs 17% and Lok Adalats 3%.
Lok Adalats are statutory forums under
the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987

secs.t: SARFAESI Act 2002 — sections → provisions, ARCs

x: Lenders with 60% of dues (75% before the 2016 amendment) issue a 60-day notice under Sec 13(2).
The Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 was based on the
Narasimham Committee
SARFAESI permits banks to enforce security over NPAs without prior court intervention, subject to the statutory safeguards and remedies.

secs.t: Schemes → restructuring, CDR 2001 to Prudential Framework 2019

x: CDR involved joint restructuring of large loans owed to multiple banks, generally outside the court process.
SDR, introduced in 2015, allowed lenders to
convert debt into a majority equity stake of 51 per cent or more and change the management
of the borrowing company.
The Prudential Framework requires a 30-day review after default, makes the Inter-Creditor Agreement mandatory and envisages resolution within 180 days.

secs.t: IBC 2016 — definitions, enactment and FIRSTs

x: Assent came in May 2016.
Insolvency is the financial state of being unable to pay debts when due.
The IBC shifted the framework
from debtor-in-possession to creditor-in-control

secs.t: Institutions under IBC — NCLT, NCLAT, DRT, IBBI

x: NCLAT hears appeals from all four: NCLT orders (Sec 61 of the IBC), IBBI orders, CCI orders (from 26 May 2017) and NFRA orders (from 7 May 2018).
Appeals from the NCLT lie to the NCLAT, and a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
NCLT and NCLAT were constituted on
1 June 2016
under Sections 408 and 410 of the Companies Act, 2013.

secs.t: IBC provisions — CIRP, timelines, liquidation, pre-packs and the 2026 amendment — CIRP

x: Section 29A
prevents wilful defaulters and promoters of NPAs from submitting resolution bids, subject to the statutory framework.
Resolution costs, workmen and secured creditors are placed above government dues in the waterfall.
CIRP ordinarily has a 180-day period with an extension and an outer limit of 330 days including litigation.

secs.t: IBC provisions — CIRP, timelines, liquidation, pre-packs and the 2026 amendment — IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026

x: The amendment includes clean-slate protection, a cross-border insolvency framework and the change in Section 7(5)(a).

The change from 'may' to 'shall' in Sec 7(5)(a) makes admission of a financial creditor's CIRP plea mandatory once default is proved, overturning the Vidarbha Industries ruling, which had read 'may' as giving the NCLT discretion.

secs.t: NARCL and IDRCL — bad bank structure, ownership, funding

x: The National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (NARCL) was announced in
Budget 2021–22
NARCL aggregates large stressed loans, while IDRCL manages their resolution, including sale to AIFs.
Public sector banks hold the majority stake in NARCL, whereas IDRCL has majority private ownership.
NARCL takes over large stressed loans above ₹500 crore, targeting about ₹2 lakh crore of fully or partly provided assets.

secs.t: Prompt Corrective Action framework — full form, triggers, restrictions

x: Exam angle: APPSC GS 2019 asked the expansion "PCA = Prompt Corrective Action".
PCA stands for
Prompt Corrective Action
, a framework used by the Reserve Bank of India to intervene in banks with weakening financial health.
The current PCA triggers are capital, measured through CRAR and CET1, asset quality measured through net NPA, and leverage measured through the Tier-1 leverage ratio.

secs.t: Acts and cases — wilful defaulters, personal guarantors, fraud

x: Personal guarantors remain liable even after approval of a resolution plan, as affirmed in Lalit Kumar Jain v. Union of India (2021).
The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India
proposed stronger safeguards for guarantor insolvency.
The Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 covers offenders in cases involving ₹100 crore or more.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The NCLT bench sits at Amaravati, while the DRT Visakhapatnam bench settles cases at Lok Adalats; statement 3 confuses their locations.
SARFAESI concerns recovery by secured lenders without court intervention; IBC provides collective, NCLT-led and time-bound resolution; DRT is a tribunal-based recovery mechanism.
The Finance Minister described the IBC as “not a debt-recovery tool”; its principal emphasis is insolvency resolution and value realisation rather than ordinary debt recovery.

rows.title: Financial inclusion - PMJDY, MUDRA, microfinance and SHG-bank linkage; digital payments and UPI
sub: Group-II M2-A-27: Financial inclusion and digital finance - PMJDY, MUDRA, UPI and the JAM trinity

secs.t: Committees → chair, subject (financial inclusion and digital payments)

x: The
Nachiket Mor
Committee was constituted in 2013 and recommended comprehensive financial services, including a bank account for every household.
Rangarajan dealt with financial inclusion; Watal with digital payments; Mohanty with the medium-term path on financial inclusion; and Malegam with the microfinance sector after the AP crisis.
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister
N. Chandrababu Naidu
chaired the 2016–17 Chief Ministers' Committee on Digital Payments.

secs.t: PMJDY — launch, objective and features

x: Exam angle: "Which 2014 reform aimed at banking access for all households?" - PMJDY.
The
Nachiket Mor Committee
, constituted in 2013, laid the groundwork for these features of universal financial access.
PMJDY provides zero-balance basic savings accounts with interest, RuPay debit cards and DBT functionality.
PMJDY accounts are linked with the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana and Atal Pension Yojana.

secs.t: Schemes → social security trio: PMJJBY, PMSBY, APY

x: APY replaced Swavalamban, provides a monthly pension of ₹1,000–₹5,000 from age 60, is administered by PFRDA, and excludes taxpayers from new enrolment from 1 October 2022.
The age limits are 18–50 years for PMJJBY, 18–70 years for PMSBY and 18–40 years for APY.
PMJJBY gives ₹2 lakh life cover for death from any cause, at ₹436 a year (revised 2022), for ages 18-50.

secs.t: MUDRA — ministry, categories, limits, refinance

x: MUDRA Ltd was set up as a subsidiary of
SIDBI
on 18 March 2015 and undertakes refinance functions.
The later CDI figure refers to more than 57 crore loans worth about ₹40 lakh crore, with 66% of loans going to women and nearly half to SC, ST and OBC borrowers.

secs.t: SHG-bank linkage — pioneers, NRLM, AP SERP/DWCRA

x: MYRADA
pioneered the SHG-bank linkage approach in the mid-1980s.
The Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas (DWCRA) programme in Andhra Pradesh dates to
and preceded the present SHG model.
AP ranks 1st in SHG-bank linkage with a 36% national share, 99.66% recovery and about ₹32,190 crore disbursed.

secs.t: NPCI products → purpose (UPI, RuPay, AePS, NFS, RTGS vs NEFT)

x: UPI links multiple bank accounts in one application, supports P2P and P2M payments, and operates 24x7.
UPI 2.0 included overdraft linking, mandates, invoice checking, signed QR and a ₹2 lakh per-day limit; it did not impose a mandatory minimum transaction value.
BHIM is NPCI’s UPI mobile payment application.
NACH handles bulk, repetitive electronic payments including salaries, dividends and bills.
The National Financial Switch, or
NFS
, is the largest interoperable ATM network.

secs.t: Policy and Acts — digital payments ministry, incentive scheme, zero MDR

x: Zero MDR on RuPay debit and BHIM-UPI since 1 Jan 2020.
Responsibility for promotion of digital payments was shifted from MeitY to the
Department of Financial Services under the Ministry of Finance
The Department of Financial Services runs the scheme, which provides 0.15% for eligible BHIM-UPI P2M payments up to ₹2,000, with NPCI as nodal agency.

secs.t: Indices — RBI-DPI and FI-Index

x: Exam angle: "DPI base year 2021" is the classic wrong statement - base is March 2018.
The five RBI-DPI parameters are payment enablers, payment infrastructure on the demand side, payment infrastructure on the supply side, payment performance and consumer centricity.
The RBI FI-Index was introduced in 2021, is annual and July-based, uses a 0–100 scale and includes 97 indicators across the stated sectors.

secs.t: Data — PMJDY coverage and UPI progress

x: The July 2026 position was reported as more than 58 crore accounts and deposits of approximately ₹3 lakh crore.
For FY 2025-26, UPI recorded 24,160 crore transactions valued at ₹314 lakh crore.
UPI represented approximately
of the world's real-time payments in 2025.
Despite widespread UPI use, over 90% of UPI users still use cash, making payment behaviour hybrid rather than exclusively digital.

secs.t: Places — UPI abroad, country → year

x: All four are among the 11 countries where UPI is live as of 2026: Cambodia (via NIPL with ACLEDA Bank on KHQR), Greece and Maldives were added in 2026, and Qatar had joined earlier, in 2025.
All four statements correctly describe UPI's international presence, the Singapore remittance linkage, Cambodia's KHQR arrangement and NIPL's wider partnerships.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: payments banks and digital finance architecture

x: ONDC is identified as part of India Stack along with Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker and Account Aggregator.
Payments banks could accept deposits up to the initial ₹1 lakh limit, issue ATM/debit cards and invest in Government securities.
An Account Aggregator facilitates consent-based sharing of financial information, including bank transactions and GST records.

secs.t: Crypto vs CBDC vs UPI — features and FIRSTs

x: The Sand Dollar of the Bahamas was the world's first live retail CBDC and was launched in 2020.
China, Nigeria and Jamaica are correctly matched with e-CNY, eNaira and JAM-DEX respectively.
The stated benefits include programmability, targeted subsidy delivery, cheaper remittances and traceability for tax compliance.
In 2020 the SC struck down the RBI's 2018 banking ban on crypto, so it was not upheld.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 2026 Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha, permits the Centre to modify zero-MDR, and allows the possibility of MDR on high-value UPI payments while retaining free consumer access.

All four statements describe the reported significance of UPI: verifiable transaction histories, credit growth without higher defaults, association with higher output, and 45% of transactions from Tier-2 and smaller cities.

rows.title: Financial markets - money market instruments and capital market segments

secs.t: Money market vs capital market — definitions and instruments

x: Commercial Paper is an unsecured short-term promissory instrument issued by eligible corporates.
CP came in 1990 on the Vaghul Committee.
All four descriptions are correct.
TREPS, or the tri-party repo arrangement, replaced
CBLO
The regulatory statement is reversed: the money market is regulated by RBI and the capital market by SEBI.

secs.t: Gilt-edged market and government securities — types, Acts, participants

x: Exam angle: "Gilt-edged market deals with" - government securities, not corporate paper.
Treasury Bills have maturities of 91, 182 and 364 days and are issued by the RBI for the Central Government.
Treasury Bills do not carry periodic interest and are issued at a discount; Cash Management Bills address temporary cash mismatches; and SDLs are long-term State Government borrowings.

secs.t: Capital market — structure, instruments and AIF categories

x: DFIs (IFCI, ICICI, IDBI, SIDBI, UTI) are a segment.
Convertible preference share
s and partly or optionally convertible debentures are hybrid instruments.
An ETF is traded on a stock exchange and its market price generally remains close to its net asset value.
REITs and InvITs pool income-yielding real-estate or infrastructure assets and facilitate asset monetisation.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: bond types and yield drivers

x: The Sovereign Gold Bond was launched in 2015 and offered 2.5% interest along with returns linked to the price of gold.
Bond prices and yields generally move inversely: when the market price of an existing bond falls, its yield rises, and vice versa.
Higher policy rates, higher inflation and greater government borrowing generally raise bond yields.

secs.t: Data — market depth and FPI flows

x: In June 2026, FAR coverage was widened to new 15-, 30- and 40-year G-Secs and sovereign green bonds.
Private placement accounts for about 98%, the market is about 16% of GDP, and approximately 85–90% is AAA-rated.
Household equity participation in financial savings rose substantially, from 2% in FY12 to 15.2% in FY25.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Budget 2026–27 framework included market-making for corporate bonds, derivatives on corporate bond indices and measures supporting bigger municipal bonds.
The RBI regulates CCPs in the money, G-Sec and forex markets (CCIL), and SEBI regulates capital-market CCPs (NSCCL, ICCL).
Andhra Pradesh planned open market borrowings through SDLs of
₹73,383 crore

rows.title: Primary and secondary markets; stock exchanges, indices, IPO process, derivatives

secs.t: Primary vs secondary market — types and data

x: An IPO is a new issue in the primary market.
In an offer for sale, existing owners sell their holdings and receive the proceeds; proceeds from a fresh issue go to the firm.
India accounted for approximately
of global IPO listings and led the world in the number of IPO issues.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: IPO process

x: In book building, investors submit bids within a price band extending from the floor price to the cap price.
Listing must take place within
T+3 days
of the issue closing (T = issue-closing day); SME IPOs list on separate platforms such as BSE SME and NSE Emerge under the same timeline.

secs.t: Stock exchanges — places, years and FIRSTs

x: BSE received its first recognition under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act on 31 August 1957.
The BSE was promoted by the
Native Share and Stock Brokers’ Association
NSE was established in 1992 at Mumbai and was set up by financial institutions following the Pherwani Committee’s advice.
India INX (BSE) at GIFT City IFSC, 30 Dec 2016, is India's first international exchange.

secs.t: Stock indices — exchange, number of stocks, method, launch

x: Exam angle: "Free-float market capitalisation weighted" - answer NIFTY or SENSEX (both use it).
NIFTY 50 consists of 50 stocks from 13 sectors, uses free-float market capitalisation and was launched in 1996.
DOLLEX-30 is a BSE dollar-linked version of the Sensex and was launched on 25 July 2001.
NIFTY is managed by IISL, now known as NSE Indices Ltd., a subsidiary of NSE.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: market participants, depositories and investor claims

x: A circuit breaker temporarily halts trading when the movement in an index or stock exceeds specified limits.
Convertible bonds or debentures are debt instruments that may carry an equity-conversion feature, making them hybrids of
debt and equity
Tokenisation is a digital representation of claims on a programmable ledger, with benefits of faster settlement, pledgeable assets and better MSME credit.

secs.t: Derivatives — types, committees, regulation and India's options market

x: A futures contract creates an obligation to buy or sell at a fixed future price.
Swaps involve exchanging cash flows; a common example is exchanging fixed-rate interest payments for floating-rate payments.
SEBI regulates derivatives under the
Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956
India’s options market is among the largest by contracts, while SEBI found that nine out of ten option traders lost money.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The STT hike on F&O in Budget 2026–27 was aimed at curbing speculation.
SEBI is still studying losses associated with short-tenure options
BSE is Asia’s oldest exchange, NSDL was India’s first depository, and India INX was India’s first international exchange.

rows.title: SEBI - establishment, powers and functions; investor protection and market regulation

secs.t: SEBI — establishment, Act, composition and functions

x: Tuhin Kanta Pandey
took charge as SEBI Chairperson in 2025.
The stated composition includes the Chairperson, two ministry representatives, one RBI representative and five other members, with at least three of the latter being whole-time members.
SEBI undertakes registration, fee collection, investor education and inspection or audit;
issuing currency notes
is not its function.

secs.t: SEBI regulatory scope — entity → regulator

x: Stock exchanges
, clearing corporations and depositories are identified as Market Infrastructure Institutions regulated by SEBI.
Foreign Portfolio Investors are covered through the
SWAFAT-FI
single-window facility introduced in 2025.
Capital-market CCPs fall within SEBI's domain, whereas money-market, government-security and foreign-exchange CCPs remain with the RBI.
The FMC regulated commodity futures under the
Forward Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1952

secs.t: SEBI powers and the Securities Appellate Tribunal

x: Framing regulations is quasi-legislative.
The Securities Appellate Tribunal was set up in 1995 under the SEBI Act.
SAT hears appeals against SEBI and exchanges, and a further appeal from SAT lies to the Supreme Court.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: investor protection tools

x: The IEPF Authority promotes investor awareness and facilitates the refund of unclaimed dividends and shares.
The 2025 PIT amendment widened UPSI, while PFUTP Regulations address fraudulent and unfair trade practices; both support investor protection.
The initiatives include a new UPI address structure for intermediaries, SEBI Check, the SEBI vs SCAM campaign, and Mission Jagrook, which was launched on SEBI’s 38th Foundation Day.

secs.t: Scams and SEBI-appointed committees → reform, subject

x: Uday Kotak dealt with corporate governance and board independence; K. M. Birla led to Clause 49; T. K. Viswanathan examined fair market conduct; Sodhi dealt with principle-based insider-trading regulations.
The Sahara OFCD matter was associated with limiting private placement to 50 investors and recognising SEBI's authority over deemed public issues.

secs.t: Recent SEBI reforms and the Securities Markets Code Bill, 2025

x: T+0 is an optional same-day settlement mechanism alongside T+1, intended to improve liquidity, efficiency and risk management, including lower settlement and counterparty risk.
The assessment identifies the SME market as under-scaled and lacking
intermediaries
; it does not state that the market lacks regulation altogether.
The Bill proposes to merge the SEBI Act, 1992, the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 and the Depositories Act, 1996.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The ₹1,492 crore SEBI-NSE settlement closed
the co-location case
The
AP MSME Development Corporation and NSE
jointly conducted the SME IPO awareness programme in Vijayawada.
The reported figures for December 2025 were
21.6 crore demat accounts and 5.9 crore mutual fund investors
The criticism is that the SMC may over-centralise power in SEBI.

rows.title: Financial instabilities - crises, systemic risk, shadow banking, macroprudential regulation

secs.t: Financial crises and scams → year, cause, India impact

x: The scam diverted bank funds into stocks via ready-forward G-Sec deals.
Defaults by IL&FS, an infrastructure NBFC, triggered an NBFC liquidity crisis and led to tighter NBFC regulations.
The East Asian crisis had a limited impact on India because of capital controls and low short-term debt; the other pairs are correctly matched.
PMC Bank had hidden exposure to one realty group, while dual control by the RBI and state Registrars weakened oversight.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: sub-prime, shadow banking, systemic risk

x: A Credit Default Swap is an insurance-like derivative on bonds; the seller pays when default occurs, and the contract carries counterparty risk.
NBFCs borrowed through short-term commercial paper and mutual fund money while lending for long-term infrastructure and housing, creating an asset-liability mismatch exposed by the IL&FS default.
Shadow banking means financial (credit) activity by non-bank entities such as NBFCs that lies outside regular bank regulation (UPPSC 2014 key).

secs.t: Systemic institutions and regulations — D-SIBs, NBFC scale-based rules, co-op banks

x: RBI's Scale-Based Regulation has
Base, Middle, Upper and Top
layers.
The 2020 amendment brought
urban and multi-state cooperative banks
under RBI supervision.
DICGC insures deposits up to
Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank
RBI-designated D-SIBs include SBI, ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank, which face an extra CET1 surcharge.
LIC, GIC Re and New India Assurance are D-SIIs identified by IRDAI.

secs.t: Macroprudential bodies → chair, function (FSDC, CFSA, FSR, PCA)

x: FSDC monitors macroprudential supervision and inter-regulatory coordination, and its sub-committee is chaired by the RBI Governor.
The December 2025 FSR discussed external and geopolitical risks and reported that macro stress tests showed banks and NBFCs to be resilient.
CFSA was co-chaired by
an RBI Deputy Governor and the Finance Secretary
(MPPSC 2020 key).

secs.t: Data — bank health and fintech defaults

x: Bank health:.
GNPA 2.2%, NNPA 0.5% (Sep 2025)
→ multi-decadal low.
CRAR
FSR June 2026:
Fintech small-ticket personal loan defaults

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The June 2026 Financial Stability Report flagged risks associated with unsecured lending through fintech platforms.
A credit-deposit ratio of 157.40 per cent indicates that lending was very high relative to deposits in Andhra Pradesh.
The RBI regulates banks and NBFCs, IRDAI regulates insurers, and the Financial Stability and Development Council coordinates among the financial regulators.

rows.title: Inflation - types, causes, measurement (CPI, WPI, core inflation), effects and control measures
sub: Group-II M2-A-29: Inflation - types, causes, measurement (CPI and WPI) and remedies

secs.t: Inflation — definitions and types

x: Core inflation excludes food and fuel and is used to indicate the underlying trend, particularly the demand-side trend.
Skewflation
describes a situation in which prices rise sharply in a few items while prices of other items remain stable and overall inflation is low.
Creeping inflation is below 3 per cent, walking or trotting inflation is around 3–10 per cent, and galloping inflation precedes hyperinflation in severity.
Food inflation is measured by the
Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI)
, which has 10 sub-groups such as cereals, pulses, vegetables and milk.

secs.t: Causes of inflation in India — factor → effect

x: Erratic monsoons, El Niño, crude oil price increases and rupee depreciation can create supply-side inflationary pressures.
The West Asia conflict in 2026 pushed up fuel and input costs, thereby creating cost-push inflationary pressure.
Stagflation may result when higher government spending adds to inflation while industrial output falls and growth slows.
Hoarding, MSP increases and inflation expectations can add to inflationary pressure.

secs.t: Effects of inflation and deflation — gainers and losers

x: Inflation creates menu costs, shoeleather costs and uncertainty that can discourage investment.
During deflation, consumers may postpone purchases, causing profits and production to fall; unemployment can rise and the real burden of debt increases.
An increase in the GDP deflator reflects a rise in the general price level and therefore reduces the
purchasing power of money

secs.t: Economists → curves: the Phillips curve

x: A.W. Phillips
established the inverse relationship between unemployment and wage inflation in 1958.
The long-run vertical curve indicates that there is no lasting trade-off between inflation and unemployment, making statement 3 false.
India’s relatively flat Phillips curve is linked to the large informal workforce, estimated at about 92%, whose weak wage-bargaining power prevents wages from responding strongly to output changes.

secs.t: Price indices → publisher, base year, weights

x: The new CPI series follows COICOP 2018 and expands the groups from
6 to 12
The CPI for Rural, Urban and Combined sectors is published by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
CPI-IW is used for determining dearness allowance for
industrial workers
GDP deflator equals nominal GDP divided by real GDP, multiplied by 100.
WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT (Ministry of Commerce and Industry), with base 2011-12 (revised from 2004-05 in 2017); it has 697 items and no services.

secs.t: WPI vs CPI vs GDP deflator; statistic → publishing body

x: National income and GDP estimates are published by the NSO, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation; the table also identifies the earlier CSO association.
The new WPI is intended to run with a new Producer Price Index for five years, after which WPI is to be phased out.
The
GDP deflator
is the broadest measure because it covers all goods and services produced in the economy, including services.

secs.t: Acts and committees — flexible inflation targeting, RBI Act sections

x: Section 45ZN requires a report when the inflation band is breached for three consecutive quarters.
The debate is whether policy should target headline or core inflation; core inflation is considered stickier and more responsive to policy.
Urjit Patel was associated with the monetary policy framework; Abhijit Sen with the 2004–05 WPI revision; and Saumitra Chaudhuri with the 2011–12 WPI revision.

secs.t: Data — inflation trends and the food-headline-core order

x: In May 2026, food inflation was 4.85%, headline inflation was 3.93% and core inflation was 3.73%, giving the order
Food > Headline > Core
Headline CPI inflation reached 4.38% in June 2026, marking the first breach of the 4% target.
WPI inflation was 9.87% in June and 9.78% in July 2026, far above CPI inflation mainly because of fuel costs associated with the West Asia conflict.

secs.t: Control measures — monetary, fiscal, supply-side, schemes, indexed bonds

x: The APPSC-G1 2024 key credited the Bharat Atta initiative (subsidised atta sold through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar) with easing cereal prices.
When the RBI sells securities through OMOs, money is withdrawn from the banking system, thereby tightening liquidity and moderating demand.
The repo rate influences aggregate demand and liquidity, but it cannot directly remove supply shocks such as sudden increases in onion or crude-oil prices.
In inflation-indexed bonds, the principal and/or interest payments are linked to an inflation index, protecting the investor’s real return.
Inflation-indexed bonds provide a real-return hedge, can widen the investor base and may shift savings from gold.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Low and stable inflation protects poorer households, supports confidence in the rupee and helps anchor foreign portfolio investment.
A key criticism is that headline CPI may reflect supply shocks that interest rates cannot quickly resolve, while policy transmission may also be slow.
Headline CPI was reported above 4% in June–July 2026, with food as the main driver while core inflation remained stable.

rows.title: Indian tax system - direct and indirect taxes, tax buoyancy, tax-GDP ratio, progressivity
sub: Group-II M2-A-34: Indian tax structure - direct and indirect taxes; tax-GDP ratio and buoyancy

secs.t: Terms → meaning: tax, fee, cess, surcharge

x: Exam angle: "pecuniary burden imposed by legislative authority to support government" =
Tax
A tax has no direct quid pro quo.
Surcharges under Article 271 are retained by the Centre and are not shared with States.
The Clean Energy Cess on coal, introduced under the Finance Act, 2010, was renamed the
Clean Environment Cess in Budget 2016–17

secs.t: Articles and Amendments — constitutional basis of taxation

x: Corporation tax, customs, Union excise, CGST/IGST and non-agricultural income tax are Union taxes shared on FC advice.
The Union, State and Concurrent Lists contain 15, 20 and 3 taxing entries respectively, while residuary taxing power, including taxes such as gift and wealth taxes, rests with Parliament.
Income from nursery saplings
is treated as agricultural income and is exempt under Section 10(1); poultry and dairy income are not treated as agricultural income for this purpose.

secs.t: Direct vs indirect taxes — classification and taxable event

x: Exam angle: "which is a direct tax" lists; STT is a direct tax even though collected by the exchange.
Direct taxes are administered by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), while indirect taxes are administered by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC).
GST, an indirect tax on the supply of goods and services, came into effect on
1 July 2017
Direct taxes are generally considered non-inflationary, while indirect taxes can raise prices because their burden is incorporated into the prices of goods and services.
GST is levied on the
supply of goods or services
, replacing the earlier tax-event distinction based mainly on manufacture, sale or provision of service.

secs.t: Types — progressive, proportional, regressive taxes

x: A regressive tax imposes a higher burden as a share of income on lower-income persons.
Income tax rate rises with income.
India's tax structure combines progressive direct taxes with regressive tendencies in indirect taxation, and a higher direct-tax share can improve progressivity.

secs.t: Data — direct vs indirect share; Centre's and States' revenue — Direct vs indirect share

x: The 2026–27 Budget Estimate places direct taxes at 61.2% and indirect taxes at 38.8%, while the FY22–FY25 average direct-tax share was 55.5%.
Excise, customs and sales taxes dominated during the early planning decades, whereas direct taxes have become dominant in the recent period.
Direct taxes accounted for approximately
of total tax revenue in FY 2024–25.

secs.t: Data — direct vs indirect share; Centre's and States' revenue — Centre's receipts

x: Exam angle: "largest source of Centre's receipts" = borrowings; "largest tax" = income tax (2026-27).

Own tax revenue was about 50% of State revenue receipts in FY25, the share in central taxes was about 32%, and the CAG average for 2014–24 was 47% for own tax revenue, 28% for tax share and 17% for grants.

secs.t: Data — tax-GDP ratio: Centre, States, combined, peers

x: The World Bank benchmark is 15 per cent, and India's 2001–2022 average was 16.36 per cent.
The combined tax-GDP ratio of the Centre and States was approximately
19.6 per cent
States' own tax revenue averages about
7 per cent
of their Gross State Domestic Product.
A falling ratio indicates that tax revenue is growing more slowly than GDP.

secs.t: Terms and persons → tax buoyancy, elasticity, Laffer curve, base widening

x: The Chelliah approach favours base widening through more taxpayers and fewer exemptions, together with lower rates rather than rate hikes.
Arthur Laffer popularised the Laffer curve in 1974, and the term was coined by
Jude Wanniski
Both are true and R explains A (APPSC-G1 2024 A-R): a simpler tax system yields productivity gains precisely by removing deadweight costs and distortions in resource allocation.

secs.t: Committees and FIRSTs — indirect tax reform, L.K. Jha (1976) to State VAT (2005)

x: The Indirect Taxation Enquiry Committee headed by
L.K. Jha
in 1976 suggested VAT for India.
MODVAT was introduced on 1 March 1986, CENVAT on 1 April 2000, Haryana adopted VAT on 1 April 2003, and State VAT became nationwide on 1 April 2005.
Service tax was introduced during 1994–95 on the advice of the
Raja J. Chelliah Committee

secs.t: Universal angles

x: PAN-based data can attribute direct taxes to the headquarters of companies rather than to the locations where the income actually arises.
Bhartruhari Mahtab
chaired the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance referred to in the criticism of income-tax enforcement.

rows.title: Direct tax reforms - income tax slabs, corporate tax cuts, faceless assessment, DTC debate
sub: Group-II M2-A-35: Direct tax reforms - income tax, corporate tax and administration reforms

secs.t: Direct taxes — FIRSTs, nature and introduced → abolished

x: Securities transaction tax was introduced in 2004, wealth tax in 1957, gift tax in April 1958 and estate duty in 1953.
Expenditure tax was introduced in 1958 by Finance Minister
T. T. Krishnamachari
on Kaldor’s advice.
DDT was abolished by Budget 2020-21 with effect from 1 April 2020; dividends thereafter became taxable in the hands of shareholders.

secs.t: Income-tax regimes → slabs (data) — New Tax Regime

x: The ₹20–24 lakh slab carries a 25% rate, while income above ₹24 lakh is taxed at 30%.
The Section 87A rebate makes income up to ₹12 lakh tax-free, and the ₹75,000 standard deduction raises the effective salaried threshold to ₹12.75 lakh.
Income tax is a direct tax and is classically progressive because the rate generally rises with taxable income.

secs.t: Income-tax regimes → slabs (data) — Old regime and earlier versions

x: Budget 2023-24 reduced the highest surcharge from 37% to 25% for income above ₹2 crore under the new regime.
The sequence is Budget 2020-21, Budget 2023-24, Budget 2025-26 and Budget 2026-27:
B, C, A, D
In the 2020-21 new regime, 0-2.5 lakh was nil, 2.5-5 lakh 5%, 5-7.5 lakh
(APPSC 2019 key), 7.5-10 lakh 15% and 10-12.5 lakh 20%.

secs.t: Corporate tax and MAT — sections → rates

x: MAT taxes so-called zero-tax companies on their book profits, ensuring a minimum tax liability despite low or nil regular income-tax liability.
Budget 2026-27 reduced MAT to 14% and made it a final tax; no new MAT credit is available after 1 April 2026.
The corporate tax cuts were announced in September 2019 through the
Taxation Laws (Amendment) Ordinance
The Economic Survey 2025-26 described the 2019 corporate tax reduction as the
first pillar of tax reform
, followed by personal income-tax reform and GST 2.0.

secs.t: Terms → meaning (capital gains, angel tax, PAN, AIS, global tax) — Capital gains

x: Rural agricultural land is not a capital asset, so no capital gains arise on its sale.
Indexation uses the Cost Inflation Index notified by the CBDT, and the stated base year is 2001-02.
Angel tax was the tax on excess share premium received by unlisted start-ups above fair value (APPSC 2019); introduced in 2012 and abolished in Budget 2024-25.

secs.t: Terms → meaning (capital gains, angel tax, PAN, AIS, global tax) — Administration terms

x: AIS shows all reported transactions and, from 2021, widened the information earlier available through Form 26AS for pre-filled income-tax returns.
BEPS is an OECD/G20 project comprising 15 actions aimed at combating base erosion and profit shifting.
OECD Pillar Two provides for a global minimum corporate tax of 15% for large multinational enterprises.

secs.t: Committees and persons → contributions

x: Nicholas Kaldor focused on expenditure, wealth and gift taxes; K.N. Raj on agricultural wealth and income; Wanchoo on black money and tax evasion; and Raja Chelliah on lower rates and a broader tax base.
The Kelkar Task Force dealt with direct and indirect taxes in 2002, FRBM implementation in 2004, and tax simplification.
The draft Direct Taxes Code was released in 2009, the Bill was introduced in 2010, it lapsed in 2014, and the Akhilesh Ranjan task force submitted its report in 2019.

secs.t: Acts and laws → year and provision

x: The Act introduces a single 12-month ‘
Tax Year
’ beginning on 1 April, replacing the separate Assessment Year and Previous Year terminology.
The amendment exempts FIIs and BIS from tax on interest from Government securities with effect from 1 April 2026.
Both statements are true, but the Shome Committee recommendation was advisory and did not itself withdraw the demands; the withdrawal was effected through the 2021 Act.

secs.t: Tax administration — CBDT and taxpayer reforms

x: Faceless assessment and the Taxpayers’ Charter were launched on 13 August 2020, faceless appeals followed in September 2020, and the initiative used the stated expression.
Project Insight uses artificial intelligence and data analytics to improve tax compliance.
CBDT is the statutory apex direct-tax body under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963, located in the Department of Revenue and serving as cadre controller of the IRS.

secs.t: Black money disclosure schemes → key facts

x: The Income Declaration Scheme, 2016 operated from 1 June to 30 September 2016 and imposed a total levy of 45%, comprising tax, surcharge and penalty.
Vivad se Vishwas is a direct-tax dispute resolution scheme under the Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act, 2020; a second scheme was introduced in 2024.
FAST-DS imposes 30% tax plus an equal additional amount, producing an effective 60% burden.

secs.t: Retrospective and cross-border taxation — issues

x: Following the Supreme Court's 2012 Vodafone ruling, indirect transfers were taxed retrospectively through the Finance Act, 2012.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance was chaired by
Bhartruhari Mahtab
and sought data on the Act’s impact on collections, assessees and litigation.
Critics have described enforcement as punitive, while retrospective taxation has been criticised for damaging investor confidence.

rows.title: Goods and Services Tax - structure, slabs, GST Council, IGST settlement, compensation cess
sub: Group-II M2-A-36: Goods and Services Tax - structure, rates, GST Council and revenue sharing

secs.t: GST — origin, model, FIRSTs and timeline

x: The roadmap was issued in 2008, the commitment to 1 April 2010 was made in July 2009, the First Discussion Paper appeared in November 2009, and GST was rolled out on 1 July 2017.
The idea was first proposed under the Vajpayee government, recommended by the Vijay Kelkar Task Force, and followed the Canadian dual model.

secs.t: Committees and persons → GST role

x: The Kelkar Task Force was chaired by Vijay Kelkar, the Empowered Committee by Asim Dasgupta, and the Revenue Neutral Rate Committee by Arvind Subramanian.
The Empowered Committee produced “
A Model and Roadmap for GST
” in April 2008 and issued the First Discussion Paper in November 2009.
The Revenue Neutral Rate Committee, chaired by Arvind Subramanian, recommended an RNR of about
15–15.5% and a standard rate of 17–18%

secs.t: Constitution (101st Amendment) — Articles → content

x: Exam angle: Bill number (122nd) vs Act number (101st) is the classic trap.
The 101st Amendment created the GST constitutional framework, omitted Article 268A, amended the relevant Schedules and provided for compensation to States for revenue loss.
Article 269A
provides for the levy and collection of IGST on inter-State supplies by the Union and its apportionment between the Union and the States on the recommendation of the GST Council.

secs.t: GST Council — composition, voting and functions

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 and G1 2024 tested "269A vs 279A" and "statutory then constitutional" - both statements are false.
The GST Council brings the Union and the States together for decisions on taxation and is regarded as an institution of
cooperative federalism

Under Article 279A the Centre's vote carries one-third weight and all States together two-thirds of the votes cast; a decision needs a three-fourths majority of weighted votes of members present and voting.

secs.t: Nature and objectives; taxes subsumed vs outside GST — Objectives and nature

x: GST is a multi-stage, destination-based consumption tax on every value addition, and the taxable event is supply.

secs.t: Nature and objectives; taxes subsumed vs outside GST — Subsumed vs retained

x: Stamp duty is retained outside GST, a common trap.
The conventional classification identifies eight Central taxes and nine State taxes as subsumed into GST.
The concept of
declared goods of special importance
was dropped under the GST framework.

secs.t: Nature and objectives; taxes subsumed vs outside GST — Items outside GST

x: The five petroleum products are crude oil, petrol or motor spirit, high-speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel.
Electricity, real estate transactions subject to stamp duty, alcoholic liquor for human consumption and aviation turbine fuel are outside the current GST levy.

secs.t: Structure and slabs — CGST, SGST, IGST, GST 2.0

x: CGST and SGST apply to intra-State supplies, while IGST is levied by the Centre on inter-State supplies and imports.
Rates are normally changed through government notification on the recommendation of the GST Council, rather than by amending the Acts each time.
The 56th meeting provided for slabs of 5% for merit goods, 18% as the standard rate and 40% for de-merit or sin goods.

secs.t: GST terms and mechanisms → meaning — Mechanisms

x: Input Tax Credit
allows tax paid on inputs to be set off against output tax.
Under reverse charge, the recipient, rather than the supplier, pays GST on specified supplies.

are eligible for the automated registration facility within three working days.

secs.t: State borrowing — Art. 293 limits, highest debt-GSDP States, AP — AP liabilities

x: The composition was market loans 75%, others 12%, central loans 6% approximately equal to provident funds 6%, and small savings 1%.

AP's total debt in 2025-26 RE was ₹6,35,177 crore = 36.04% of GSDP (35.73% in 2024-25), with market borrowing (₹4,83,093 crore) the largest component. ₹5,64,488 crore/35.15% is the 2024-25 RE figure; ₹9,74,556 crore is total liabilities incl.

secs.t: Off-budget borrowing — FCI and NSSF, guarantees, AP corporations

x: Off-budget borrowing is raised by PSUs, SPVs or other government-owned entities but serviced from the government budget, so it does not appear directly in the deficit.
Budget 2021-22 ended the FCI borrowing arrangement with the NSSF and placed the food subsidy fully on-budget.
The 16th Finance Commission recommended stopping off-budget borrowing, bringing existing debt on-budget and widening the definitions of deficit and debt.

secs.t: Institutions → public debt management roles

x: The
Reserve Bank of India
manages public debt and acts as banker to the Central and State governments under the RBI Act, 1934.
The
Department of Economic Affairs
sets the debt strategy and handles external borrowing, while the RBI manages public debt operations.
The PDMC was set up in 2016 in DEA under the Joint Secretary (Budget), as a transition to a PDMA.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Public debt and its servicing burden affect fiscal space; high interest payments, amounting to about 40% of revenue receipts, constrain other spending.
Andhra Pradesh’s debt-to-GSDP ratio is described as stabilising in the mid-30s, while the absolute debt stock continues to increase.
State off-budget borrowings and guarantees can conceal the true consolidated debt burden and adversely affect perceptions of sovereign creditworthiness.

rows.title: Deficit financing - meaning, methods and consequences
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I C-99

secs.t: Deficit financing — meaning, purpose and plan phases

x: Western usage is broader and covers any method of financing a budget deficit, particularly borrowing from the public or financial market.
Fiscal deficit in the Union Budget comprises the budgetary deficit together with the net increase in internal and external borrowings.
The post-Independence need arose partly because India had a low tax base, poor compliance, a weak privately owned banking sector and low domestic savings.

secs.t: Acts and agreements controlling deficit financing

x: Deficit financing is controlled within the fiscal-discipline framework of the
Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003
The FRBM framework bars normal-time RBI financing of the Centre, while monetised borrowing may be allowed under the escape clause.
The escape clause lets the Centre deviate from the target (and allows monetised borrowing) but the deviation is capped at
0.5% of GDP a year

secs.t: Consequences — mode of financing → effect

x: Heavy government borrowing absorbs available loanable funds, tends to raise interest rates and can reduce the funds available for private investment.
A
debt trap
occurs when borrowing is undertaken mainly to service interest on earlier debt, leaving fewer resources for health, education and infrastructure.
RBI financing can raise money supply and demand without a matching increase in goods and services, producing demand-pull inflation.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Interest payments account for 20 paise of every rupee spent and are close to 40 per cent of revenue receipts.
The RBI has urged a shift from subsidies towards capital expenditure, or capex.
Market loans account for 75 per cent of Andhra Pradesh's debt; its 2024–25 fiscal deficit was 5.05 per cent against a 4 per cent ceiling.

rows.title: Fiscal policy - objectives, instruments; fiscal, revenue, primary and effective revenue deficits
sub: Group-II M2-A-30: India's fiscal policy - objectives, instruments and stance
Group-II M2-A-31: Fiscal imbalance - fiscal, revenue, primary and effective revenue deficits

secs.t: Fiscal policy — definition and FIRSTs

x: Fiscal policy uses government revenue and expenditure to influence aggregate demand, resource allocation and income distribution.
The term fiscal is derived from the Latin word fiscus, meaning a basket or public purse.
The Department of Economic Affairs prepares the Union Budget.
J. M. Keynes
developed the theory linking fiscal policy with economic performance.

secs.t: Persons → contributions to fiscal policy

x: The
distribution
function seeks to reduce inequality through progressive taxation and welfare spending, thereby changing the distribution of disposable income.
The stabilisation function seeks to smooth the business cycle and address inflation and unemployment through appropriate fiscal action.
Both statements are true, and expenditure and taxation affect aggregate demand, thereby explaining how fiscal policy can support employment and growth.

secs.t: Fiscal rules → year → target (FRBM to debt anchor)

x: The FY 2021-22 commitment was to bring the fiscal deficit below 4.5% of GDP by 2025-26, and it was met at 4.4%.
The Debt-GDP ratio is estimated at 55.6% in 2026-27 (BE), lower than 56.1% in 2025-26 (RE).
The FRBM Act, 2003 set the fiscal deficit target at 3% of GDP and revenue deficit at zero; it was amended in 2018.

secs.t: Objectives of fiscal policy — what is and is not an objective

x: Managing liquidity and money supply is an objective of monetary policy, not fiscal policy.
Economic growth, equitable distribution, resource mobilisation and balanced regional development are all objectives of fiscal policy.

secs.t: Instruments of fiscal policy — fiscal vs monetary policy

x: Fiscal policy is slower because it generally works through the budget cycle and has direct, targeted effects.
Public borrowing may be internal, such as bonds, Treasury Bills and small savings, or external, such as multilateral borrowing and sovereign bonds.
Public expenditure of the Centre and States together is about
of GDP (ES 2016-17; asked in APPSC G2 2017).

secs.t: Deficits → formula and meaning

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2019 - budget deficit + borrowings and other liabilities =
fiscal deficit
; APPSC 2023 - RD = revenue expenditure -
revenue receipts
Exam angle: definitions asked directly ("total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowing" = fiscal deficit; RD = revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts).
Effective Revenue Deficit equals
Revenue Deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets
Monetised Deficit is the part of the deficit financed by the RBI, involving an increase in RBI credit to the government and creation of high-powered money.
The correct sequence is the 1994 agreement, abolition of ad hoc Treasury Bills from 1 April 1997, introduction of ERD in 2011-12, and its incorporation through the 2012 amendment.

secs.t: Relationship between deficits — which is larger, zero deficits, worked example

x: Exam angle: give a budget table, ask FD/PD/RD; remember FD always equals borrowings and other liabilities.
Fiscal Deficit as a percentage of GDP = (₹4 crore ÷ ₹400 crore) × 100 =
1 percent
Effective Revenue Deficit is obtained after deducting grants for creation of capital assets from Revenue Deficit.
With zero Primary Deficit, the government borrows an amount equal to its interest payments.
A Primary Surplus occurs when non-debt receipts cover non-interest expenditure completely and leave an excess.

secs.t: Financing the fiscal deficit — RBI, ad hoc T-bills, WMA, market borrowings

x: Ways and Means Advances
replaced ad hoc Treasury Bills and are designed to meet temporary cash-flow mismatches.
Deficit financing in the Indian context includes drawing down cash balances, borrowing from the RBI and issuing new currency to cover the financing gap.
Fiscal deficit is financed through market borrowings, small savings or NSSF, provident funds and external loans.
Money-printing or direct RBI financing expands the monetary base and is identified as the most inflationary route of deficit financing.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: deficit quality, twin deficit, fiscal stance, multiplier — Quality of deficit and twin deficit

x: A high RD/FD ratio means a larger part of borrowing finances revenue or consumption expenditure rather than investment.
Government dissaving lowers national savings, and the resulting savings-investment gap can increase reliance on foreign capital and widen the current account deficit.
Neutral policy seeks a stable demand effect, while counter-cyclical policy offsets the cycle and recession policy may increase public spending.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: deficit quality, twin deficit, fiscal stance, multiplier — Crowding out, crowding in and multiplier

x: Crowding in occurs when public capital expenditure creates infrastructure and conditions that draw in private investment.
Capital expenditure generally has a larger fiscal multiplier than revenue expenditure or transfers because it can create productive capacity and stimulate complementary investment.
Crowding out: heavy government borrowing absorbs loanable funds, pushes up interest rates and reduces private investment (UPSC 2026).

secs.t: Deficit data — Union glide path, historical peak and latest

x: The fiscal deficit was 9.2% of GDP in 2020-21, the peak shown in the series, and is estimated at 4.3% in 2026-27 (BE).
The fiscal deficit target for 2026-27 is
₹16.96 lakh crore
, equivalent to 4.3% of GDP.
The revenue deficit was 1.7% in 2024-25 and the primary deficit was 0.8% in 2025-26 (RE).
The earlier gross fiscal-deficit peak was 8.4% of GDP in

secs.t: Subsidies and measures to reduce the deficit

x: Under fertiliser DBT, retail sale is recorded on PoS machines and the buyer is authenticated through Aadhaar; the subsidy is then released to the companies.
Rationalising subsidies through direct benefit transfer is an expenditure-side deficit-reduction measure.
The
CAG and NITI Aayog
have stressed checking that capital-asset grants are not diverted to other uses.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh still runs a primary deficit, indicating that its fiscal deficit remains even after excluding interest payments.
The marginal consolidation from 4.4 percent to 4.3 percent has been criticised as slow and as a factor that could delay rating upgrades.
The debt-anchor rule permits a higher debt ratio than the FRBM's 40 percent level, and critics describe consolidation as slow.
S&P cited general government debt above 80 percent of GDP while discussing India's fiscal position and the slow pace of consolidation.

rows.title: FRBM Act - targets, escape clause, N.K. Singh Committee; fiscal consolidation path
sub: Group-II M2-A-33: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act - targets, escape clause and review

secs.t: FRBM Act, 2003 — origin, FIRSTs, objectives and original targets

x: The FRBM Act was introduced by Yashwant Sinha and enacted in 2003 for fiscal discipline.

The FRBM Act aims at inter-generational equity, long-run macroeconomic stability, elimination of the revenue deficit and reduction of the fiscal deficit, fiscal discipline, transparency and a balanced budget over time.
James Wilson presented India's first Budget in 1860.

secs.t: FRBM Act — mandated statements; what it prescribes and does not

x: Exam angle: "FRBM does NOT provide penal provisions" - the favourite trap.

The Macro-Economic Framework covers macroeconomic prospects and risks; the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement gives rolling targets; the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement sets fiscal strategy; and the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework gives expenditure projections.

The Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement covers four rolling indicators: revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, tax-related revenue or tax-GDP indicator, and total outstanding liabilities as percentages of GDP.

secs.t: Committees on FRBM → chair → recommendations — Kelkar Task Force, 2004

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2017 - head of the FRBM review panel =
N.K. Singh
(Urjit Patel, Sumit Bose, Rathin Roy in options were members).
The Task Force on Implementation of the FRBM Act, 2004 was chaired by
Vijay Kelkar
The Kelkar Task Force emphasised tax reform, widening the tax base and introducing a comprehensive Goods and Services Tax to help meet FRBM targets.

secs.t: Committees on FRBM → chair → recommendations — N.K. Singh Committee — recommendations

x: Debt-to-GDP is the principal anchor and FD the operational target.
The proposed Fiscal Council was an independent, advisory institution rather than a body with binding executive or judicial powers.

secs.t: FRBM amendments and suspension episodes → year → change

x: Exam angle: BPSC 2023 - FD reached
in FY21 (true; statement 1 correct).
The sequence is 2004 Rules, 2008-09 suspension, 2012 additions, and 2018 amendment introducing the debt anchor and clauses.
Fiscal targets were suspended during the global financial crisis, the COVID-19 fiscal deficit reached 9.2 per cent of GDP in 2020–21, and a gradual return path was adopted thereafter.

secs.t: Escape clause and buoyancy clause — conditions and deviation limit

x: The stated grounds include national security, war, national calamity, agricultural collapse, structural reforms with unforeseen fiscal effects and a sharp fall in real output growth.
One escape-clause trigger is a fall in real output growth by
3 percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters
The buoyancy clause requires a reduction in the fiscal deficit when real output growth rises sharply; it does not permit an automatic increase.

secs.t: Fiscal consolidation path — data and the new debt rule

x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 supported delaying strict FRBM-type targets in view of
a volatile geopolitical environment
, while also warning that States’ finances were worsening.

All four statements are correct as stated: the FRBM ceilings included 3% fiscal deficit, 60% general government debt and 40% Centre debt, while the 16th Finance Commission limits were 3% for States and 3.5% for the Union.

secs.t: State fiscal responsibility laws — AP FRBM Act, 2005

x: The Twelfth Finance Commission linked debt relief for States to the enactment of fiscal responsibility legislation through
the Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility
The FRBM limits restrain Andhra Pradesh’s
open-market borrowing
by imposing fiscal and borrowing discipline.
The Sixteenth Finance Commission sought State fiscal-rule reform and a wider deficit definition that would include off-budget borrowing.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Frequent use of the escape clause and repeated postponement of targets are criticised for weakening the credibility of the fiscal framework.
The new debt anchor is 50 ± 1 per cent by 2031, higher than the 40 per cent level associated with FRBM, while repeated misses and the absence of a penalty clause remain criticisms.

rows.title: Union Budget - structure, process, key documents; highlights of the latest Union Budget
sub: Group-II M2-A-38: Recent Union Budget - receipts, expenditure, deficits and major announcements

secs.t: Union Budget — FIRSTs, timeline and records

x: Liaquat Ali Khan
presented the 1947-48 budget in the Interim Government.
The separate Railway Budget began in 1924 following the recommendations of the
Acworth Committee
constituted in 1921.
Morarji Desai presented 10 budgets; 1973-74 was the Black Budget, 1997-98 was the Dream Budget, and Nirmala Sitharaman has presented every Budget since 2019.

secs.t: Persons → budget records and contributions
Budget types and fiscal terms → meaning

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 - justifying the entire budget from the beginning =
zero-base budgeting
Gender budgeting involves making allocations with reference to gender in areas where gender disparities are chronic.
Zero-based budget
ing requires every expenditure item to be justified afresh from zero for each period.
The 16th Finance Commission has pushed output-based spending by linking Centrally Sponsored Schemes to measurable outcomes.
A surplus budget occurs when receipts exceed expenditure; it can curb inflation but may slow growth.

secs.t: Constitutional Articles and key budget documents

x: Article 112 concerns the Annual Financial Statement, Article 113 the procedure on estimates, Article 114 the Appropriation Bill, and Article 115 supplementary, additional or excess grants.
The Annual Financial Statement is provided under Article 112 and covers the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account.
The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of Finance prepares the Union Budget, in coordination with NITI Aayog and spending ministries.
A Finance Bill comes within the scope of a Money Bill under
Article 110(1)(a)
, insofar as it contains provisions dealing with taxation.
Article 112(3)
lists charged expenditure (President's emoluments, debt charges, judges' salaries, CAG etc.).

secs.t: Charged vs voted expenditure — items

x: The President’s emoluments, interest on public debt, and the salary and administrative office expenses of the CAG are charged expenditure.
Salaries, allowances and pensions of Supreme Court judges, and pensions of High Court judges, are charged expenditure.
The specified salaries and office expenses of the presiding officers, UPSC, and CAG are charged expenditure.

secs.t: Receipts and expenditure → classification

x: Market borrowings are debt capital receipts, recovery of loans is a non-debt capital receipt, GST is tax revenue and fees and fines are non-tax revenue.
Wealth tax, gift tax and estate duty were described as paper taxes because they never generated large revenue and are now abolished.
Capital expenditure
creates assets or reduces liabilities
; examples include capital works, loans given and debt repayment.
Developmental expenditure covers
economic and social services
, whereas interest, defence, administration and pensions are classified as non-developmental.
Capital expenditure creates assets or provides loans, such as
construction of roads
, defence equipment and loans to States.

secs.t: Receipts and expenditure → classification — Plan vs non-plan expenditure

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 - non-plan expenditure =
interest payments
Interest payments, defence, subsidies, salaries, pensions and maintenance of assets created in earlier Plans were non-Plan items.
Defence spending is called committed because the scope for reducing it is limited, even when expenditure rationalisation is attempted.
Development expenditure includes education, health, employment and industry; non-development expenditure includes defence, police, interest and administration.

secs.t: Budget process — stages and parliamentary control terms — Preparation and presentation

x: The Budget circular is issued in September, and the Halwa ceremony marks the printing of the Budget documents.

secs.t: Budget process — stages and parliamentary control terms — Six stages

x: Presentation is the first stage: the Finance Minister presents the Budget in the Lok Sabha and there is no discussion that day.
The sequence is presentation, general discussion, voting on Demands for Grants and then the Finance Bill, with the Appropriation Bill preceding the Finance Bill.
General discussion is held in both Houses, committees scrutinise the Demands, and voting occurs only in the Lok Sabha.

secs.t: Budget process — stages and parliamentary control terms — Control terms → meaning

x: Demands for Grants are voted by the Lok Sabha, while the Rajya Sabha can discuss them; charged expenditure is discussed but not voted upon.
On the last day fixed for the discussion of demands, all outstanding demands are put to vote without further discussion.
Article 266 refers to the Consolidated Fund; withdrawal requires an Appropriation Act, while a vote on account authorises advance expenditure for part of the year.

secs.t: Budget process — stages and parliamentary control terms — Appropriation and Finance Bills

x: The Appropriation Bill provides legal authority for withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund, while the Finance Bill gives effect to tax proposals.
Article 114 governs the Appropriation Bill, and amendments cannot vary a voted grant, change its destination or vary charged expenditure.
The second batch of supplementary demands for 2025-26 (Art. 115) carried an Economic Stabilisation Fund of
Rs 1 lakh crore

secs.t: Deficit and tax data — BE vs RE

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 - FD RE 2024-25
was higher than BE 2025-26
(both statements correct).
Gross tax revenue to GDP is shown as
11.5% in FY25, 11.4% in FY26 RE and 11.2% in FY27 BE
Expenditure was ₹53,47,315 crore, receipts excluding borrowing were ₹36,51,547 crore and fiscal deficit was 4.3 per cent of GDP.
Budget 2026-27 maintained fiscal consolidation, with a 4.3% fiscal-deficit estimate and a debt-GDP path, without large tax cuts.

secs.t: Union Budget 2026-27 — theme, size, allocations and rupee data — Presentation and theme

x: The Union Budget for 2026-27 was presented by Nirmala Sitharaman on
1 February 2026
The 2026-27 Union Budget was billed as a “
Yuva Shakti-driven Budget
The three Kartavyas are accelerating and sustaining growth, fulfilling aspirations and building capacity, and ensuring access under Sabka Sath, Sabka Vikas.

secs.t: Union Budget 2026-27 — theme, size, allocations and rupee data — Ministry-wise allocations

x: The
Ministry of Defence
received the highest allocation, amounting to ₹7,84,678 crore.
Mission VATSALYA received
Rs 900 crore
in Budget 2021-22 and concerns child protection and welfare.
Every ministry, barring a few exempted ministries, earmarks
of Gross Budgetary Support for the North-Eastern region since 1998-99.
The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports got
Rs 3,794.30 crore
in Budget 2025-26.

secs.t: Union Budget 2026-27 — theme, size, allocations and rupee data — Rupee comes from / rupee goes to

x: Borrowings and other liabilities
account for the largest share, at 24 paise of each rupee.
Income tax contributes
21 paise
of every rupee in the stated receipt composition.
The
States' share of taxes and duties
is the largest outflow, accounting for 22 paise.
Interest payments account for
20 paise
of each rupee in the stated expenditure distribution.

secs.t: Union Budget 2026-27 — schemes, initiatives and tax proposals

x: VB-G RAM G
replaced MGNREGA and received an allocation of ₹95,692 crore.
Seven
high-speed rail corridors were announced in the Union Budget 2026-27.
The Gender Budget was ₹5.01 lakh crore, or 9.37 per cent, described as the highest ever.
Budget 2025-26 included
personal income-tax restructuring effective from April 2025 and GST 2.0 in September 2025

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Budget is the principal instrument of fiscal policy and performs the functions of resource allocation, income redistribution and economic stabilisation.
The States’ combined fiscal deficit was 3.2 percent of GDP in FY25, and 18 States exceeded the 3 percent limit in FY24.
The CAG flagged Andhra Pradesh’s revenue deficit for three years, and revenue receipts were only 48 percent of the Budget Estimates by November 2025.

rows.title: Economic Survey - structure and key themes of the latest Survey

secs.t: Economic Survey — preparer, FIRSTs and format

x: Presentation of the Economic Survey before the Union Budget is a convention, whereas Article 112 relates to the Annual Financial Statement.
The Economic Survey 2025-26 was reconfigured into
17 chapters
, described as 16 chapters with Chapter 16 divided into two parts.
Artificial intelligence and urbanisation
were added as chapters in the reconfigured Economic Survey 2025-26.

secs.t: Chief Economic Advisers → Survey editions and ideas

x: Exam angle: match the concept to the Survey year; the 2016-17 edition is the most-asked (UBI, twin balance sheet, property tax, toilets).
The
Economic Survey discussed behavioural economics and the idea of using nudges, describing people as Homo Sapiens rather than purely rational Homo Economicus.
The 2017-18 Survey dealt with gender and climate change and agriculture; 2019-20 introduced Thalinomics; 2020-21 presented the Bare Necessities Index; and 2023-24 emphasised ‘letting go’.

secs.t: Survey terms and indices → meaning

x: Twin balance sheet = over-leveraged corporates + stressed banks, choking private capex.
ES 2016-17 used satellite imagery to estimate
Bengaluru
's property-tax gap between actual collection and potential (APPSC-G1 2017 key).
ES 2016-17 noted that most women in households without toilets
had to travel long distances for a toilet facility
(APPSC-G1 2017 key).

secs.t: Economic Survey 2025-26 — theme, chapters and statistical reforms

x: The Systemic Shock Cascade scenario was assigned a probability of 10 to 20 per cent and was described as worse than the 2008 crisis.
The distinction between Sreya and Preya was linked to the
Katha Upanishad
The Survey tied faster release of estimates to AI and CAPI (Computer-Assisted Personal Interviewing).

secs.t: Economic Survey 2025-26 — data

x: Private Final Consumption Expenditure was 61.5 per cent of GDP, its highest share since FY12, while Gross Fixed Capital Formation remained steady at 30 per cent.
All three indicators are correctly stated for H1 FY26: CAD at 0.8 per cent of GDP, forex cover above 11 months of imports, and rupee depreciation of approximately 6.5 per cent.

secs.t: Reforms and recurring frameworks — deregulation, Viksit Bharat, Ease of Living

x: ES 2023-24 argued for 'letting go' and lighter licensing/inspection on MSMEs.
Infrastructure is the growth pillar of Viksit Bharat @2047, not a constraint.
Ease of Doing Business and Ease of Living
was identified as a pillar in Budget 2026-27.
The Bare Necessities Index in the Economic Survey 2020-21 measured Ease of Living at the
State level

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The survey found that half of the firms felt that strong macroeconomic growth was not fully reaching their businesses.
The Andhra Pradesh Socio-Economic Survey is associated with the
Planning Department
and is tabled in both Houses along with the State Budget.
The UN ESCAP Economic Survey 2026 is a separate Asia-Pacific regional report from ESCAP, which is headquartered in Bangkok.

etres.

; one old key says Section 30, and some CA notes say Section 89 - both wrong); statement-pairs on 90(1)-(4).

The foreign expert panel (6th visit, with CWC) reviewed Gap-1, Gap-2 and the D-wall.

sub: Group-II M2-A-86: Irrigation in Andhra Pradesh - sources, major projects and micro-irrigation

secs.t: Irrigation — classification of projects and FIRSTs

x: Eluru
recorded the largest GIA at 2.39 lakh hectares, followed by Ananthapuramu at 2.04 lakh hectares and Nandyal at 1.98 lakh hectares.
In Andhra Pradesh, minor irrigation covers schemes with an ayacut up to
5,000 acres
Nationally, minor irrigation means CCA up to 2,000 ha, medium 2,000–10,000 ha and major above 10,000 ha.
Undulating plateau relief and impervious rocks favour tanks.

secs.t: Data — irrigated area, potential and sources — GIA/GCA share

x: The gross irrigated area was 32.71 lakh hectares and the net irrigated area was 26.03 lakh hectares.
The PYQ (2021) figure for AP's GIA/GCA is
, per AP Economy in Brief 2020.

secs.t: Data — irrigated area, potential and sources — Sources of irrigation

x: Groundwater, represented mainly by wells and tube wells, was the largest source of GIA.
Tube wells accounted for 47.3% of India's net irrigated area in 2021-22, followed by canals at 24.7%, other wells at 13.2% and other sources at 12%.

secs.t: Projects → river, districts and key facts

x: The Telugu Ganga project carries Krishna surplus through the Srisailam-Somasila-Kandaleru-Poondi system, supplying drinking water to Chennai and irrigation water to Rayalaseema and Nellore.
The Veligonda Project draws from the Srisailam reservoir through tunnels and serves
Prakasam, Nellore and YSR Kadapa
districts.
Veligonda takes Krishna water from Srisailam by gravity through tunnels in the Nallamala range and conveys it into Nallamala Sagar.
Veligonda Phase-I releases 10.70 TMC into Nallamala Sagar, irrigates about 1.19 lakh acres and supplies drinking water to approximately 4 lakh people.

secs.t: Pattiseema and Polavaram — features and status

x: Exam angle: "Pattiseema is a lift irrigation project" and "not true" statement sets on its canal and purpose.
Pattiseema had 24 pumps, was built during 2014-19, commissioned in 2015 and helped supply the Krishna delta during the 2026 El Niño deficit.
Pattiseema is a lift irrigation scheme on the Godavari, its water serves Krishna delta farmers, and it is temporary until Polavaram's gravity flow starts - all true.

secs.t: Persons and governments → projects; plan-wise launch

x: The Polavaram dam was initially proposed as “
Ramapada Sagaram
”; the proposal is credited to Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy.

Prakasam Barrage belongs to the First-to-Second Plan (a-ii); Srisailam was sanctioned in the Third Plan (b-i); Telugu Ganga (1983) is a Sixth Plan project (c-iv); Jalayagnam (2004) falls in the Tenth Plan (d-iii).

secs.t: Acts, boards and tribunals on irrigation

x: The Eleventh Schedule lists
Handri-Neeva, Telugu Ganga, Galeru-Nagari, Veligonda, Kalwakurthy and Nettempadu
for completion with the existing water-sharing arrangements.
APWALTA - the
AP Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002
- is AP's law against indiscriminate borewell digging (PYQ 2018) and also mandates rainwater harvesting on premises of 200 sq m or more.

secs.t: Schemes and programmes → aim and data — Jalayagnam

x: Jalayagnam aimed to irrigate one crore acres and stabilise 21 lakh acres; 41 major and 25 minor projects were proposed.
Neeru-Meeru was a watershed and rainwater-harvesting drive intended to raise groundwater levels.
Neeru-Chettu was launched on
2 October 2014
Jaladhara-Jalaharathi is
a 100-day water-conservation plan launched in April 2026

secs.t: Schemes and programmes → aim and data — APMIP and micro-irrigation

x: 1.90 lakh hectares were covered during the stated period, Andhra Pradesh ranked first nationally in 2024–25, and SC/ST beneficiaries receive 100% subsidy.
The target is micro-irrigation over 35% of gross sown area by 2030 and 50% by 2047.
The Micro Irrigation Fund is maintained through NABARD with a ₹10,000 crore corpus, and Andhra Pradesh is among the eight States funded.

secs.t: Terms → meaning

x: APFAMGS promotes farmer-led collection of rainfall and well-level data, crop-water budgeting on a hydrological-unit basis and voluntary regulation of pumping.
APFAMGS was an FAO-supported NGO initiative in drought-prone districts and used hydrological-unit-based crop-water budgeting by farmers.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The proposal was to complete Polavaram before the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu and to divert about 200 TMC of Godavari water to the Nagarjunasagar ayacut.
PMKSY includes AIBP, Har Khet Ko Pani, Watershed and Per Drop More Crop.
The White Paper aims to
complete 36 projects by December 2028 at Rs 35,555 crore
, backed by an Irrigation Action Calendar.

of GVA at current prices in 2025-26.

Capital uncertainty, the absence of a ready administrative set-up and agitations reduced FDI and private investment.
No mature power grids, logistics parks or ready factories raised costs.

secs.t: IT and e-governance — FIRSTs and persons → contributions

x: Exam angle: chronology (CARD, then eSeva, then MeeSeva) and "first in India" claims.
APSFL is described as India’s first State-owned Internet Service Provider and also functions as a telecom and IPTV provider.
The first ISM-framework unit cleared was an OSAT project by
Advanced System in Package Technologies
, with an investment of ₹2,388 crore at Tarluvada, Visakhapatnam.

x: Exam angle: a GCC is a multinational's own offshore unit, not a third-party vendor; that is why the policy is named for it.
The
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
(MeitY) is the custodian of the IT Act, 2000, which was last amended in 2008.
A GCC is an offshore unit owned and operated by a multinational company for its own capabilities and operations, rather than a third-party vendor.

secs.t: Electronics, data centre and drone policies → targets — Electronics policies

x: The ESDM Policy 2021-24 provides 100 per cent reimbursement of stamp duty, transfer duty and registration fee in the Zone A/B incentive.
The stated support for component makers consists of advance and matching incentives, interim support and plug-and-play facilities.
The
Electronics Components Manufacturing Policy 2025
is intended to develop a component ecosystem.

x: Andhra Pradesh targets up to 1 GW of additional data-centre capacity, while Gujarat targets 7.5 GW.
