secs.t: E-governance platforms → year and feature

x: The correct sequence is APSWAN in November 2010, MeeSeva in November 2011, APSFL incorporation in October 2015, and Village and Ward Secretariats in October 2019.
CARD
, or Computer-aided Administration of Registration Department, was introduced in 1998 for computerised land and property registration.
MeeSeva training during its first year was delivered through television in partnership with
MANA TV

secs.t: Network backbone — AP State FiberNet, BharatNet, APSWAN

x: APSFL was incorporated in October 2015 and launched on 27 December 2017.
Phase-I comprises 24,000 km of fibre on an IP-MPLS ring, and its Network Operations Centre is at Visakhapatnam.
The triple-play model provides
internet, IPTV and voice
services.
APSFL is the state implementing agency, and the Phase-II rollout covers 54,502 km and 11,254 Gram Panchayats.

secs.t: e-Pragati — whole-of-government platform

x: The e-Pragati framework consisted of
14 packages and 72 projects
across 33 departments.
All three statements are correct. e-Pragati interconnects departmental systems, provides a single-window interface for several departments and follows the Seva model.
e-Pragati was launched under CM
N. Chandrababu Naidu
during 2014-19 (APPSC 2021 key, asked twice).
e-Pragati aims at faceless, paperless, cashless governance by integrating departments on a single window.

secs.t: RTGS — command centre, data lake, Mana Mitra and tools

x: The RTGS Command and Control Centre uses AI, big data, GIS, IoT and dashboards.
The State Data Lake serves as a single source of truth for more than 40 departments and approximately 400 applications.
RTGS has broad governance, analytics and early-warning functions; it is not confined to monitoring IT exports.

secs.t: Bodies → year and role — innovation, cyber security, NIC solutions

x: APTS dates from 1986 and is the nodal body for IT procurement, cyber security, digital certificates and Aadhaar.
APEITA handles policy implementation and investment promotion, APSAC works in remote sensing, GIS and drones, and IIDT at Tirupati develops AI, VLSI and cybersecurity skills.
SPARK, Catalyst, Velocity Labs and Innotribe
are programmes associated with the AP Innovation Society and the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub.

is the IT/ITES SEZ (PYQ 2022).

are also located in Tirupati in association with the Tirupati cluster area.

x: The inauguration of the Google AI data-centre project is scheduled for
28 September 2028
Visakhapatnam
is the global AI hub city (PYQ 2025; APPSC 2025 key), with Google's 1 GW AI data centre at Tarluvada.
About US$15 bn (₹1.35 lakh crore), run by Raiden Infotech with AdaniConneX and Airtel Nxtra.

secs.t: Places → IT parks, SEZs, EMCs, data centres and tech clusters — Amaravati Quantum Valley (AQV) and state tech clusters

x: Data & AI City is at Visakhapatnam, Quantum Valley at Amaravati, the Green Hydrogen cluster at Kakinada and Drone City at Orvakal in Kurnool.

secs.t: Places → IT parks, SEZs, EMCs, data centres and tech clusters — Drone City and drone summit

Mangalagiri
, while the associated drone show was held at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada.

Airbound
for the Amaravati Capital Region Drone Delivery Network.

x: After bifurcation in 2014, residual Andhra Pradesh's IT sector was described as having started from zero.

secs.t: Terms and acronyms → meaning

x: LIFT means Land Incentive for Tech Hubs; GCC means Global Capability Centre; RTIH means Ratan Tata Innovation Hub; OSAT means Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test.

The Data Center Policy targets up to 1 GW additional capacity; LIFT offers land incentives; the Components Policy develops the component ecosystem; and the ESDM Policy provides Zone A/B reimbursement incentives.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Naidu's 1990s IT push contributed to HITEC City's development, and after 2014 Andhra Pradesh rebuilt its IT base around Visakhapatnam.
The 1995-2004 period was associated with
HITEC City, eSeva and the SMART governance model
Google's Vizag AI hub is associated with 1 GW, whereas the APCRDA call referred to a 9 GW data-centre ecosystem.

rows.title: Approaches and initiatives in AP agriculture - APCNF/ZBNF, horticulture, aquaculture, allied sectors
sub: Group-II M2-A-85: Cropping pattern of Andhra Pradesh - major crops, area, production and productivity
Group-II M2-A-91: Strategies, schemes and programmes for the agricultural sector in Andhra Pradesh
Group-II M2-A-92: Natural farming in Andhra Pradesh (APCNF/ZBNF) - approach, coverage and outcomes
Group-II M2-A-93: Horticulture in Andhra Pradesh - major crops, area, production and schemes
Group-II M2-A-94: Animal husbandry and dairying in Andhra Pradesh - livestock, milk production and schemes
Group-II M2-A-95: Fisheries and aquaculture in Andhra Pradesh - marine and inland, exports and schemes

secs.t: AP agriculture — FIRSTs, largest and ranks — FIRSTs and largest

x: Paddy
has the largest area of any crop in AP (PYQ 2018): 20.97 lakh ha in 2024-25, about 56% of the food-grain area.
Cotton
('white gold') is the commercial crop whose area expanded most (PYQ 2022).
The Godavari Mega Aqua Food Park at
Tundurru in West Godavari
was India’s first operational Mega Aqua Food Park.

secs.t: AP agriculture — FIRSTs, largest and ranks — Horticulture ranks

x: Oil palm
was ranked first in productivity in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26.
Andhra Pradesh ranks fourth in coffee production, and 100% of its coffee production comes from Araku Valley.
Both statements are correct, as keyed in APPSC Group 2 (2025): AP is 1st in oil palm productivity and 2nd in mango production.

secs.t: AP agriculture — FIRSTs, largest and ranks — Livestock product ranks

x: The first option is incorrect because 2,739 crore eggs refers to egg production, not meat.
The correct unit is
crore eggs
; the printing of lakh eggs is an erroneous unit representation.
Andhra Pradesh ranked first in egg production, at 2,548.74 crore eggs, and fifth in meat production, at 10.68 lakh metric tonnes.

secs.t: Data — land use, net sown area and cropping intensity

x: Exam angle: land-use figures are asked with the year and the report named (NITI Aayog / SES); always tie the number to its year.
Net sown area fell to
49.55 lakh hectares
in 2023-24, a decline of about one-quarter from 2008-09.
The net area sown was 59.14 lakh hectares, constituting 36.29 per cent, while forests constituted 22.63 per cent of land use.

secs.t: Data — food grains, paddy and seasons — Food grains and paddy

x: Paddy covered 20.97 lakh hectares out of the 37.51 lakh hectares under food grains, which is approximately
Food-grain area was 41.44 lakh hectares in 2021-22, 33.24 lakh hectares in 2023-24 and 37.51 lakh hectares in 2024-25.
The Economic Survey 2025-26 reported that yields of major crops increased nationally, but they remained below global averages.

secs.t: Data — food grains, paddy and seasons — Kharif vs rabi

x: The 2024-25 rise in food-grain area was 12.85%, following an 11.7% rainfall surplus.
Kharif 2026 was described as a drought season, with all 28 districts in deficit, 25 deficit and 3 large-deficit, and sowing at about 61% of normal by 19 August.

secs.t: Places → crops, research institutes and varieties — Crop → dominant region/district

x: Palasa in Srikakulam is known as the “White Gold City” because of its association with
cashew
Bananas are exported from Tadipatri in Anantapur district through refrigerated trains.
The Godavari delta, covering East and West Godavari, is the main rice-growing area and an aquaculture hub.
The Tobacco Board is located at
Guntur
, although Prakasam and Nellore are the main FCV tobacco districts.

secs.t: Places → crops, research institutes and varieties — Research institutes → place

x: Exam angle: institute → place matching (Pedavegi vs Razole, Maruteru, Bapatla).
Officials advised stopping Bondalu paddy cultivation because Kerala, its earlier buyer, had started producing the rice itself.
The Kuppam centre produces
grafted vegetable seedlings
; 3,49,364 seedlings were produced in 2025-26.
Kuppam is the Indo-Israel vegetable centre, while the new vegetable and spice centre is at Gundlapalli in Nekarikallu mandal of Palnadu district.
The ICAR Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research is located at
Pedavegi in the West Godavari region

secs.t: Persons → contributions; separate agriculture budget

x: The Separate Agriculture and Allied Budget for 2026-27 is approximately
₹53,753 crore
Undivided Andhra Pradesh first presented a separate agriculture budget in 2013.
K. Atchannaidu presented the 2026-27 Agriculture & Allied Budget, for the third time.

secs.t: Changes — cropping pattern shifts and growth engines

x: The cropping pattern is shifting towards
fruits, vegetables, flowers and spices
because of their profitability and export potential.
The 11 crops include paddy, maize, jowar, bajra, ragi, redgram, blackgram, bengalgram, groundnut, sunflower and sesamum.
Andhra Pradesh has set a target of
₹3 lakh crore
horticulture GVA by 2029-30, covering 22 growth-engine crops.
MIDH covers horticultural crops including fruits and bamboo; it does not cover all cereal crops without exception.

secs.t: Farmer income-support schemes → amount and domain

x: Exam angle: amount traps (₹13,500 vs ₹20,000 vs Telangana's ₹12,000 per acre) and "tenant farmers included - true".
During 2019–2024, YSR Rythu Bharosa-PM Kisan provided ₹13,500 per family per year and covered owners, tenant farmers and RoFR cultivators.
Annadata Sukhibhava-PM Kisan provides ₹20,000 per farmer family annually, including ₹14,000 from the State and ₹6,000 under PM-KISAN from the Centre.
Annadata Sukhibhava-PM Kisan operates from 2024–25 onwards, covers farmer families including CCRC-holding tenants, and includes the ₹6,000 PM-KISAN component for landholders.

secs.t: Farmer service and extension institutions — Rythu Bazars, RSKs, ATMA, Polambadi — Rythu Bazar

x: A Rythu Bazar is run by an Estate Officer, while a regulated yard is run by a Market Committee.
Rythu Bazars facilitate direct sale from farmers to consumers; 129 are functioning and 10 are under construction.
Rythu Bazar prices are fixed at about 25% above wholesale prices but below local retail prices.

secs.t: Farmer service and extension institutions — Rythu Bazars, RSKs, ATMA, Polambadi — RBKs / RSKs

x: Rythu Bharosa Kendras were established in 2020, and
10,778 centres
were set up beside village secretariats.
The centres are now called Rythu Seva Kendras, and the rationalised number of functional RSKs is 8,489.
RSKs provide agricultural services such as soil testing, e-Panta, CCRC issuance, input subsidies, crop insurance, drone awareness and procurement.
ATMA is district-level and demand-driven, prepares the SREP, and operates under a 60:40 centrally sponsored funding pattern.

secs.t: Acts → year and provision — tenancy, aquaculture, co-operatives

x: CCRCs facilitate loans, insurance, MSP and scheme access, but they do not confer permanent ownership on tenants.
CCRCs are issued under the AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019 and are valid for 11 months.
Coastal farms within 2 km of the High Tide Line are regulated by the Coastal Aquaculture Authority under the CAA Act, 2005.

secs.t: Farm support tools → feature — soil health, e-Crop, farm ponds, DBT of farm power

x: e-Crop booking creates a digital crop record that serves as the basis for insurance, MSP procurement, input subsidy and loss assessment.
Farm ponds under Panta Sanjeevani were dug through convergence with the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.
Srikakulam district
was selected for the 2020 pilot involving smart meters on farm pump-sets and direct credit of subsidy to farmers' accounts.

secs.t: ZBNF to APCNF — origin and implementing agency RySS

x: RySS ran the Debt Redemption Scheme 2014, under which assistance was provided up to ₹1.5 lakh per family, and currently runs APCNF.
The Andhra Pradesh Community-Managed Natural Farming programme is implemented by
Rythu Sadhikara Samstha
(RySS).
“Zero budget” refers to avoiding purchased fertilisers and pesticides; it does not mean that every input or labour cost is absent.
ZBNF was developed in the mid-1990s by Maharashtrian agriculturist
Subhash Palekar
(Padma Shri).

secs.t: APCNF practices — terms → meaning

x: ZBNF is based on avoiding chemicals, not their exclusive use.
Jeevamrutham is prepared from cow dung, cow urine, jaggery, pulse flour and soil.
All four statements correctly describe mulching, PMDS and the 365-day green-cover approach.
APCNF promotes native seeds, minimal or no tillage, livestock integration and trap crops;
exclusive dependence on purchased chemical fertilisers
is contrary to the model.

secs.t: Natural farming data — APCNF coverage, NMNF and PKVY

x: Universal Gram Panchayat coverage is targeted for 2026-27, while 41 lakh farmers and 19 lakh hectares are targeted for 2028-29 under Swarna Andhra@2047.
The 2024-25 plan adopts 5-10 village clusters per Parliamentary Constituency, with 1,000 acres per constituency and 25,000 acres in total as stated in the programme design.
The stated APCNF coverage is 10.20 lakh farmers over 4.89 lakh hectares, with a target of 41 lakh farmers over 19 lakh hectares by 2028–29.

secs.t: APCNF awards, recognition and replication

x: The
M.S. Swaminathan Award for Environment Protection
(2022-23) went to RySS, the agency that implements APCNF.
APCNF was the first Indian finalist, and the June 2026 prize at Bastad, Sweden, carried an award of 1.5 million US dollars from the Curt Bergfors Foundation.
APCNF received the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity in 2024; the prize was shared and the recognition was associated with Lisbon on 11 July 2024.

secs.t: Data — horticulture size, growth, GVA and Rayalaseema hub

x: Andhra Pradesh recorded horticulture GVA of ₹1,52,950 crore, ranked third after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra, and registered 21% growth in 2024-25.
The 2025-26 figures were 46.43 lakh acres and 406.38 lakh MT.
Rayalaseema is the horticulture hub, with about 45% of the area (the figure the Survey prints; 19.50 lakh acres works out to about 43%) and 52% of output.

secs.t: Oil palm — area, production and NMEO-OP

x: In 2023–24, Andhra Pradesh led India in oil palm area and production, with 2.27 lakh ha, 1.74 lakh farmers and 17.63 lakh MT of fresh fruit bunches (FFB).
The earlier APPSC-asked figure for Andhra Pradesh oil palm production in 2017–18 was
17.81 lakh tonnes
Under NMEO-OP, the Viability Price is paid through
Direct Benefit Transfer
when prices crash.

secs.t: Horticulture, micro-irrigation and post-harvest schemes — MIDH

x: MIDH follows a 60:40 pattern in general States, 90:10 in North-Eastern and Himalayan States, and provides 100% central funding for NHB, CDB and CIH.
APIIATP is an externally aided programme with a
subsidy component.
MIDH is a centrally sponsored scheme launched in
, subsuming NHM and HMNEH.
APMIP has been implemented in Andhra Pradesh since
and is now linked with RKVY-PDMC.

secs.t: Horticulture, micro-irrigation and post-harvest schemes — Post-harvest infrastructure

x: The target is 1,030 post-harvest units, including ripening chambers, cold storages, pack houses and collection centres.
The six crops were mango, banana, tomato, pomegranate, sweet lime and papaya.
The plan aims to reduce logistics costs from about 14% to
8–9% of GSDP
Operation Greens is the TOP scheme: tomato, onion, potato, modelled on Operation Flood.

secs.t: Data — livestock products and Livestock Census — AP livestock product trend

x: Egg, meat and milk outputs all fell in 2023-24; milk recorded the largest decline, at 9.41%.
Milk production was supported by
crossbred cattle and graded Murrah buffaloes
India's per capita milk availability was 471 grams per day in 2023-24.
India is 2nd in world egg production with 142.77 billion eggs.

secs.t: Data — livestock products and Livestock Census — Livestock Census — AP species ranks

x: The 20th Livestock Census recorded
303.76 million
bovines in India.
Fieldwork for the 21st Livestock Census has been completed and its results are being compiled.
The total livestock population of Andhra Pradesh was
340.60 lakh
Sheep population increased by 29.99%
over 2012.
The descending order is poultry (1,078.63 lakh), sheep (176.27 lakh), buffalo (62.19 lakh) and cattle (46.00 lakh).

secs.t: Livestock credit, insurance and schemes — PKCC, AHIDF, dairy, NLM — Pashu Kisan Credit Card

x: The Pashu Kisan Credit Card provides up to ₹1.60 lakh without collateral at 7%.
PKCC is open to livestock owners, lessees and members of self-help groups.
Pasu Bhima Padhakam provides for settlement of claims within
15 days
AHIDF funds dairy and meat processing, feed plants, breed farms, waste-to-wealth projects and vaccine plants; irrigation canals are outside its stated scope.

secs.t: Livestock credit, insurance and schemes — PKCC, AHIDF, dairy, NLM — Dairy

x: Jeeva Kranthi
is associated with sheep and goat units, whereas Paala Velluva concerns dairy units for women.
The programme planned two clinics per constituency, inaugurated 175 Phase-I clinics on 19 May 2022, and provided 165 clinics in Phase II.
NLM covers breed development, feed and fodder, innovation, extension and insurance; urban metro rail is unrelated.

secs.t: Livestock credit, insurance and schemes — PKCC, AHIDF, dairy, NLM — Central schemes

x: NADCP has been merged into the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (
LHDCP
Pashu Aadhaar is a 12-digit identification number attached through an ear tag to livestock.
The
1962 app
replaced e-Gopala for livestock-related services.

secs.t: Data — fisheries output, coastline and seafood exports

x: Andhra Pradesh is India's largest shrimp producer, accounting for about 75% of India's cultured-shrimp exports (2025-26).
Fish output was
55.39 lakh tonnes
Andhra Pradesh accounted for
of India’s seafood export value by the end of 2018-19.
MPEDA is
the apex export body under the Ministry of Commerce
for marine products.
China
was the second-largest destination in 2025-26, with exports increasing by 20.1% by volume.

secs.t: Fisheries infrastructure and schemes — aqua power tariff, harbours, PMMSY, PM-MKSSY — Aqua power tariff

x: The tariff is ₹1.50 per unit for farms up to 10 acres inside notified aqua zones and ₹3.85 per unit for bigger farms or farms outside those zones.
The 10 fishing harbours are under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme component of PMMSY, not Sagarmala.
A chilling plant at Bhogapuram airport and an Aquatic Quarantine Facility
have been proposed.

secs.t: Fisheries infrastructure and schemes — aqua power tariff, harbours, PMMSY, PM-MKSSY — PMMSY

x: PM-MKSSY supports institutional credit, aquaculture insurance and supply-chain traceability.
The reported PMMSY results include 28 fishing harbours and 2,195 Fisheries Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs).
PMMSY was launched in 2020 with ₹20,050 crore (Blue Revolution). ₹7,522 crore is the FIDF corpus and ₹6,000 crore the outlay of PM-MKSSY (2023-24 to 2026-27); option D is unrelated.

secs.t: Fishermen welfare — ban-period relief, ex-gratia, credit

x: The marine fishing ban lasts
61 days
, covering the breeding season from 15 April to 14 June.
The relief was ₹4,000 before 2019-20, ₹10,000 from 2019-20 and
Families of deceased fishermen receive ex-gratia assistance of
₹10 lakh

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The plan included a control room, advisories through Rythu Seva Kendras, crop shifts to red gram, black gram and castor, and one Mobile Rythu Bazaar per district.
The identified concerns are the gap between CCRC issuance and actual financing, and the demand by APRS to restore free insurance.
The initiative won the Food Planet Prize in 2026 and had earlier become
the first Indian initiative to reach the Food Planet Prize final
The approach is described as chemical-free, climate-resilient, soil-carbon friendly and inexpensive to adopt.
Rayalaseema's shift to horticulture depends on
drip irrigation
, which is suited to its water-scarce conditions.
More than five lakh families depend on aquaculture, which is central to the Blue Economy, and high input and electricity costs are concerns.

rows.title: Agro-climatic zones of Andhra Pradesh and their cropping suitability
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I C-114

secs.t: Agro-climatic zones — types, districts and definitions

x: The Southern Zone includes Chittoor, YSR Kadapa and SPS Nellore; the Scarce Rainfall Zone includes Kurnool and Anantapur; and Agency areas form the High Altitude and Tribal Zone.
An agro-ecological zone is a land unit carved out of an agro-climatic zone by superimposing
landform
, which modifies climate and the length of the growing period.

secs.t: Zones → soils, crops and ANGRAU research stations

x: The
Godavari
zone, characterised by fertile deltaic alluvium, is described as a rice bowl and an aquaculture hub.
ANGRAU works on drought-resistant paddy, flood-tolerant pulses, pest-resistant cotton, drone-based precision farming and soil restoration in rain-shadow areas.
The North Coastal, Godavari, Krishna and Southern zones have their zonal headquarters at Anakapalle, Maruteru, Lam–Guntur and Tirupati respectively.

secs.t: Data — rainfall, drought-prone zones and contingency planning

x: Pre-monsoon dry sowing is referred to as
PMDS
and uses residual soil moisture, particularly in drought-prone areas.
Zone-based planning provides region-specific interventions, including advice on alternative crops when Kharif sowing is inadequate.
For the South-West Monsoon, the normal rainfall was 574.7 mm and the actual rainfall was 681.6 mm, representing a positive deviation of 18.6%.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Both statements are true, and uneven water distribution across the six agro-climatic zones contributes directly to disparities in irrigation and farm income.
Karnataka
has 10 agro-climatic zones, whereas the current Andhra Pradesh classification has six.
India has 15 agro-climatic zones.

rows.title: Rural credit cooperatives in Andhra Pradesh - structure, performance and problems
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I C-114

secs.t: Acts, amendment and committees on cooperatives

x: The Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Tribunal is constituted under
Section 75
of the Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Societies Act, 1964.
The MACS Act, 1995 provides for self-reliant societies without government share capital, run by members with minimal state control.
The 2004 Task Force on revival of cooperative credit was chaired by A.
Vaidyanathan
The 2013 Expert Committee on short-term cooperative credit structure was chaired by
Prakash Bakshi

secs.t: Cooperative credit structure → tiers and data

x: A total of 1,756 primary Labour Contract Cooperative Societies, along with their district and state federations, were under liquidation.
The number of cooperative societies in AP has
decreased
compared with 2001-02 (PYQ 2008); defunct labour contract and joint farming societies are being wound up.
APSES 2024–25 gives 18 APCOB branches, 13 DCCBs with 442 branches and 2,042 PACS.

secs.t: PACS → functions and computerisation

x: PACS undertake procurement, seed processing, PDS, insurance, RO drinking water, petrol bunks, rice mills and warehousing.
PACS in 207 blocks are eligible for NCDC equity grants as FPOs, with APCOB acting as the CBBO (2024-25).
Nationally, ERP software covers about 80,000 PACS, while model bye-laws allow PACS to undertake more than 25 non-credit activities.

secs.t: Ministry of Cooperation → schemes, initiatives and FIRSTs

x: The programme is a cooperative-based, PACS-level storage initiative supported through AIF, AMI and other schemes.
By July 2026, godowns had been completed in 313 PACS with storage capacity exceeding 1.80 lakh metric tonnes.
The plan covers two lakh societies, 24,417 have been set up, and PACS computerisation has an outlay of Rs 2,925.39 crore.

secs.t: Problems — overdues, political interference, low deposits, DCCB losses

x: Political capture distorts credit allocation and shields politically connected defaulters from recovery, thereby feeding overdues.
The identified problems include political interference, inactive societies, weak professional management, inadequate digital capacity, lack of spontaneity and state domination.
State audits in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh indicated that about
one-third
of PACS were inactive despite registration.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The announcements included a cooperative life insurance company, expansion of Bharat Taxi to 500 cities and foundation stones for 47 grain godowns.
White Revolution 2.0 targets
more milk procurement.
The ICDP-II godowns are associated with
Chittoor, East Godavari and Kurnool
Nehru identified cooperatives,
panchayats and schools
as three pillars of democracy.

rows.title: Institutional credit to agriculture in Andhra Pradesh - banks, NABARD and SHGs
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I C-114

secs.t: NABARD and Andhra Bank → establishment

x: NABARD was established on 12 July 1982 under the NABARD Act, 1981, on the recommendation of the B.
Sivaraman Committee
NABARD took over RBI's ACD and RPCC and the whole of the ARDC, so all three are correct; each option leaving one out is incomplete.
NABARD is headquartered in Mumbai with an initial corpus of Rs 100 crore.

secs.t: Sources of institutional finance → who lends what

x: The PACS-DCCB-SCB cooperative system mainly provides short-term credit, whereas ARDBs provide long-term credit.
Scheduled commercial banks provide
over 70%
of formal farm credit nationally.
Tenant, tribal, women and oral-lessee farmers may be excluded because formal lending generally requires land records.
Priority Sector Lending applies to commercial banks, RRBs, SFBs, LABs and primary UCBs.

secs.t: Credit plans → data (PLPs, State Focus Paper, SLBC)

x: District Potential Linked Credit Plans are aggregated into NABARD's State Focus Paper, which subsequently feeds the SLBC Annual Credit Plan.
The plan allocated ₹2.55 lakh crore to agriculture and allied activities and ₹1.64 lakh crore to MSMEs.
The Chief Minister noted inadequate MSME lending and the lagging performance of some banks, and asked banks to lend at scale for PM Surya Ghar.

secs.t: Schemes and funds → purpose — State-NABARD programmes → purpose

x: Indira Prabha
is the state programme supported by NABARD for land development.
RIDF began in 1995-96 with an initial corpus of
Rs 2,000 crore

x: Metro Railway, Kolkata
, was the 17th zone and dates from 29 December 2010, before SCoR became the 18th zone.
The criticisms included a decade of delay, the ceding of the K-K line and Waltair revenue to Odisha, and staff shortages.
The dedicated zone is expected to cut freight costs for the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor and improve port connectivity.

rows.title: Kadapa steel plant, Dugarajapatnam port, Ramayapatnam port and other Act commitments

secs.t: Thirteenth Schedule infrastructure commitments → location → status

x: The steel plant is associated with YSR Kadapa, the refinery and petrochemical complex with Kakinada, the railway zone with Visakhapatnam headquarters, and metro rail with the Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada–Guntur–Tenali region.
The proposed new major port at Duggirajupatnam, for which Phase I was envisaged by the end of 2018, was dropped as non-feasible.
The present development is described as a VPA–APMB greenfield port together with a shipbuilding cluster.

secs.t: Educational institutions → location and establishing Act

x: The educational commitments included one each of an IIT, NIT, IIM, IISER, Central University, Petroleum University, Agricultural University and IIIT, besides an AIIMS-type hospital, Tribal Universities and NIDM.
IIM Visakhapatnam began in September 2015 at Gambheeram, with
IIM Bangalore
serving as its mentor institution.
AIIMS Mangalagiri is associated with the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY), not the IIM Act, 2017.

secs.t: Kadapa steel plant — events by year and JSW plant features

x: Land was allotted during the YSR era of 2004–09, the foundation stone was laid in December 2018, stones were laid again in 2019 and 2023, and JSW construction was launched on 3 July 2026.
The Centre and SAIL did not build the plant; instead, the State formed its own special-purpose vehicle, AP High Grade Steels Limited, in 2018.

secs.t: Ports — Dugarajapatnam and Ramayapatnam → place, developer, status — Dugarajapatnam port

x: After Dugarajapatnam was dropped on feasibility grounds, the State developed Ramayapatnam as the substitute greenfield port.
The 2 January 2026 Government Order allowed the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board to establish the port and shipbuilding cluster under the Centre’s Shipbuilding Development Scheme.
The greenfield port and shipbuilding cluster at Dugarajapatnam is in
Tirupati district

secs.t: Ports — Dugarajapatnam and Ramayapatnam → place, developer, status — Ramayapatnam port

x: Ramayapatnam Port is being developed by the State SPV
Ramayapatnam Port Development Corporation Ltd
, permitted in February 2020.

Phase-I costs ₹4,929.39 crore with 4 berths and 34.04 MTPA. ₹1,638.52 crore is the Phase-II approval for three ports, 9 MTPA is the BPCL refinery capacity, 81% is the Aug 2026 progress, and ₹354.23 crore the variation works.

secs.t: Refinery and metro rail → place, agency, status

x: The Act required Indian Oil Corporation or Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited to examine, within six months, a
greenfield crude refinery and petrochemical complex
The BPCL complex is proposed near Ramayapatnam Port, between
Prakasam and Nellore
districts, in the villages of Chevuru and Ravuru.
The implementing agency for the metro rail projects in both cities is
Andhra Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Ltd

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The criticism referred to the
Kadapa steel plant, Dugarajapatnam port and metro projects
, with the unfulfilled promises valued at approximately ₹5 lakh crore.
Kadapa steel, Ramayapatnam Port and the BPCL refinery are linked by a new rail line
, forming a southern Andhra Pradesh industrial cluster.
Works at the JSW Kadapa plant were launched on 3 July 2026.

sub: Group-II M2-A-102: Industrial corridors in Andhra Pradesh - VCIC, CBIC nodes and industrial parks

secs.t: Act commitments — corridors, connectivity and corridor laws

x: The Thirteenth Schedule directed the Government of India to examine the
Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor
within six months.
The
Asian Development Bank
is the funding partner of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor.
The Act provides for rapid rail and road connectivity from the new Andhra Pradesh capital to
Hyderabad and other important cities of Telangana

secs.t: VCIC — definition, parent corridor and FIRSTs

x: Exam angle: "VCIC is funded by?" - ADB; "part of?" - ECEC; "modelled on?" - DMIC.
The corridor is about 800 km long, forms the first phase of the East Coast Economic Corridor, and is linked with Act East and Make in India.
The East Coast Economic Corridor is described as extending from
Kolkata to Tuticorin
; some descriptions refer to its southern end as Kanyakumari.

secs.t: VCIC funding — ADB data, tranches and externally aided projects

x: The USD 125 million policy-based loan, entirely from the ADB, funds
ease of doing business and institutional reform

The Integrated Irrigation and Agriculture Transformation Project is funded by the World Bank; VCIC combines ADB and Government of Andhra Pradesh funding; APFAMGS is FAO-executed and Netherlands-funded; and Amaravati capital loans involve the World Bank and ADB.

secs.t: VCIC nodes, parks and SEZs → location

x: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor is about 800 km long, covers over 33,000 acres across its three principal nodes, develops 30 percent initially as start-up area and involves ₹5,000 crore of works.

Kopparthy's trunk infrastructure costs about ₹1,264 crore (funded via NICDIT) and the node targets about ₹8,860 crore of investment. ₹3,000 crore is NICDIT's BE 2026-27, ₹33,660 crore the BHAVYA outlay, and ₹202 crore the PM Gati Shakti-SASCI grant for water and rail siding.

secs.t: Institutions and schemes → role (NICDC, NICDIT, AP-ICDA, APIIC, BHAVYA)

x: The VCIC financing totals $840 million, comprising $625 million from ADB and $215 million from the Government of Andhra Pradesh, with respective shares of 74.4% and 25.6%.

All three statements correctly describe the institutional arrangement: the Department of Industries and Commerce is the executing agency, the PMU is under the Commissioner of Industries, and there are four PIUs including APIIC, APRDC and AP Transco.

secs.t: Expressways, rail corridors and logistics → route

x: The expressway is a greenfield project under Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I and starts at Hoskote in Karnataka.
The expressway crosses Chittoor via the
Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary
elephant corridor; the SC-NBWL cleared 3,475 m of underpasses (1,400 m continuous).
The stated focus includes the Visakhapatnam–Kakinada port corridor and port-led growth, while PM Gati Shakti-related planning includes multimodal logistics parks and freight corridors.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: APIIC can directly allot land up to
50 acres
The
SCoR zone, greenfield ports and Bhogapuram airport
are identified as feeding the VCIC logistics chain.
DMIC is associated with the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor and Japanese aid, whereas VCIC is ADB-funded and port-led.

rows.title: Special Category Status - criteria, the 14th Finance Commission position and the controversy

secs.t: SCS — definition, origin and FIRSTs

x: Exam angle: "SCS was first introduced in 1969 on the recommendation of which FC?" - 5th.
Special Category Status is not a constitutional category; it emerged as an executive and Planning Commission-era classification linked to preferential Plan assistance.
The Gadgil Formula was later modified and became the
Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula

secs.t: SCS criteria and benefits — features

x: High population density and advanced infrastructure
were not criteria for Special Category Status.
SCS was meant to give such States a larger tax share to cover the gap arising from geographic disadvantage and economic and infrastructural backwardness.
SCS States got Central loans at concessional interest, while general States got normal terms.

secs.t: SCS states → status

x: The first three SCS States were
Jammu & Kashmir, Assam and Nagaland
Telangana
has never been granted Special Category Status.
Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory in 2019.

secs.t: Finance Commissions → position on SCS and devolution

x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended 42 per cent, while the Fifteenth and Sixteenth Finance Commissions retained 41 per cent; the Sixteenth also added a 10 per cent Contribution to GDP criterion.
The 16th FC is chaired by Arvind Panagariya, and its award runs from 1 Apr 2026 to 31 Mar 2031; it keeps the share at 41%.

secs.t: AP and SCS — 2014 assurance and controversy timeline

x: The correct sequence is 2014 assurance, 2015 Fourteenth Finance Commission award, September 2016 Special Assistance Package, and 2018 withdrawal of TDP from the NDA.
In 2018, the
TDP broke from the NDA and moved a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha
in July; the motion was defeated.
The demand was revived in 2026 through interventions by Congress MP Manickam Tagore in the Lok Sabha, YSRCP leader Botcha Satyanarayana and APCC chief Y.S. Sharmila.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 16th Finance Commission retains a 41 per cent share for the States, ends revenue deficit grants, and covers 2026–2031.
Both the Assertion and the Reason are true.
Special Category Status is associated with an automatic 90:10 funding pattern, while a special package consists of project-linked financial assistance.

rows.title: Special Assistance Package vs Special Category Status - Government's stand and measures taken

secs.t: Special Assistance Package — definition and Act provisions

x: FM Arun Jaitley announced it in September 2016 in place of SCS.
All four statements correctly describe the special-assistance and Polavaram provisions and the Section 94(1) industrial incentives.
The promised ten-year tax holiday was delayed, diluted or subsumed in the GST framework; it was not implemented fully and without dilution.
The package covered five years, from
, corresponding to the promised SCS period.

secs.t: Externally Aided Projects and SASCI — how the schemes work

x: The fuller package design described support equivalent to the 90% central grant share under SCS, routed through repayment of externally aided project loans.
SASCI (Ministry of Finance, since Oct 2020) gives 50-year interest-free loans for capital works only, over and above the net borrowing ceiling and outside the 3% of GSDP deficit ceiling.

secs.t: Persons and governments → stand

x: The relevant sequence is the 2014-18 alliance period, the September 2016 package announcement, the 2018 NDA exit and the 2019 campaign emphasis on SCS.
The loss of up to ₹38,000 crore came from the 16th FC dropping revenue deficit grants, with the revenue deficit rising from ₹16,000 crore (2014-19) to a projected ₹48,000 crore (2025-26).

secs.t: Data — assistance released and measures (2014-2026)

x: was released as special assistance for 2016-17 (APPSC-G1 2017 key). ₹3,979 crore was the 2014-15 revenue deficit grant, ₹24,350 crore the total SAM package, and ₹2,500 crore the amount promised for the capital.

The Centre extended support for the Visakhapatnam Economic Region; its in-principle nod went to the Rayalaseema Global Horticulture Hub (Centre ₹10,000 crore + State ₹30,000 crore), not a ₹4,000 crore UIDF allocation.

secs.t: SCS vs Special Assistance Package — benefit by benefit

x: SCS included
tax concessions for industry
, whereas the package offered only the weaker Section 94(1) incentives.
SCS had recognised and automatic features, while the package was executive in nature and tied to approved externally aided projects.
Andhra Pradesh argued that the apparent monetary equivalence did not compensate for the absence of automatic flows and tax benefits and the reliance on project-linked loans.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The package has been criticised as a loans-and-projects arrangement instead of a status-based framework.
SASCI and project grants have become the main forms of special help, including the specified grants for Amaravati and Polavaram.
The debate between Special Category Status and the package became an important part of
the 2019 election narrative
in Andhra Pradesh.
